field.documentation: Type of every element: 1: line segment, its ends are given by the start and end points; index = 2: arc of a circle; index = 3: full circle

field.name: start_points
field.documentation: Position of the start point of every element

field.name: phi
field.documentation: Toroidal angle (oriented counter-clockwise when viewing from above)

field.name: intermediate_points
field.documentation: Position of an intermediate point along the circle or arc of circle, for every element, providing the orientation of the element (must define with the corresponding start point an aperture angle strictly inferior to PI). In the case of a line segment (../types/index=1), fill this node with a point such that the vector intermediate_point - start_point defines the direction of the element's normal axis (see documentation of ../elements)

field.name: phi
field.documentation: Toroidal angle (oriented counter-clockwise when viewing from above)

field.name: end_points
field.documentation: Position of the end point of every element. Meaningful only if type/index = 1 or 2, fill with default/empty value otherwise

field.name: phi
field.documentation: Toroidal angle (oriented counter-clockwise when viewing from above)

field.name: centres
field.documentation: Position of the centre of the arc of a circle of every element (meaningful only if type/index = 2 or 3, fill with default/empty value otherwise)

field.name: phi
field.documentation: Toroidal angle (oriented counter-clockwise when viewing from above)

field.name: elements
field.documentation: Set of geometrical elements (line segments and/or arcs of a circle) describing the contour of the conductor centre. We define a coordinate system associated to each element as follows: for the arc and circle elements: binormal = (start point - center) x (intermediate point - center). This vector points in the direction of the circle / arc axis. normal = (center - point on curve). The normal vector will rotate as the point moves around the curve. Tangent = normal x binormal. For the line element we require an extra point, using the currently redundant intermediate point to define the line element's normal axis. The local coordinates for the line element then become: tangent = end point - start point; normal = intermediate point - start point; binormal = tangent x normal. It is assumed that all the axes above are normalized such that they have a unit length.

field.name: psi
field.documentation: Poloidal magnetic flux. Integral of magnetic field passing through a contour defined by the intersection of a flux surface passing through the point of interest and a Z=constant plane. If the integration surface is flat, the surface normal vector is in the increasing vertical coordinate direction, Z, namely upwards.

field.name: rho_tor_norm
field.documentation: Normalised toroidal flux coordinate. The normalizing value for rho_tor_norm, is the toroidal flux coordinate at the equilibrium boundary (LCFS or 99.x % of the LCFS in case of a fixed boundary equilibium calculation, see time_slice/boundary/b_flux_pol_norm in the equilibrium IDS)

field.name: rho_tor
field.documentation: Toroidal flux coordinate. rho_tor = sqrt(b_flux_tor/(pi*b0)) ~ sqrt(pi*r^2*b0/(pi*b0)) ~ r [m]. The toroidal field used in its definition is indicated under vacuum_toroidal_field/b0

field.name: volume
field.documentation: Volume enclosed inside the magnetic surface

field.name: area
field.documentation: Cross-sectional area of the flux surface

field.name: surface
field.documentation: Surface area of the toroidal flux surface

field.name: psi_magnetic_axis
field.documentation: Value of the poloidal magnetic flux at the magnetic axis (useful to normalize the psi array values when the radial grid doesn't go from the magnetic axis to the plasma boundary)

field.name: psi_boundary
field.documentation: Value of the poloidal magnetic flux at the plasma boundary (useful to normalize the psi array values when the radial grid doesn't go from the magnetic axis to the plasma boundary)

field.name: rho_tor_norm
field.documentation: Normalized toroidal flux coordinate. The normalizing value for rho_tor_norm, is the toroidal flux coordinate at the equilibrium boundary (LCFS or 99.x % of the LCFS in case of a fixed boundary equilibium calculation, see time_slice/boundary/b_flux_pol_norm in the equilibrium IDS)

field.name: rho_tor
field.documentation: Toroidal flux coordinate = sqrt(phi/(pi*b0)), where the toroidal magnetic field, b0, corresponds to that stored in vacuum_toroidal_field/b0 and pi can be found in the IMAS constants

field.name: psi
field.documentation: Poloidal magnetic flux. Integral of magnetic field passing through a contour defined by the intersection of a flux surface passing through the point of interest and a Z=constant plane. If the integration surface is flat, the surface normal vector is in the increasing vertical coordinate direction, Z, namely upwards.

field.name: volume
field.documentation: Volume enclosed inside the magnetic surface

field.name: area
field.documentation: Cross-sectional area of the flux surface

field.name: surface
field.documentation: Surface area of the toroidal flux surface

field.name: psi_magnetic_axis
field.documentation: Value of the poloidal magnetic flux at the magnetic axis (useful to normalize the psi array values when the radial grid doesn't go from the magnetic axis to the plasma boundary)

field.name: psi_boundary
field.documentation: Value of the poloidal magnetic flux at the plasma boundary (useful to normalize the psi array values when the radial grid doesn't go from the magnetic axis to the plasma boundary)

field.name: measured
field.documentation: Measured values. Units are: as_parent for a local measurement, as_parent.m for a line integrated measurement.

field.name: source
field.documentation: Path to the source data for each measurement in the IMAS data dictionary, e.g. ece/channel(i)/t_e for the electron temperature on the i-th channel in the ECE IDS

field.name: time_measurement
field.documentation: Exact time slices used from the time array of the measurement source data. The time slice is indicated for each measurement point considered in the fit since measurements may come from different and thus asynchronous diagnostics. If the time slice does not exist in the time array of the source data, it means linear interpolation has been used

field.name: time_measurement_slice_method
field.documentation: Method used to slice the data : index = 0 means using exact time slice of the measurement, 1 means linear interpolation, ...

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: time_measurement_width
field.documentation: In case the measurements are averaged over a time interval, this node is the full width of this time interval (empty otherwise). In case the slicing/averaging method doesn't use a hard time interval cutoff, this width is the characteristic time span of the slicing/averaging method. By convention, the time interval starts at time_measurement-time_width and ends at time_measurement.

field.name: local
field.documentation: Integer flag : 1 means local measurement, 0 means line-integrated measurement

field.name: rho_tor_norm
field.documentation: Normalized toroidal flux coordinate of each measurement (local value for a local measurement, minimum value reached by the line of sight for a line measurement)

field.name: weight
field.documentation: Weight given to each measured value

field.name: reconstructed
field.documentation: Value reconstructed from the fit. Units are: as_parent for a local measurement, as_parent.m for a line integrated measurement.

field.name: chi_squared
field.documentation: Squared error normalized by the weighted standard deviation considered in the minimization process : chi_squared = weight^2 *(reconstructed - measured)^2 / sigma^2, where sigma is the standard deviation of the measurement error

field.name: parameters
field.documentation: List of the fit specific parameters in XML format

field.name: core_profiles_ions_charge_states2
field.documentation: Quantities related to the a given state of the ion species

field.name: z_min
field.documentation: Minimum Z of the charge state bundle

field.name: z_max
field.documentation: Maximum Z of the charge state bundle (equal to z_min if no bundle)

field.name: z_average
field.documentation: Average Z of the charge state bundle, volume averaged over the plasma radius (equal to z_min if no bundle), = sum (Z*x_z) where x_z is the relative concentration of a given charge state in the bundle, i.e. sum(x_z) = 1 over the bundle.

field.name: z_square_average
field.documentation: Average Z square of the charge state bundle, volume averaged over the plasma radius (equal to z_min squared if no bundle), = sum (Z^2*x_z) where x_z is the relative concentration of a given charge state in the bundle, i.e. sum(x_z) = 1 over the bundle.

field.name: z_average_1d
field.documentation: Average charge profile of the charge state bundle (equal to z_min if no bundle), = sum (Z*x_z) where x_z is the relative concentration of a given charge state in the bundle, i.e. sum(x_z) = 1 over the bundle.

field.name: z_average_square_1d
field.documentation: Average square charge profile of the charge state bundle (equal to z_min squared if no bundle), = sum (Z^2*x_z) where x_z is the relative concentration of a given charge state in the bundle, i.e. sum(x_z) = 1 over the bundle.

field.name: ionization_potential
field.documentation: Cumulative and average ionization potential to reach a given bundle. Defined as sum (x_z* (sum of Epot from z'=0 to z-1)), where Epot is the ionization potential of ion Xz’+, and x_z is the relative concentration of a given charge state in the bundle, i.e. sum(x_z) = 1 over the bundle.

field.name: name
field.documentation: String identifying state (e.g. C+, C+2 , C+3, C+4, C+5, C+6, ...)

field.name: electron_configuration
field.documentation: Configuration of atomic orbitals of this state, e.g. 1s2-2s1

field.name: vibrational_mode
field.documentation: Vibrational mode of this state, e.g. "A_g". Need to define, or adopt a standard nomenclature.

field.name: rotation_frequency_tor
field.documentation: Toroidal rotation frequency (i.e. toroidal velocity divided by the major radius at which the toroidal velocity is taken)

field.name: velocity
field.documentation: Velocity at the position of maximum major radius on every flux surface

field.documentation: Information on the fit used to obtain the density profile

field.documentation: Squared error normalized by the weighted standard deviation considered in the minimization process : chi_squared = weight^2 *(reconstructed - measured)^2 / sigma^2, where sigma is the standard deviation of the measurement error

field.name: parameters
field.documentation: List of the fit specific parameters in XML format

field.name: collisionality_norm
field.documentation: Collisionality normalized to the bounce frequency

field.name: core_profiles_profiles_1d
field.documentation: 1D radial profiles for core and edge

field.name: rho_tor_norm
field.documentation: Normalized toroidal flux coordinate. The normalizing value for rho_tor_norm, is the toroidal flux coordinate at the equilibrium boundary (LCFS or 99.x % of the LCFS in case of a fixed boundary equilibium calculation, see time_slice/boundary/b_flux_pol_norm in the equilibrium IDS)

field.name: rho_tor
field.documentation: Toroidal flux coordinate = sqrt(phi/(pi*b0)), where the toroidal magnetic field, b0, corresponds to that stored in vacuum_toroidal_field/b0 and pi can be found in the IMAS constants

field.name: psi
field.documentation: Poloidal magnetic flux. Integral of magnetic field passing through a contour defined by the intersection of a flux surface passing through the point of interest and a Z=constant plane. If the integration surface is flat, the surface normal vector is in the increasing vertical coordinate direction, Z, namely upwards.

field.name: volume
field.documentation: Volume enclosed inside the magnetic surface

field.name: area
field.documentation: Cross-sectional area of the flux surface

field.name: surface
field.documentation: Surface area of the toroidal flux surface

field.name: psi_magnetic_axis
field.documentation: Value of the poloidal magnetic flux at the magnetic axis (useful to normalize the psi array values when the radial grid doesn't go from the magnetic axis to the plasma boundary)

field.name: psi_boundary
field.documentation: Value of the poloidal magnetic flux at the plasma boundary (useful to normalize the psi array values when the radial grid doesn't go from the magnetic axis to the plasma boundary)

field.name: temperature_validity
field.documentation: Indicator of the validity of the temperature profile. 0: valid from automated processing, 1: valid and certified by the RO; - 1 means problem identified in the data processing (request verification by the RO), -2: invalid data, should not be used

field.name: temperature_fit
field.documentation: Information on the fit used to obtain the temperature profile

field.name: measured
field.documentation: Measured values. Units are: as_parent for a local measurement, as_parent.m for a line integrated measurement.

field.name: source
field.documentation: Path to the source data for each measurement in the IMAS data dictionary, e.g. ece/channel(i)/t_e for the electron temperature on the i-th channel in the ECE IDS

field.name: time_measurement
field.documentation: Exact time slices used from the time array of the measurement source data. The time slice is indicated for each measurement point considered in the fit since measurements may come from different and thus asynchronous diagnostics. If the time slice does not exist in the time array of the source data, it means linear interpolation has been used

field.name: time_measurement_slice_method
field.documentation: Method used to slice the data : index = 0 means using exact time slice of the measurement, 1 means linear interpolation, ...

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: time_measurement_width
field.documentation: In case the measurements are averaged over a time interval, this node is the full width of this time interval (empty otherwise). In case the slicing/averaging method doesn't use a hard time interval cutoff, this width is the characteristic time span of the slicing/averaging method. By convention, the time interval starts at time_measurement-time_width and ends at time_measurement.

field.documentation: Pressure (thermal+non-thermal) (sum over charge states when multiple charge states are considered)

field.name: pressure_thermal
field.documentation: Pressure (thermal) associated with random motion ~average((v-average(v))^2) (sum over charge states when multiple charge states are considered)

field.name: pressure_fast_perpendicular
field.documentation: Fast (non-thermal) perpendicular pressure (sum over charge states when multiple charge states are considered)

field.name: pressure_fast_parallel
field.documentation: Fast (non-thermal) parallel pressure (sum over charge states when multiple charge states are considered)

field.name: rotation_frequency_tor
field.documentation: Toroidal rotation frequency (i.e. toroidal velocity divided by the major radius at which the toroidal velocity is taken) (average over charge states when multiple charge states are considered)

field.name: velocity
field.documentation: Velocity (average over charge states when multiple charge states are considered) at the position of maximum major radius on every flux surface

field.name: multiple_states_flag
field.documentation: Multiple states calculation flag : 0-Only the 'ion' level is considered and the 'state' array of structure is empty; 1-Ion states are considered and are described in the 'state' array of structure

field.name: state
field.documentation: Quantities related to the different states of the species (ionization, energy, excitation, ...)

field.name: z_min
field.documentation: Minimum Z of the charge state bundle

field.name: z_max
field.documentation: Maximum Z of the charge state bundle (equal to z_min if no bundle)

field.name: z_average
field.documentation: Average Z of the charge state bundle, volume averaged over the plasma radius (equal to z_min if no bundle), = sum (Z*x_z) where x_z is the relative concentration of a given charge state in the bundle, i.e. sum(x_z) = 1 over the bundle.

field.name: z_square_average
field.documentation: Average Z square of the charge state bundle, volume averaged over the plasma radius (equal to z_min squared if no bundle), = sum (Z^2*x_z) where x_z is the relative concentration of a given charge state in the bundle, i.e. sum(x_z) = 1 over the bundle.

field.name: z_average_1d
field.documentation: Average charge profile of the charge state bundle (equal to z_min if no bundle), = sum (Z*x_z) where x_z is the relative concentration of a given charge state in the bundle, i.e. sum(x_z) = 1 over the bundle.

field.name: z_average_square_1d
field.documentation: Average square charge profile of the charge state bundle (equal to z_min squared if no bundle), = sum (Z^2*x_z) where x_z is the relative concentration of a given charge state in the bundle, i.e. sum(x_z) = 1 over the bundle.

field.name: ionization_potential
field.documentation: Cumulative and average ionization potential to reach a given bundle. Defined as sum (x_z* (sum of Epot from z'=0 to z-1)), where Epot is the ionization potential of ion Xz’+, and x_z is the relative concentration of a given charge state in the bundle, i.e. sum(x_z) = 1 over the bundle.

field.name: electron_configuration

field.name: vibrational_mode

field.name: parameters
field.documentation: List of the fit specific parameters in XML format

field.name: pressure_ion_total
field.documentation: Total (sum over ion species) thermal ion pressure

field.name: j_total
field.documentation: Total parallel current density = average(jtot.B) / B0, where B0 = Core_Profiles/Vacuum_Toroidal_Field/ B0

field.name: current_parallel_inside
field.documentation: Parallel current driven inside the flux surface. Cumulative surface integral of j_total

field.name: j_phi
field.documentation: Total toroidal current density = average(J_phi/R) / average(1/R)

field.name: j_ohmic
field.documentation: Ohmic parallel current density = average(J_Ohmic.B) / B0, where B0 = Core_Profiles/Vacuum_Toroidal_Field/ B0

field.name: j_non_inductive
field.documentation: Non-inductive (includes bootstrap) parallel current density = average(jni.B) / B0, where B0 = Core_Profiles/Vacuum_Toroidal_Field/ B0

field.name: j_bootstrap
field.documentation: Bootstrap current density = average(J_Bootstrap.B) / B0, where B0 = Core_Profiles/Vacuum_Toroidal_Field/ B0

field.name: e_field
field.documentation: Electric field, averaged on the magnetic surface. E.g for the parallel component, average(E.B) / B0, using core_profiles/vacuum_toroidal_field/b0

field.name: phi_potential
field.documentation: Electrostatic potential, averaged on the magnetic flux surface

field.name: rotation_frequency_tor_sonic
field.documentation: Derivative of the flux surface averaged electrostatic potential with respect to the poloidal flux, multiplied by (1/2pi). This quantity is the toroidal angular rotation frequency due to the ExB drift, introduced in formula (43) of Hinton and Wong, Physics of Fluids 3082 (1985), also referred to as sonic flow in regimes in which the toroidal velocity is dominant over the poloidal velocity

field.name: q
field.documentation: Safety factor (only positive when toroidal current and magnetic field are in same direction)

field.name: magnetic_shear
field.documentation: Magnetic shear, defined as rho_tor/q . dq/drho_tor

field.name: rows_uri
field.documentation: List of URIs corresponding to the rows (1st dimension) of the covariance matrix. If not all indices of a given node are used, they must be listed explicitly e.g. rows_uri(i) = pf_active:1/coil(i) will refer to a list of indices of the occurrence 1 of the pf_active IDS of this data entry. If the rows correspond to all indices of a given vector it is sufficient to give a single URI where this vector is denoted using the (:) implicit notation, e.g. rows_uri(1) = /grid_ggd(3)/grid_subset(2)/elements(:).

field.name: lower_bound
field.documentation: Lower bound of the energy band

field.name: upper_bound
field.documentation: Upper bound of the energy band

field.name: energies
field.documentation: Array of discrete energy values inside the band

field.name: detection_efficiency

field.name: n_phi
field.documentation: Array of toroidal mode numbers, where quantities vary as exp(i.n_phi.phi) and phi runs anticlockwise when viewed from above

field.documentation: Test particles for a given time slice

field.name: coordinate_identifier
field.documentation: Set of coordinate identifiers, coordinates on which the markers are represented

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: weights
field.documentation: Weight of the markers, i.e. number of real particles represented by each marker. The dimension of the vector correspond to the number of markers

field.name: positions
field.documentation: Position of the markers in the set of coordinates. The first dimension corresponds to the number of markers, the second dimension to the set of coordinates

field.name: orbit_integrals
field.documentation: Integrals along the markers orbit. These dimensionless expressions are of the form: (1/tau) integral (f(n_tor,m_pol,k,eq,...) dt) from time - tau to time, where tau is the transit/trapping time of the marker and f() a dimensionless function (phase factor,drift,etc) of the equilibrium (e.g. q) and perturbation (Fourier harmonics n_tor,m_pol and bounce harmonic k) along the particles orbits. In fact the integrals are taken during the last orbit of each marker at the time value of the time node below

field.name: expressions
field.documentation: List of the expressions f(n_tor,m_pol,k,q,...) used in the orbit integrals

field.name: n_phi
field.documentation: Array of toroidal mode numbers, where quantities vary as exp(i.n_phi.phi) and phi runs anticlockwise when viewed from above

field.name: m_pol
field.documentation: Array of poloidal mode numbers, where quantities vary as exp(-i.m_pol.theta) and theta is the angle defined by the choice of ../../coordinate_identifier, with its centre at the magnetic axis recalled at the root of this IDS

field.name: orbit_integrals_instant
field.documentation: Integrals/quantities along the markers orbit. These dimensionless expressions are of the form: (1/tau) integral ( f(eq) dt) from time - tau to time_orbit for different values of time_orbit in the interval from time - tau to time, where tau is the transit/trapping time of the marker and f(eq) a dimensionless function (phase, drift,q,etc) of the equilibrium along the markers orbits. The integrals are taken during the last orbit of each marker at the time value of the time node below

field.documentation: Geometry of the filter contour. Note that there is some flexibility in the choice of the local coordinate system (X1,X2,X3). The data provider should choose the most convenient coordinate system for the filter, respecting the definitions of (X1,X2,X3) indicated below.

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: centre
field.documentation: Coordinates of the origin of the local coordinate system (X1,X2,X3) describing the filter. This origin is located within the filter area and should be the middle point of the filter surface. If geometry_type=2, it's the centre of the circular filter. If geometry_type=3, it's the centre of the rectangular filter.

field.name: phi
field.documentation: Toroidal angle (oriented counter-clockwise when viewing from above)

field.name: radius
field.documentation: Radius of the circle, used only if geometry_type/index = 2

field.name: x1_unit_vector
field.documentation: Components of the X1 direction unit vector in the (X,Y,Z) coordinate system, where X is the major radius axis for phi = 0, Y is the major radius axis for phi = pi/2, and Z is the height axis. The X1 vector is more horizontal than X2 (has a smaller abs(Z) component) and oriented in the positive phi direction (counter-clockwise when viewing from above).

field.name: x2_unit_vector
field.documentation: Components of the X2 direction unit vector in the (X,Y,Z) coordinate system, where X is the major radius axis for phi = 0, Y is the major radius axis for phi = pi/2, and Z is the height axis. The X2 axis is orthonormal so that uX2 = uX3 x uX1.

field.name: x3_unit_vector
field.documentation: Components of the X3 direction unit vector in the (X,Y,Z) coordinate system, where X is the major radius axis for phi = 0, Y is the major radius axis for phi = pi/2, and Z is the height axis. The X3 axis is normal to the filter surface and oriented towards the plasma.

field.name: x2_width

field.name: x2_curvature
field.documentation: Radius of curvature in the X2 direction, to be filled only for curvature_type/index = 3 or 5

field.name: surface

In case of 'outline', the surface is described by an outline of point in a local coordinate system defined by a centre and three unit vectors X1, X2, X3. Note that there is some flexibility here and the data provider should choose the most convenient coordinate system for the object, respecting the definitions of (X1,X2,X3) indicated below. In case of 'circular', the surface is a circle defined by its centre, radius, and normal vector oriented towards the plasma X3. In case of 'rectangle', the surface is a rectangle defined by its centre, widths in the X1 and X2 directions, and normal vector oriented towards the plasma X3.

field.name: x2_curvature
field.documentation: Radius of curvature in the X2 direction, to be filled only for curvature_type/index = 3 or 5

field.name: thickness
field.documentation: Distance between front_surface and back_surface along the X3 vector

field.name: material_properties
field.documentation: Material properties of the optical element

field.name: type
field.documentation: Type of optical element material. In case of 'metal' refractive_index and extinction_coefficient are used. In case of 'dielectric' refractive_index and transmission_coefficient are used.

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: wavelengths
field.documentation: Wavelengths array for refractive_index, extinction_coefficient and transmission_coefficient

field.name: roughness
field.documentation: Roughness parameter of the material. Varies in range [0, 1]. 0 is perfectly specular, 1 is perfectly rough

field.name: geometry
field.documentation: Further geometrical description of the element

field.name: geometry_type
field.documentation: Type of geometry used to describe the surface of the detector or aperture (1:'outline', 2:'circular', 3:'rectangle'). In case of 'outline', the surface is described by an outline of point in a local coordinate system defined by a centre and three unit vectors X1, X2, X3. Note that there is some flexibility here and the data provider should choose the most convenient coordinate system for the object, respecting the definitions of (X1,X2,X3) indicated below. In case of 'circular', the surface is a circle defined by its centre, radius, and normal vector oriented towards the plasma X3. In case of 'rectangle', the surface is a rectangle defined by its centre, widths in the X1 and X2 directions, and normal vector oriented towards the plasma X3.

field.name: centre
field.documentation: If geometry_type=2, coordinates of the centre of the circle. If geometry_type=1 or 3, coordinates of the origin of the local coordinate system (X1,X2,X3) describing the plane detector/aperture. This origin is located within the detector/aperture area.

field.name: phi
field.documentation: Toroidal angle (oriented counter-clockwise when viewing from above)

field.name: radius
field.documentation: Radius of the circle, used only if geometry_type = 2

field.name: x1_unit_vector
field.documentation: Components of the X1 direction unit vector in the (X,Y,Z) coordinate system, where X is the major radius axis for phi = 0, Y is the major radius axis for phi = pi/2, and Z is the height axis. The X1 vector is more horizontal than X2 (has a smaller abs(Z) component) and oriented in the positive phi direction (counter-clockwise when viewing from above).

field.name: x2_unit_vector
field.documentation: Components of the X2 direction unit vector in the (X,Y,Z) coordinate system, where X is the major radius axis for phi = 0, Y is the major radius axis for phi = pi/2, and Z is the height axis. The X2 axis is orthonormal so that uX2 = uX3 x uX1.

field.name: x3_unit_vector
field.documentation: Components of the X3 direction unit vector in the (X,Y,Z) coordinate system, where X is the major radius axis for phi = 0, Y is the major radius axis for phi = pi/2, and Z is the height axis. The X3 axis is normal to the detector/aperture plane and oriented towards the plasma.

field.name: x1_width
field.documentation: Full width of the aperture in the X1 direction, used only if geometry_type = 3

field.name: x2_width
field.documentation: Full width of the aperture in the X2 direction, used only if geometry_type = 3

field.name: outline
field.documentation: Irregular outline of the detector/aperture in the (X1, X2) coordinate system. Repeat the first point since this is a closed contour

field.name: surface
field.documentation: Surface of the detector/aperture, derived from the above geometric data

field.name: entry_tag
field.documentation: Tag qualifying an entry or a list of entries

field.name: comment
field.documentation: Any comment describing the content of the tagged list of entries

field.name: z

field.name: length_beta

field.name: beta
field.documentation: Inclination of second angle measured counter-clockwise from vertically upwards directed vector (grad Z). If both alpha and beta are zero (rectangle) then the simpler rectangular elements description should be used.

field.name: reference
field.documentation: List of references used to populate or calculate this node, identified as explained below. In case the node is the result of of a calculation / data processing, the reference is an input to the process described in the "code" structure at the root of the IDS. The reference can be an IDS (identified by a URI or a persitent identifier, see syntax in the link below) or non-IDS data imported directly from an non-IMAS database (identified by the command used to import the reference, or the persistent identifier of the data reference). Often data are obtained by a chain of processes, however only the last process input are recorded here. The full chain of provenance has then to be reconstructed recursively from the provenance information contained in the data references.

field.name: timestamp
field.documentation: Date and time (UTC) at which the reference was created, expressed in a human readable form (ISO 8601) : the format of the string shall be : YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ. Example : 2020-07-24T14:19:00Z

field.name: node
field.documentation: Set of IDS nodes for which the provenance is given. The provenance information applies to the whole structure below the IDS node. For documenting provenance information for the whole IDS, set the size of this array of structure to 1 and leave the child "path" node empty

field.documentation: Generic declaration of Plasma Composition for a simulation

field.name: element
field.documentation: List of elements forming the atom or molecule

field.name: atoms_n
field.documentation: Number of atoms of this element in the molecule

field.name: z_ion
field.documentation: Ion charge (of the dominant ionization state; lumped ions are allowed)

field.name: name
field.documentation: String identifying ion (e.g. H+, D+, T+, He+2, C+, ...)

field.name: multiple_states_flag
field.documentation: Multiple states calculation flag : 0-Only one state is considered; 1-Multiple states are considered and are described in the state structure

field.name: state
field.documentation: Quantities related to the different states of the species (ionization, energy, excitation, ...)

field.name: z_min
field.documentation: Minimum Z of the charge state bundle (z_min = z_max = 0 for a neutral)

field.name: z_max
field.documentation: Maximum Z of the charge state bundle (equal to z_min if no bundle)

field.name: name
field.documentation: String identifying ion state (e.g. C+, C+2 , C+3, C+4, C+5, C+6, ...)

field.name: electron_configuration
field.documentation: Configuration of atomic orbitals of this state, e.g. 1s2-2s1

field.name: vibrational_mode
field.documentation: Vibrational mode of this state, e.g. "A_g". Need to define, or adopt a standard nomenclature.

field.documentation: Generic decription of the code-specific parameters for the code that has produced this IDS

field.name: description
field.documentation: Short description of the software (type, purpose)

field.name: parameters
field.documentation: List of the code specific parameters in XML format

field.name: output_flag
field.documentation: Output flag : 0 means the run is successful, other values mean some difficulty has been encountered, the exact meaning is then code specific. Negative values mean the result shall not be used.

field.name: library
field.documentation: List of external libraries used by the code that has produced this IDS

field.documentation: Short description of the software (type, purpose)

field.name: parameters
field.documentation: List of the code specific parameters in XML format

field.name: parameters_input
field.documentation: Code parameters block passed from the wrapper to the subroutine. Does not appear as such in the data structure. This is inserted in DD_Support.xsd for automatic declaration in the Fortran and C++ type definitions.

field.name: parameters_value
field.documentation: Actual value of the code parameters (instance of Code_Parameters/Parameters in XML format)

field.name: parameters_default
field.documentation: Default value of the code parameters (instance of Code_Parameters/Parameters in XML format)

field.name: error_description
field.documentation: Error description, an array of this structure is passed as argument of the access layer calls (get and put) for handling errorbars. Does not appear as such in the data structure. This is inserted in dd_support.xsd for automatic declaration in the Fortran and C++ type definitions.

field.name: symmetric
field.documentation: Flag indicating whether the error is “+/-“ symmetric (1) or not (0)

field.name: type
field.documentation: Type of error bar description which is used (assumed to be identical for the lower and upper error): constant_absolute|constant_relative|explicit_values|expression

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: expression_upper_0d
field.documentation: Upper error expression (absolute value taken), for 1D dynamic quantities

field.name: expression_upper_1d
field.documentation: Upper error expression (absolute value taken), for 2D dynamic quantities. If its dimension is equal to 1, the same error expression is applied to all indices of the original physical quantity

field.name: expression_lower_0d
field.documentation: Lower error expression (absolute value taken), for 1D dynamic quantities

field.name: expression_lower_1d
field.documentation: Lower error expression (absolute value taken), for 2D dynamic quantities. If its dimension is equal to 1, the same error expression is applied to all indices of the original physical quantity

IDS.name: amns_data
IDS.documentation: Atomic, molecular, nuclear and surface physics data. Each occurrence contains the data for a given element (nuclear charge), describing various physical processes. For each process, data tables are organized by charge states. The coordinate system used by the data tables is described under the coordinate_system node.

field.name: process
field.documentation: Description and data for a set of physical processes.

field.name: source
field.documentation: Filename or subroutine name used to provide this data

field.name: provider
field.documentation: Name of the person in charge of producing this data

field.name: name
field.documentation: String identifying the process (e.g. EI, RC, ...)

field.name: reactants
field.documentation: Set of reactants involved in this process

field.name: element
field.documentation: List of elements forming the atom (in such case, this array should be of size 1) or molecule. Mass of atom and nuclear charge should be set to 0 for photons and electrons. The mass of atom shouldn't be set for an atomic process that is not isotope dependent.

field.name: atoms_n
field.documentation: Number of atoms of this element in the molecule

field.name: role
field.documentation: Identifier for the role of this paricipant in the reaction. For surface reactions distinguish between projectile and wall.

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: relative_charge
field.documentation: This is a flag indicating that charges are absolute (if set to 0), relative (if 1) or irrelevant (-1); relative would be used to categorize the ionization reactions from i to i+1 for all charge states; in the case of bundles, the +1 relative indicates the next bundle

field.name: metastable
field.documentation: An array identifying the metastable; if zero-length, then not a metastable; if of length 1, then the value indicates the electronic level for the metastable (mostly used for atoms/ions); if of length 2, then the 1st would indicate the electronic level and the second the vibrational level for the metastable (mostly used for molecules and molecular ions); if of length 3, then the 1st would indicate the electronic level, the second the vibrational level and the third the rotational level for the metastable (mostly used for molecules and molecular ions)

field.name: metastable_label
field.documentation: Label identifying in text form the metastable

field.name: products
field.documentation: Set of products resulting of this process

field.name: element
field.documentation: List of elements forming the atom (in such case, this array should be of size 1) or molecule. Mass of atom and nuclear charge should be set to 0 for photons and electrons. The mass of atom shouldn't be set for an atomic process that is not isotope dependent.

field.name: atoms_n
field.documentation: Number of atoms of this element in the molecule

field.name: role
field.documentation: Identifier for the role of this paricipant in the reaction. For surface reactions distinguish between projectile and wall.

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: relative_charge
field.documentation: This is a flag indicating that charges are absolute (if set to 0), relative (if 1) or irrelevant (-1); relative would be used to categorize the ionization reactions from i to i+1 for all charge states; in the case of bundles, the +1 relative indicates the next bundle

field.name: metastable
field.documentation: An array identifying the metastable; if zero-length, then not a metastable; if of length 1, then the value indicates the electronic level for the metastable (mostly used for atoms/ions); if of length 2, then the 1st would indicate the electronic level and the second the vibrational level for the metastable (mostly used for molecules and molecular ions); if of length 3, then the 1st would indicate the electronic level, the second the vibrational level and the third the rotational level for the metastable (mostly used for molecules and molecular ions)

field.name: metastable_label
field.documentation: Label identifying in text form the metastable

field.name: table_dimension
field.documentation: Table dimensionality of the process (1 to 6), valid for all charge states. Indicates which of the tables is filled (below the charge_state node)

field.name: coordinate_index
field.documentation: Index in tables_coord, specifying what coordinate systems to use for this process (valid for all tables)

field.name: result_label
field.documentation: Description of the process result (rate, cross section, sputtering yield, ...)

field.name: result_transformation
field.documentation: Transformation of the process result. Integer flag: 0=no transformation; 1=10^; 2=exp()

field.name: charge_state
field.documentation: Process tables for a set of charge states. Only one table is used for that process, defined by process(:)/table_dimension. If the data in the table_Nd array are used as parameters for a function, then no coordinates are needed, and coordinate_index should be set to -1, and result_transformation should contain the integer identifier to the internally provided functions. If the results will come from an interpolation in the table_Nd data, then coordinates must be provided in coordinate_system(process(i1)/coordinate_index), and the shape of the table should match the cartesian product of the coordinates

field.name: name
field.documentation: String identifying charge state (e.g. C+, C+2 , C+3, C+4, C+5, C+6, ...)

field.name: z_min
field.documentation: Minimum Z of the charge state bundle

field.name: z_max
field.documentation: Maximum Z of the charge state bundle (equal to z_min if no bundle)

field.name: coordinate_system
field.documentation: Array of possible coordinate systems for process tables

field.name: coordinate
field.documentation: Set of coordinates for that coordinate system. A coordinate an be either a range of real values or a set of discrete values (if interpolation_type=0)

field.name: interpolation_type
field.documentation: Interpolation strategy in this coordinate direction. Integer flag: 0=discrete (no interpolation); 1=linear; ...

field.name: extrapolation_type
field.documentation: Extrapolation strategy when leaving the domain. The first value of the vector describes the behaviour at lower bound, the second describes the at upper bound. Possible values: 0=none, report error; 1=boundary value; 2=linear extrapolation

field.name: value_labels
field.documentation: String description of discrete coordinate values (if interpolation_type=0). E.g., for spectroscopic lines, the spectroscopic description of the transition.

field.name: transformation
field.documentation: Coordinate transformation applied to coordinate values stored in coord. Integer flag: 0=none; 1=log10; 2=ln

field.name: spacing
field.documentation: Flag for specific coordinate spacing (for optimization purposes). Integer flag: 0=undefined; 1=uniform; ...

field.name: release
field.documentation: List of available releases of the AMNS data; each element contains information about the AMNS data that is included in the release. This part of the IDS is filled and stored only into shot/run=0/1, playing the role of a catalogue.

field.name: data_entry
field.documentation: For this release, list of each data item (i.e. shot/run pair containing the actual data) included in this release

field.name: run
field.documentation: Which run number is the active run number for this version

field.name: geometry_type
field.documentation: Type of geometry used to describe the surface of the detector or aperture (1:'outline', 2:'circular', 3:'rectangle'). In case of 'outline', the surface is described by an outline of point in a local coordinate system defined by a centre and three unit vectors X1, X2, X3. Note that there is some flexibility here and the data provider should choose the most convenient coordinate system for the object, respecting the definitions of (X1,X2,X3) indicated below. In case of 'circular', the surface is a circle defined by its centre, radius, and normal vector oriented towards the plasma X3. In case of 'rectangle', the surface is a rectangle defined by its centre, widths in the X1 and X2 directions, and normal vector oriented towards the plasma X3.

field.name: centre
field.documentation: If geometry_type=2, coordinates of the centre of the circle. If geometry_type=1 or 3, coordinates of the origin of the local coordinate system (X1,X2,X3) describing the plane detector/aperture. This origin is located within the detector/aperture area.

field.name: phi
field.documentation: Toroidal angle (oriented counter-clockwise when viewing from above)

field.name: radius
field.documentation: Radius of the circle, used only if geometry_type = 2

field.name: x1_unit_vector
field.documentation: Components of the X1 direction unit vector in the (X,Y,Z) coordinate system, where X is the major radius axis for phi = 0, Y is the major radius axis for phi = pi/2, and Z is the height axis. The X1 vector is more horizontal than X2 (has a smaller abs(Z) component) and oriented in the positive phi direction (counter-clockwise when viewing from above).

field.name: x2_unit_vector
field.documentation: Components of the X2 direction unit vector in the (X,Y,Z) coordinate system, where X is the major radius axis for phi = 0, Y is the major radius axis for phi = pi/2, and Z is the height axis. The X2 axis is orthonormal so that uX2 = uX3 x uX1.

field.name: x3_unit_vector
field.documentation: Components of the X3 direction unit vector in the (X,Y,Z) coordinate system, where X is the major radius axis for phi = 0, Y is the major radius axis for phi = pi/2, and Z is the height axis. The X3 axis is normal to the detector/aperture plane and oriented towards the plasma.

field.name: x1_width
field.documentation: Full width of the aperture in the X1 direction, used only if geometry_type = 3

field.name: x2_width
field.documentation: Full width of the aperture in the X2 direction, used only if geometry_type = 3

field.name: outline
field.documentation: Irregular outline of the detector/aperture in the (X1, X2) coordinate system. Repeat the first point since this is a closed contour

field.name: surface
field.documentation: Surface of the detector/aperture, derived from the above geometric data

field.name: aperture
field.documentation: Description of a set of collimating apertures

field.documentation: Temperature of the optical components (digital levels)

field.documentation: Processed image in apparent temperature. First dimension : row index (horizontal orientation). Second dimension: column index (vertical orientation). The size of this matrix is assumed to be constant over time

field.name: integration_time
field.documentation: Integration time per pixel. First dimension : row index (horizontal orientation). Second dimension: column index (vertical orientation). The size of this matrix is assumed to be constant over time. Allocate dimensions to 1 in case of uniform exposure time.

field.name: region_of_interest
field.documentation: Set of regions of interest for the real-time monitoring of machine protection. Regions of interest are defined by a combination of polygons for each image

field.name: name
field.documentation: Short string identifier (unique for a given device)

field.name: emissivity
field.documentation: Emissivity of the region of interest

field.name: surface_area
field.documentation: Area of the region of interest

field.name: type
field.documentation: Type of the region of interest usage, physical or operational. When operational, it means machine protection is active on this region of interest

field.name: mask
field.documentation: Mask of the region of interest on the frame (0 = point outside the ROI, 1 = point inside the ROI). First dimension : row index (horizontal orientation). Second dimension: column index (vertical orientation)

field.name: temperature_limit_max
field.documentation: Maximum allowed apparent temperature in the region of interest. A machine protection message is triggered if this limit is exceeded

field.name: temperature_max
field.documentation: Maximum apparent temperature measured in the region of interest

field.name: row_index_temperature_max
field.documentation: Row index with maximum apparent temperature

field.name: column_index_temperature_max
field.documentation: Column index with maximum apparent temperature

field.name: pinhole
field.documentation: Pinhole position in the (X,Y,Z) coordinate system

field.name: direction
field.documentation: Line of sight direction unit vector

field.name: field_of_view_horizontal
field.documentation: Field of view in the horizontal detector plane

field.name: field_of_view_vertical
field.documentation: Field of view in the vertical detector plane

field.name: pixels_n_horizontal
field.documentation: Number of pixels in the horizontal direction (of the detector)

field.name: pixels_n_vertical
field.documentation: Number of pixels in the vertical direction (of the detector)

field.name: target_surface_center
field.documentation: Position of the center of the targeted surface

field.name: midplane
field.documentation: Choice of midplane definition for the mapping of measurements on an equilibrium

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: frame_analysis
field.documentation: Quantities deduced from frame analysis for a set of time slices

field.name: sol_heat_decay_length
field.documentation: Heat flux decay length in SOL at divertor entrance, mapped to the mid-plane, this is the lambda_q parameter defined in reference T. Eich et al, Nucl. Fusion 53 (2013) 093031

field.name: distance_separatrix_midplane
field.documentation: Distance between the measurement position and the separatrix, mapped along flux surfaces to the outboard midplane, in the major radius direction. Positive value means the measurement is outside of the separatrix.

field.name: power_flux_parallel
field.documentation: Parallel heat flux received by the element monitored by the camera, along the distance_separatrix_midplane coordinate

field.name: type
field.documentation: Type of optical element. In case of 'mirror' and 'diaphragm', the element is described by one 'front_surface'. In case of 'lens', the element is described by 'front_surface' and 'back_surface'.

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.documentation: Radius of curvature in the X1 direction, to be filled only for curvature_type/index = 2, 4 or 5

field.name: x2_curvature
field.documentation: Radius of curvature in the X2 direction, to be filled only for curvature_type/index = 3 or 5

field.name: x2_curvature
field.documentation: Radius of curvature in the X2 direction, to be filled only for curvature_type/index = 3 or 5

field.name: thickness
field.documentation: Distance between front_surface and back_surface along the X3 vector

field.name: material_properties
field.documentation: Material properties of the optical element

field.name: type
field.documentation: Type of optical element material. In case of 'metal' refractive_index and extinction_coefficient are used. In case of 'dielectric' refractive_index and transmission_coefficient are used.

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: wavelengths
field.documentation: Wavelengths array for refractive_index, extinction_coefficient and transmission_coefficient

field.name: roughness
field.documentation: Roughness parameter of the material. Varies in range [0, 1]. 0 is perfectly specular, 1 is perfectly rough

field.name: geometry
field.documentation: Further geometrical description of the element

field.name: geometry_type
field.documentation: Type of geometry used to describe the surface of the detector or aperture (1:'outline', 2:'circular', 3:'rectangle'). In case of 'outline', the surface is described by an outline of point in a local coordinate system defined by a centre and three unit vectors X1, X2, X3. Note that there is some flexibility here and the data provider should choose the most convenient coordinate system for the object, respecting the definitions of (X1,X2,X3) indicated below. In case of 'circular', the surface is a circle defined by its centre, radius, and normal vector oriented towards the plasma X3. In case of 'rectangle', the surface is a rectangle defined by its centre, widths in the X1 and X2 directions, and normal vector oriented towards the plasma X3.

field.name: centre
field.documentation: If geometry_type=2, coordinates of the centre of the circle. If geometry_type=1 or 3, coordinates of the origin of the local coordinate system (X1,X2,X3) describing the plane detector/aperture. This origin is located within the detector/aperture area.

field.name: phi
field.documentation: Toroidal angle (oriented counter-clockwise when viewing from above)

field.name: radius
field.documentation: Radius of the circle, used only if geometry_type = 2

field.name: x1_unit_vector
field.documentation: Components of the X1 direction unit vector in the (X,Y,Z) coordinate system, where X is the major radius axis for phi = 0, Y is the major radius axis for phi = pi/2, and Z is the height axis. The X1 vector is more horizontal than X2 (has a smaller abs(Z) component) and oriented in the positive phi direction (counter-clockwise when viewing from above).

field.name: x2_unit_vector
field.documentation: Components of the X2 direction unit vector in the (X,Y,Z) coordinate system, where X is the major radius axis for phi = 0, Y is the major radius axis for phi = pi/2, and Z is the height axis. The X2 axis is orthonormal so that uX2 = uX3 x uX1.

field.name: x3_unit_vector
field.documentation: Components of the X3 direction unit vector in the (X,Y,Z) coordinate system, where X is the major radius axis for phi = 0, Y is the major radius axis for phi = pi/2, and Z is the height axis. The X3 axis is normal to the detector/aperture plane and oriented towards the plasma.

field.name: x1_width
field.documentation: Full width of the aperture in the X1 direction, used only if geometry_type = 3

field.name: x2_width
field.documentation: Full width of the aperture in the X2 direction, used only if geometry_type = 3

field.name: outline
field.documentation: Irregular outline of the detector/aperture in the (X1, X2) coordinate system. Repeat the first point since this is a closed contour

field.name: surface
field.documentation: Surface of the detector/aperture, derived from the above geometric data

In case of 'outline', the surface is described by an outline of point in a local coordinate system defined by a centre and three unit vectors X1, X2, X3. Note that there is some flexibility here and the data provider should choose the most convenient coordinate system for the object, respecting the definitions of (X1,X2,X3) indicated below. In case of 'circular', the surface is a circle defined by its centre, radius, and normal vector oriented towards the plasma X3. In case of 'rectangle', the surface is a rectangle defined by its centre, widths in the X1 and X2 directions, and normal vector oriented towards the plasma X3.

field.name: centre
field.documentation: If geometry_type=2, coordinates of the centre of the circle. If geometry_type=1 or 3, coordinates of the origin of the local coordinate system (X1,X2,X3) describing the plane detector/aperture. This origin is located within the detector/aperture area.

field.name: phi
field.documentation: Toroidal angle (oriented counter-clockwise when viewing from above)

field.name: radius
field.documentation: Radius of the circle, used only if geometry_type = 2

field.name: x1_unit_vector
field.documentation: Components of the X1 direction unit vector in the (X,Y,Z) coordinate system, where X is the major radius axis for phi = 0, Y is the major radius axis for phi = pi/2, and Z is the height axis. The X1 vector is more horizontal than X2 (has a smaller abs(Z) component) and oriented in the positive phi direction (counter-clockwise when viewing from above).

field.name: x2_unit_vector
field.documentation: Components of the X2 direction unit vector in the (X,Y,Z) coordinate system, where X is the major radius axis for phi = 0, Y is the major radius axis for phi = pi/2, and Z is the height axis. The X2 axis is orthonormal so that uX2 = uX3 x uX1.

field.name: x3_unit_vector
field.documentation: Components of the X3 direction unit vector in the (X,Y,Z) coordinate system, where X is the major radius axis for phi = 0, Y is the major radius axis for phi = pi/2, and Z is the height axis. The X3 axis is normal to the detector/aperture plane and oriented towards the plasma.

field.name: x1_width
field.documentation: Full width of the aperture in the X1 direction, used only if geometry_type = 3

field.name: x2_width
field.documentation: Full width of the aperture in the X2 direction, used only if geometry_type = 3

field.name: outline
field.documentation: Irregular outline of the detector/aperture in the (X1, X2) coordinate system. Repeat the first point since this is a closed contour

field.name: surface
field.documentation: Surface of the detector/aperture, derived from the above geometric data

field.name: viewing_angle_alpha_bounds
field.documentation: Minimum and maximum values of alpha angle of the field of view, where alpha is the agle between the axis X3 and projection of the chord of view on the plane X1X3 counted clockwise from the top view of X2 axis. X1, X2, X3 are the ones of the first aperture (i.e. the closest to the plasma).

field.name: viewing_angle_beta_bounds
field.documentation: Minimum and maximum values of beta angle of the field of view, where beta is the angle between the axis X3 and projection of the chord of view on the plane X2X3 counted clockwise from the top view of X1 axis. X1, X2, X3 are the ones of the first aperture (i.e. the closest to the plasma).

field.name: pixel_to_alpha
field.documentation: Alpha angle of each pixel in the horizontal axis

field.name: pixel_to_beta
field.documentation: Beta angle of each pixel in the vertical axis

field.name: wavelength_lower
field.documentation: Lower bound of the detector wavelength range

field.name: wavelength_upper
field.documentation: Upper bound of the detector wavelength range

field.name: counts_to_radiance
field.documentation: Counts to radiance factor, for each pixel of the detector. Includes both the transmission losses in the relay optics and the quantum efficiency of the camera itself, integrated over the wavelength range

field.name: noise
field.documentation: Detector noise (e.g. read-out noise) (rms counts per second exposure time)

field.name: columns_n
field.documentation: Number of pixel columns in the horizontal direction

field.name: lines_n
field.documentation: Number of pixel lines in the vertical direction

field.name: image_raw
field.documentation: Raw image (unprocessed) (digital levels). First dimension : line index (horizontal axis). Second dimension: column index (vertical axis).

field.name: radiance
field.documentation: Radiance image. First dimension : line index (horizontal axis). Second dimension: column index (vertical axis).

field.name: geometry_matrix
field.documentation: Description of geometry matrix (ray transfer matrix)

field.name: data
field.documentation: The Ray Transfer Matrix (RTM, or geometry matrix) here provides transformation of the signal from each individual unit light source (voxel) to each pixel of the receiver (detector). The emission profile has [photons.m^-3.s^-1.sr^-1] units and radiance signal has [photons.m^-2.s^-1.sr^-1] units. So the RTM has [m] units. This data is stored in a sparse form, i.e. the array contains only the non-zero element of the Ray transfer matrix. The voxel index corresponding to an element of this array can be found in voxel_indices. The pixel indices corresponding to an element of this array can be found in pixel_indices

field.name: voxel_indices
field.documentation: List of voxel indices (defined in the voxel map) used in the sparse data array

field.name: pixel_indices
field.documentation: List of pixel indices used in the sparse data array. The first dimension refers to the data array index. The second dimension lists the line index (horizontal axis) in first position, then the column index (vertical axis).

field.name: data
field.documentation: The Ray Transfer Matrix (RTM, or geometry matrix) here provides transformation of the signal from each individual unit light source (voxel) to each pixel of the receiver (detector). The emission profile has [photons.m^-3.s^-1.sr^-1] units and radiance signal has [photons.m^-2.s^-1.sr^-1] units. So the RTM has [m] units. This data is stored in a sparse form, i.e. the array contains only the non-zero element of the Ray transfer matrix. The voxel index corresponding to an element of this array can be found in voxel_indices. The pixel indices corresponding to an element of this array can be found in pixel_indices

field.name: voxel_indices
field.documentation: List of voxel indices (defined in the voxel map) used in the sparse data array

field.name: pixel_indices
field.documentation: List of pixel indices used in the sparse data array. The first dimension refers to the data array index. The second dimension lists the line index (horizontal axis) in first position, then the column index (vertical axis).

field.name: interpolated
field.documentation: Interpolated geometry matrix for reflected light

field.name: phi
field.documentation: Toroidal angle (oriented counter-clockwise when viewing from above) of interpolation knots

field.name: data
field.documentation: Interpolated Ray Transfer Matrix (RTM, or geometry matrix), which provides transformation of the reflected light from each interpolation knot to the receiver (detector pixel). When convolving with an emission profile, the values must be interpolated to the emission grid and multiplied by the volume of the grid cells. The interpolated matrix is given on an array of interpolation knots of coordinates r, z and phi (third dimension of this array). The first two dimension correspond to the detector pixels : first dimension : line index (horizontal axis); second dimension: column index (vertical axis).

field.name: voxel_map
field.documentation: Voxel map for geometry matrix. The cells with same number are merged in the computation into a single emission source meta-cell (the voxel). Cells with number -1 are excluded. Voxel count starts from 0.

field.name: voxels_n
field.documentation: Number of voxels defined in the voxel_map.

field.name: emission_grid
field.documentation: Grid defining the light emission cells

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: type
field.documentation: Type of optical element. In case of 'mirror' and 'diaphragm', the element is described by one 'front_surface'. In case of 'lens', the element is described by 'front_surface' and 'back_surface'.

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: x1_curvature
field.documentation: Radius of curvature in the X1 direction, to be filled only for curvature_type/index = 2, 4 or 5

field.name: x2_curvature
field.documentation: Radius of curvature in the X2 direction, to be filled only for curvature_type/index = 3 or 5

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.documentation: Radius of curvature in the X1 direction, to be filled only for curvature_type/index = 2, 4 or 5

field.name: x2_curvature
field.documentation: Radius of curvature in the X2 direction, to be filled only for curvature_type/index = 3 or 5

field.name: thickness
field.documentation: Distance between front_surface and back_surface along the X3 vector

field.name: material_properties
field.documentation: Material properties of the optical element

field.name: type
field.documentation: Type of optical element material. In case of 'metal' refractive_index and extinction_coefficient are used. In case of 'dielectric' refractive_index and transmission_coefficient are used.

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: wavelengths
field.documentation: Wavelengths array for refractive_index, extinction_coefficient and transmission_coefficient

field.name: roughness
field.documentation: Roughness parameter of the material. Varies in range [0, 1]. 0 is perfectly specular, 1 is perfectly rough

If 0, the time values are stored in the various time fields at lower levels in the tree. In the case only constant or static nodes are filled within the IDS, homogeneous_time must be set to 2

field.name: path

field.name: reference
field.documentation: List of references used to populate or calculate this node, identified as explained below. In case the node is the result of of a calculation / data processing, the reference is an input to the process described in the "code" structure at the root of the IDS. The reference can be an IDS (identified by a URI or a persitent identifier, see syntax in the link below) or non-IDS data imported directly from an non-IMAS database (identified by the command used to import the reference, or the persistent identifier of the data reference). Often data are obtained by a chain of processes, however only the last process input are recorded here. The full chain of provenance has then to be reconstructed recursively from the provenance information contained in the data references.

field.name: timestamp

field.documentation: Radius of the circle, used only if geometry_type/index = 2

field.name: x1_unit_vector
field.documentation: Components of the X1 direction unit vector in the (X,Y,Z) coordinate system, where X is the major radius axis for phi = 0, Y is the major radius axis for phi = pi/2, and Z is the height axis. The X1 vector is more horizontal than X2 (has a smaller abs(Z) component) and oriented in the positive phi direction (counter-clockwise when viewing from above).

field.name: x2_unit_vector
field.documentation: Components of the X2 direction unit vector in the (X,Y,Z) coordinate system, where X is the major radius axis for phi = 0, Y is the major radius axis for phi = pi/2, and Z is the height axis. The X2 axis is orthonormal so that uX2 = uX3 x uX1.

field.name: x3_unit_vector
field.documentation: Components of the X3 direction unit vector in the (X,Y,Z) coordinate system, where X is the major radius axis for phi = 0, Y is the major radius axis for phi = pi/2, and Z is the height axis. The X3 axis is normal to the filter surface and oriented towards the plasma.

field.name: x1_width
field.documentation: Full width of the filter in the X1 direction, used only if geometry_type/index = 3

field.name: x2_width
field.documentation: Full width of the filter in the X2 direction, used only if geometry_type/index = 3

field.name: outline
field.documentation: Irregular outline of the filter in the (X1, X2) coordinate system, used only if geometry_type/index=1. Repeat the first point since this is a closed contour

field.name: x1_curvature
field.documentation: Radius of curvature in the X1 direction, to be filled only for curvature_type/index = 2, 4 or 5

field.name: x2_curvature
field.documentation: Radius of curvature in the X2 direction, to be filled only for curvature_type/index = 3 or 5

field.name: surface
field.documentation: Surface of the filter, derived from the above geometric data

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: wavelength_lower
field.documentation: Lower bound of the filter wavelength range

field.name: wavelength_upper
field.documentation: Upper bound of the filter wavelength range

field.name: photon_absorption
field.documentation: Probability of absorbing a photon passing through the filter as a function of its wavelength

field.name: readout_time
field.documentation: Time used to read out each frame on the detector

field.name: latency
field.documentation: Upper bound of the delay between physical information received by the detector and data available on the real-time (RT) network.

field.name: detector_humidity
field.documentation: Fraction of humidity (0-1) measured at the detector level

field.name: detector_temperature
field.documentation: Temperature measured at the detector level
