field.name: aperture
field.documentation: Description of the collimating aperture of the diagnostic, relevant to all lines-of-sight (channels)

field.name: geometry_type
field.documentation: Type of geometry used to describe the surface of the detector or aperture (1:'outline', 2:'circular', 3:'rectangle'). In case of 'outline', the surface is described by an outline of point in a local coordinate system defined by a centre and three unit vectors X1, X2, X3. Note that there is some flexibility here and the data provider should choose the most convenient coordinate system for the object, respecting the definitions of (X1,X2,X3) indicated below. In case of 'circular', the surface is a circle defined by its centre, radius, and normal vector oriented towards the plasma X3. In case of 'rectangle', the surface is a rectangle defined by its centre, widths in the X1 and X2 directions, and normal vector oriented towards the plasma X3.

field.name: centre
field.documentation: If geometry_type=2, coordinates of the centre of the circle. If geometry_type=1 or 3, coordinates of the origin of the local coordinate system (X1,X2,X3) describing the plane detector/aperture. This origin is located within the detector/aperture area.

field.name: phi
field.documentation: Toroidal angle (oriented counter-clockwise when viewing from above)

field.name: radius
field.documentation: Radius of the circle, used only if geometry_type = 2

field.name: x1_unit_vector
field.documentation: Components of the X1 direction unit vector in the (X,Y,Z) coordinate system, where X is the major radius axis for phi = 0, Y is the major radius axis for phi = pi/2, and Z is the height axis. The X1 vector is more horizontal than X2 (has a smaller abs(Z) component) and oriented in the positive phi direction (counter-clockwise when viewing from above).

field.name: x2_unit_vector
field.documentation: Components of the X2 direction unit vector in the (X,Y,Z) coordinate system, where X is the major radius axis for phi = 0, Y is the major radius axis for phi = pi/2, and Z is the height axis. The X2 axis is orthonormal so that uX2 = uX3 x uX1.

field.name: x3_unit_vector
field.documentation: Components of the X3 direction unit vector in the (X,Y,Z) coordinate system, where X is the major radius axis for phi = 0, Y is the major radius axis for phi = pi/2, and Z is the height axis. The X3 axis is normal to the detector/aperture plane and oriented towards the plasma.

field.name: x1_width
field.documentation: Full width of the aperture in the X1 direction, used only if geometry_type = 3

field.name: x2_width
field.documentation: Full width of the aperture in the X2 direction, used only if geometry_type = 3

field.name: outline
field.documentation: Irregular outline of the detector/aperture in the (X1, X2) coordinate system. Repeat the first point since this is a closed contour

field.name: surface
field.documentation: Surface of the detector/aperture, derived from the above geometric data

field.name: etendue
field.documentation: Etendue (geometric extent) of the optical system

field.name: etendue_method
field.documentation: Method used to calculate the etendue. Index = 0 : exact calculation with a 4D integral; 1 : approximation with first order formula (detector surface times solid angle subtended by the apertures); 2 : other methods

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: channel
field.documentation: Set of channels (lines-of-sight). The line-of-sight is defined by the centre of the collimating aperture and the position of the measurements.

field.name: name
field.documentation: Short string identifier (unique for a given device)

field.name: description
field.documentation: Description, e.g. “channel viewing the upper divertor”

field.name: phi
field.documentation: Toroidal angle (oriented counter-clockwise when viewing from above)

field.name: t_i_average
field.documentation: Ion temperature (averaged on charge states and ion species) at the channel measurement point

field.name: t_i_average_method
field.documentation: Description of the method used to reconstruct the average ion temperature

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: zeff
field.documentation: Local ionic effective charge at the channel measurement point

field.name: zeff_method
field.documentation: Description of the method used to reconstruct the local effective charge

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: zeff_line_average
field.documentation: Ionic effective charge, line average along the channel line-of-sight

field.name: zeff_line_average_method
field.documentation: Description of the method used to reconstruct the line average effective charge

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: momentum_phi
field.documentation: Total plasma toroidal momentum, summed over ion species and electrons weighted by their density and major radius, i.e. sum_over_species(n*R*m*Vphi), at the channel measurement point

field.name: momentum_phi_method
field.documentation: Description of the method used to reconstruct the total plasma toroidal momentum

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: ion
field.documentation: Physical quantities related to ion species and charge stage (H+, D+, T+, He+2, Li+3, Be+4, C+6, N+7, O+8, Ne+10, Si+14, Ar+16 or Ar+18) derived from the measured charge exchange emission of each species, at the position of the measurement

field.name: a
field.documentation: Mass of atom of the ion

field.name: name
field.documentation: String identifying the ion (e.g. H+, D+, T+, He+2, C+6, ...)

field.name: t_i
field.documentation: Ion temperature at the channel measurement point

field.name: t_i_method
field.documentation: Description of the method used to derive the ion temperature

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: velocity_phi
field.documentation: Toroidal velocity of the ion (oriented counter-clockwise when seen from above) at the channel measurement point

field.name: velocity_phi_method
field.documentation: Description of the method used to reconstruct the ion toroidal velocity

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: velocity_pol
field.documentation: Poloidal velocity of the ion (oriented clockwise when seen from front on the right side of the tokamak axi-symmetry axis) at the channel measurement point

field.name: velocity_pol_method
field.documentation: Description of the method used to reconstruct the ion poloidal velocity

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: n_i_over_n_e
field.documentation: Ion concentration (ratio of the ion density over the electron density) at the channel measurement point

field.name: n_i_over_n_e_method
field.documentation: Description of the method used to derive the ion concentration

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: a
field.documentation: Mass of atom of the diagnostic neutral beam particle

field.name: z_ion
field.documentation: Ion charge of the diagnostic neutral beam particle

field.name: z_n
field.documentation: Nuclear charge of the diagnostic neutral beam particle

field.name: name
field.documentation: String identifying the diagnostic neutral beam particle

field.name: transition_wavelength
field.documentation: Unshifted wavelength of the BES transition

field.name: doppler_shift
field.documentation: Doppler shift due to the diagnostic neutral beam particle velocity

field.name: lorentz_shift
field.documentation: Lorentz shift due to the Lorentz electric field (vxB) in the frame of the diagnostic neutral beam particles moving with a velocity v across the magnetic field B

field.name: radiances
field.documentation: Calibrated intensities of the 9 splitted lines (Stark effect due to Lorentz electric field). Note: radiances are integrated over the sightline crossing the neutral beam

field.name: ion_fast
field.documentation: Derived Fast Ion Charge eXchange (FICX) parameters

field.name: a
field.documentation: Mass of atom of the fast ion

field.name: z_n
field.documentation: Nuclear charge of the fast ion

field.name: name
field.documentation: String identifying the fast ion (e.g. H+, D+, T+, He+2, C+6, ...)

field.name: transition_wavelength
field.documentation: Unshifted wavelength of the fast ion charge exchange transition

field.name: radiance
field.documentation: Calibrated radiance of the fast ion charge exchange spectrum assuming the shape is pre-defined (e.g. by the Fokker-Planck slowing-down function). Note: radiance is integrated over the sightline crossing the neutral beam

field.name: radiance_spectral_method
field.documentation: Description of the method used to reconstruct the fast ion charge exchange spectrum (e.g. what pre-defined slowing-down and source functions used)

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: spectrum
field.documentation: Set of spectra obtained by various gratings

field.name: grating
field.documentation: Number of grating lines per unit length

field.name: slit_width
field.documentation: Width of the slit (placed in the object focal plane)

field.name: instrument_function
field.documentation: Array of Gaussian widths and amplitudes which as a sum make up the instrument fuction. IF(lambda) = sum( instrument_function(1,i)/sqrt(2 * pi * instrument_function(2,i)^2 ) * exp( -lambda^2/(2 * instrument_function(2,i)^2) ) ),whereby sum( instrument_function(1,i) ) = 1

field.name: intensity_spectrum
field.documentation: Intensity spectrum (not calibrated), i.e. number of photoelectrons detected by unit time by a wavelength pixel of the channel, taking into account electronic gain compensation and channels relative calibration

field.name: radiance_spectral
field.documentation: Calibrated spectral radiance (radiance per unit wavelength)

field.name: name
field.documentation: String identifying the processed spectral line: Spectroscopy notation emitting element (e.g. D I, Be IV, W I, C VI), transition - if known - between round brackets (e.g. (3-2) ) and indication type of charge exchange - if applicable - between square brackets (e.g. [ACX] or [PCX]). Example for beryllium active charge exchange line at 468.5 nm: 'Be IV (8-6) [ACX]'. Example for impact excitation tungsten line coming from the plasma edge: 'W I'

field.name: wavelength_central
field.documentation: Unshifted central wavelength of the processed spectral line

field.name: radiance
field.documentation: Calibrated, background subtracted radiance (integrated over the spectrum for this line)

field.name: intensity
field.documentation: Non-calibrated intensity (integrated over the spectrum for this line), i.e. number of photoelectrons detected by unit time, taking into account electronic gain compensation and channels relative calibration

field.name: width
field.documentation: Full width at Half Maximum (FWHM) of the emission line

field.name: shift
field.documentation: Shift of the emission line wavelength with respected to the unshifted cental wavelength (e.g. Doppler shift)

field.name: radiance_continuum
field.documentation: Calibrated continuum intensity in the middle of the spectrum per unit wavelength

field.name: latency
field.documentation: Upper bound of the delay between physical information received by the detector and data available on the real-time (RT) network.

field.name: conductor
field.documentation: Set of conductors inside the coil. The structure can be used with size 1 for a simplified description as a single conductor. A conductor is composed of several elements, serially connected, i.e. transporting the same current.

field.name: elements
field.documentation: Set of geometrical elements (line segments and/or arcs of a circle) describing the contour of the conductor centre. We define a coordinate system associated to each element as follows: for the arc and circle elements: binormal = (start point - center) x (intermediate point - center). This vector points in the direction of the circle / arc axis. normal = (center - point on curve). The normal vector will rotate as the point moves around the curve. Tangent = normal x binormal. For the line element we require an extra point, using the currently redundant intermediate point to define the line element's normal axis. The local coordinates for the line element then become: tangent = end point - start point; normal = intermediate point - start point; binormal = tangent x normal. It is assumed that all the axes above are normalized such that they have a unit length.

field.name: types
field.documentation: Type of every element: 1: line segment, its ends are given by the start and end points; index = 2: arc of a circle; index = 3: full circle

field.name: start_points
field.documentation: Position of the start point of every element

field.name: phi
field.documentation: Toroidal angle (oriented counter-clockwise when viewing from above)

field.name: intermediate_points
field.documentation: Position of an intermediate point along the circle or arc of circle, for every element, providing the orientation of the element (must define with the corresponding start point an aperture angle strictly inferior to PI). In the case of a line segment (../types/index=1), fill this node with a point such that the vector intermediate_point - start_point defines the direction of the element's normal axis (see documentation of ../elements)

field.name: phi
field.documentation: Toroidal angle (oriented counter-clockwise when viewing from above)

field.name: end_points
field.documentation: Position of the end point of every element. Meaningful only if type/index = 1 or 2, fill with default/empty value otherwise

field.name: phi
field.documentation: Toroidal angle (oriented counter-clockwise when viewing from above)

field.name: centres
field.documentation: Position of the centre of the arc of a circle of every element (meaningful only if type/index = 2 or 3, fill with default/empty value otherwise)

field.name: phi
field.documentation: Toroidal angle (oriented counter-clockwise when viewing from above)

field.name: cross_section
field.documentation: The cross-section perpendicular to the conductor contour is described by a series of contour points, given by their relative position with respect to the start point of each element. If the size of this array of structure is equal to 1, then the cross-section is given only for the first element and translated along the conductor elements. Otherwise, it's given explictly for each element, allowing to describe changes of the cross section shape

field.name: geometry_type
field.documentation: Geometry type used to describe the cross section of this element. The conductor centre is given by the ../../elements description.

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: width
field.documentation: Full width of the rectangle or square in the normal direction, when geometry_type/index = 3 or 4. Diameter of the circle when geometry_type/index = 2. Outer diameter of the annulus in case geometry_type/index = 5

field.name: height
field.documentation: Full height of the rectangle in the binormal direction, used only if geometry_type/index = 3

field.name: radius_inner
field.documentation: Inner radius of the annulus, used only if geometry_type/index = 5

field.name: outline
field.documentation: Polygonal outline of the cross section in the (normal, binormal) coordinate system. Do NOT repeat the first point.

field.name: area
field.documentation: Area of the conductor cross-section, derived from the above geometric data

field.name: voltage
field.documentation: Voltage on the conductor terminals. Sign convention : positive when the current flows in the direction in which conductor elements are ordered (from start to end for a positive polarity coil)

field.name: turns
field.documentation: Number of total turns in the coil. May be a fraction when describing the coil connections.

field.name: current
field.documentation: Current in one turn of the coil (to be multiplied by the number of turns to calculate the magnetic field generated). Sign convention : a positive current flows in the direction in which conductor elements are ordered (from start to end for a positive polarity coil)

field.name: voltage
field.documentation: Voltage on the coil terminals. Sign convention : positive when the current flows in the direction in which conductor elements are ordered (from start to end for a positive polarity coil)

field.name: latency
field.documentation: Upper bound of the delay between input command received from the RT network and actuator starting to react. Applies globally to the system described by this IDS unless specific latencies (e.g. channel-specific or antenna-specific) are provided at a deeper level in the IDS structure.

field.name: vacuum_toroidal_field
field.documentation: Characteristics of the vacuum toroidal field (used in Rho_Tor definition and in the normalization of current densities)

field.name: r0
field.documentation: Reference major radius where the vacuum toroidal magnetic field is given (usually a fixed position such as the middle of the vessel at the equatorial midplane)

field.name: b0
field.documentation: Vacuum toroidal field at R0 [T]; Positive sign means anti-clockwise when viewing from above. The product R0B0 must be consistent with the b_tor_vacuum_r field of the tf IDS.

field.name: change
field.documentation: Set of instant change terms (each being due to a different phenomenon)

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: profiles_1d
field.documentation: Changes in 1D core profiles for various time slices. This structure mirrors core_profiles/profiles_1d and describes instant changes to each of these physical quantities (i.e. a signed difference quantity after change - quantity before change)

field.name: rho_tor_norm
field.documentation: Normalized toroidal flux coordinate. The normalizing value for rho_tor_norm, is the toroidal flux coordinate at the equilibrium boundary (LCFS or 99.x % of the LCFS in case of a fixed boundary equilibium calculation, see time_slice/boundary/b_flux_pol_norm in the equilibrium IDS)

field.name: rho_tor
field.documentation: Toroidal flux coordinate = sqrt(phi/(pi*b0)), where the toroidal magnetic field, b0, corresponds to that stored in vacuum_toroidal_field/b0 and pi can be found in the IMAS constants

field.name: psi
field.documentation: Poloidal magnetic flux. Integral of magnetic field passing through a contour defined by the intersection of a flux surface passing through the point of interest and a Z=constant plane. If the integration surface is flat, the surface normal vector is in the increasing vertical coordinate direction, Z, namely upwards.

field.name: volume
field.documentation: Volume enclosed inside the magnetic surface

field.name: area
field.documentation: Cross-sectional area of the flux surface

field.name: surface
field.documentation: Surface area of the toroidal flux surface

field.name: psi_magnetic_axis
field.documentation: Value of the poloidal magnetic flux at the magnetic axis (useful to normalize the psi array values when the radial grid doesn't go from the magnetic axis to the plasma boundary)

field.name: psi_boundary
field.documentation: Value of the poloidal magnetic flux at the plasma boundary (useful to normalize the psi array values when the radial grid doesn't go from the magnetic axis to the plasma boundary)

field.name: temperature_validity
field.documentation: Indicator of the validity of the temperature profile. 0: valid from automated processing, 1: valid and certified by the RO; - 1 means problem identified in the data processing (request verification by the RO), -2: invalid data, should not be used

field.name: temperature_fit
field.documentation: Information on the fit used to obtain the temperature profile

field.name: measured
field.documentation: Measured values. Units are: as_parent for a local measurement, as_parent.m for a line integrated measurement.

field.name: source
field.documentation: Path to the source data for each measurement in the IMAS data dictionary, e.g. ece/channel(i)/t_e for the electron temperature on the i-th channel in the ECE IDS

field.name: time_measurement
field.documentation: Exact time slices used from the time array of the measurement source data. The time slice is indicated for each measurement point considered in the fit since measurements may come from different and thus asynchronous diagnostics. If the time slice does not exist in the time array of the source data, it means linear interpolation has been used

field.name: time_measurement_slice_method
field.documentation: Method used to slice the data : index = 0 means using exact time slice of the measurement, 1 means linear interpolation, ...

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: time_measurement_width
field.documentation: In case the measurements are averaged over a time interval, this node is the full width of this time interval (empty otherwise). In case the slicing/averaging method doesn't use a hard time interval cutoff, this width is the characteristic time span of the slicing/averaging method. By convention, the time interval starts at time_measurement-time_width and ends at time_measurement.

field.name: local
field.documentation: Integer flag : 1 means local measurement, 0 means line-integrated measurement

field.name: rho_tor_norm
field.documentation: Normalized toroidal flux coordinate of each measurement (local value for a local measurement, minimum value reached by the line of sight for a line measurement)

field.name: weight
field.documentation: Weight given to each measured value

field.name: reconstructed
field.documentation: Value reconstructed from the fit. Units are: as_parent for a local measurement, as_parent.m for a line integrated measurement.

field.name: chi_squared
field.documentation: Squared error normalized by the weighted standard deviation considered in the minimization process : chi_squared = weight^2 *(reconstructed - measured)^2 / sigma^2, where sigma is the standard deviation of the measurement error

field.name: parameters
field.documentation: List of the fit specific parameters in XML format

field.documentation: Indicator of the validity of the density profile. 0: valid from automated processing, 1: valid and certified by the RO; - 1 means problem identified in the data processing (request verification by the RO), -2: invalid data, should not be used

field.name: pressure_fast_perpendicular
field.documentation: Fast (non-thermal) perpendicular pressure (sum over charge states when multiple charge states are considered)

field.name: pressure_fast_parallel
field.documentation: Fast (non-thermal) parallel pressure (sum over charge states when multiple charge states are considered)

field.name: rotation_frequency_tor
field.documentation: Toroidal rotation frequency (i.e. toroidal velocity divided by the major radius at which the toroidal velocity is taken) (average over charge states when multiple charge states are considered)

field.name: velocity
field.documentation: Velocity (average over charge states when multiple charge states are considered) at the position of maximum major radius on every flux surface

field.name: multiple_states_flag
field.documentation: Multiple states calculation flag : 0-Only the 'ion' level is considered and the 'state' array of structure is empty; 1-Ion states are considered and are described in the 'state' array of structure

field.name: state
field.documentation: Quantities related to the different states of the species (ionization, energy, excitation, ...)

field.name: z_min
field.documentation: Minimum Z of the charge state bundle

field.name: z_max
field.documentation: Maximum Z of the charge state bundle (equal to z_min if no bundle)

field.name: z_average
field.documentation: Average Z of the charge state bundle, volume averaged over the plasma radius (equal to z_min if no bundle), = sum (Z*x_z) where x_z is the relative concentration of a given charge state in the bundle, i.e. sum(x_z) = 1 over the bundle.

field.name: z_square_average
field.documentation: Average Z square of the charge state bundle, volume averaged over the plasma radius (equal to z_min squared if no bundle), = sum (Z^2*x_z) where x_z is the relative concentration of a given charge state in the bundle, i.e. sum(x_z) = 1 over the bundle.

field.name: z_average_1d
field.documentation: Average charge profile of the charge state bundle (equal to z_min if no bundle), = sum (Z*x_z) where x_z is the relative concentration of a given charge state in the bundle, i.e. sum(x_z) = 1 over the bundle.

field.name: z_average_square_1d
field.documentation: Average square charge profile of the charge state bundle (equal to z_min squared if no bundle), = sum (Z^2*x_z) where x_z is the relative concentration of a given charge state in the bundle, i.e. sum(x_z) = 1 over the bundle.

field.name: ionization_potential
field.documentation: Cumulative and average ionization potential to reach a given bundle. Defined as sum (x_z* (sum of Epot from z'=0 to z-1)), where Epot is the ionization potential of ion Xz’+, and x_z is the relative concentration of a given charge state in the bundle, i.e. sum(x_z) = 1 over the bundle.

field.name: name
field.documentation: String identifying state (e.g. C+, C+2 , C+3, C+4, C+5, C+6, ...)

field.name: electron_configuration
field.documentation: Configuration of atomic orbitals of this state, e.g. 1s2-2s1

field.name: vibrational_mode
field.documentation: Vibrational mode of this state, e.g. "A_g". Need to define, or adopt a standard nomenclature.

field.name: rotation_frequency_tor
field.documentation: Toroidal rotation frequency (i.e. toroidal velocity divided by the major radius at which the toroidal velocity is taken)

field.name: velocity
field.documentation: Velocity at the position of maximum major radius on every flux surface

field.name: density_fit
field.documentation: Information on the fit used to obtain the density profile

field.name: measured
field.documentation: Measured values. Units are: as_parent for a local measurement, as_parent.m for a line integrated measurement.

field.name: source
field.documentation: Path to the source data for each measurement in the IMAS data dictionary, e.g. ece/channel(i)/t_e for the electron temperature on the i-th channel in the ECE IDS

field.name: time_measurement
field.documentation: Exact time slices used from the time array of the measurement source data. The time slice is indicated for each measurement point considered in the fit since measurements may come from different and thus asynchronous diagnostics. If the time slice does not exist in the time array of the source data, it means linear interpolation has been used

field.name: time_measurement_slice_method
field.documentation: Method used to slice the data : index = 0 means using exact time slice of the measurement, 1 means linear interpolation, ...

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: time_measurement_width
field.documentation: In case the measurements are averaged over a time interval, this node is the full width of this time interval (empty otherwise). In case the slicing/averaging method doesn't use a hard time interval cutoff, this width is the characteristic time span of the slicing/averaging method. By convention, the time interval starts at time_measurement-time_width and ends at time_measurement.

field.documentation: Integer flag : 1 means local measurement, 0 means line-integrated measurement

field.name: rho_tor_norm
field.documentation: Normalized toroidal flux coordinate of each measurement (local value for a local measurement, minimum value reached by the line of sight for a line measurement)

field.name: weight
field.documentation: Weight given to each measured value

field.name: reconstructed
field.documentation: Value reconstructed from the fit. Units are: as_parent for a local measurement, as_parent.m for a line integrated measurement.

field.name: chi_squared
field.documentation: Squared error normalized by the weighted standard deviation considered in the minimization process : chi_squared = weight^2 *(reconstructed - measured)^2 / sigma^2, where sigma is the standard deviation of the measurement error

field.name: pressure_ion_total
field.documentation: Total (sum over ion species) thermal ion pressure

field.name: j_total
field.documentation: Total parallel current density = average(jtot.B) / B0, where B0 = Core_Profiles/Vacuum_Toroidal_Field/ B0

field.name: current_parallel_inside
field.documentation: Parallel current driven inside the flux surface. Cumulative surface integral of j_total

field.name: j_phi
field.documentation: Total toroidal current density = average(J_phi/R) / average(1/R)

field.name: j_ohmic
field.documentation: Ohmic parallel current density = average(J_Ohmic.B) / B0, where B0 = Core_Profiles/Vacuum_Toroidal_Field/ B0

field.name: j_non_inductive
field.documentation: Non-inductive (includes bootstrap) parallel current density = average(jni.B) / B0, where B0 = Core_Profiles/Vacuum_Toroidal_Field/ B0

field.name: j_bootstrap
field.documentation: Bootstrap current density = average(J_Bootstrap.B) / B0, where B0 = Core_Profiles/Vacuum_Toroidal_Field/ B0

field.name: e_field
field.documentation: Electric field, averaged on the magnetic surface. E.g for the parallel component, average(E.B) / B0, using core_profiles/vacuum_toroidal_field/b0

field.name: phi_potential
field.documentation: Electrostatic potential, averaged on the magnetic flux surface

field.name: rotation_frequency_tor_sonic
field.documentation: Derivative of the flux surface averaged electrostatic potential with respect to the poloidal flux, multiplied by (1/2pi). This quantity is the toroidal angular rotation frequency due to the ExB drift, introduced in formula (43) of Hinton and Wong, Physics of Fluids 3082 (1985), also referred to as sonic flow in regimes in which the toroidal velocity is dominant over the poloidal velocity

field.name: q
field.documentation: Safety factor (only positive when toroidal current and magnetic field are in same direction)

field.name: magnetic_shear
field.documentation: Magnetic shear, defined as rho_tor/q . dq/drho_tor

If 1, the time of this IDS is homogeneous, i.e. the time values for this IDS are stored in the time node just below the root of this IDS. If 0, the time values are stored in the various time fields at lower levels in the tree. In the case only constant or static nodes are filled within the IDS, homogeneous_time must be set to 2

field.name: path
field.documentation: Path of the node within the IDS, following the syntax given in the link below. If empty, means the provenance information applies to the whole IDS.

field.name: reference
field.documentation: List of references used to populate or calculate this node, identified as explained below. In case the node is the result of of a calculation / data processing, the reference is an input to the process described in the "code" structure at the root of the IDS. The reference can be an IDS (identified by a URI or a persitent identifier, see syntax in the link below) or non-IDS data imported directly from an non-IMAS database (identified by the command used to import the reference, or the persistent identifier of the data reference). Often data are obtained by a chain of processes, however only the last process input are recorded here. The full chain of provenance has then to be reconstructed recursively from the provenance information contained in the data references.

field.name: psi

field.name: pressure_fast_parallel

field.name: rotation_frequency_tor

field.name: z_min
field.documentation: Minimum Z of the charge state bundle

field.name: z_max
field.documentation: Maximum Z of the charge state bundle (equal to z_min if no bundle)

field.name: z_average
field.documentation: Average Z of the charge state bundle, volume averaged over the plasma radius (equal to z_min if no bundle), = sum (Z*x_z) where x_z is the relative concentration of a given charge state in the bundle, i.e. sum(x_z) = 1 over the bundle.

field.name: z_square_average
field.documentation: Average Z square of the charge state bundle, volume averaged over the plasma radius (equal to z_min squared if no bundle), = sum (Z^2*x_z) where x_z is the relative concentration of a given charge state in the bundle, i.e. sum(x_z) = 1 over the bundle.

field.name: z_average_1d
field.documentation: Average charge profile of the charge state bundle (equal to z_min if no bundle), = sum (Z*x_z) where x_z is the relative concentration of a given charge state in the bundle, i.e. sum(x_z) = 1 over the bundle.

field.name: z_average_square_1d
field.documentation: Average square charge profile of the charge state bundle (equal to z_min squared if no bundle), = sum (Z^2*x_z) where x_z is the relative concentration of a given charge state in the bundle, i.e. sum(x_z) = 1 over the bundle.

field.name: ionization_potential
field.documentation: Cumulative and average ionization potential to reach a given bundle. Defined as sum (x_z* (sum of Epot from z'=0 to z-1)), where Epot is the ionization potential of ion Xz’+, and x_z is the relative concentration of a given charge state in the bundle, i.e. sum(x_z) = 1 over the bundle.

field.documentation: List of the fit specific parameters in XML format

field.name: pressure_ion_total
field.documentation: Total (sum over ion species) thermal ion pressure

field.name: j_total
field.documentation: Total parallel current density = average(jtot.B) / B0, where B0 = Core_Profiles/Vacuum_Toroidal_Field/ B0

field.name: current_parallel_inside
field.documentation: Parallel current driven inside the flux surface. Cumulative surface integral of j_total

field.name: j_phi
field.documentation: Total toroidal current density = average(J_phi/R) / average(1/R)

field.name: j_ohmic
field.documentation: Ohmic parallel current density = average(J_Ohmic.B) / B0, where B0 = Core_Profiles/Vacuum_Toroidal_Field/ B0

field.name: j_non_inductive
field.documentation: Non-inductive (includes bootstrap) parallel current density = average(jni.B) / B0, where B0 = Core_Profiles/Vacuum_Toroidal_Field/ B0

field.name: j_bootstrap
field.documentation: Bootstrap current density = average(J_Bootstrap.B) / B0, where B0 = Core_Profiles/Vacuum_Toroidal_Field/ B0

field.name: e_field
field.documentation: Electric field, averaged on the magnetic surface. E.g for the parallel component, average(E.B) / B0, using core_profiles/vacuum_toroidal_field/b0

field.name: phi_potential
field.documentation: Electrostatic potential, averaged on the magnetic flux surface

field.name: rotation_frequency_tor_sonic
field.documentation: Derivative of the flux surface averaged electrostatic potential with respect to the poloidal flux, multiplied by (1/2pi). This quantity is the toroidal angular rotation frequency due to the ExB drift, introduced in formula (43) of Hinton and Wong, Physics of Fluids 3082 (1985), also referred to as sonic flow in regimes in which the toroidal velocity is dominant over the poloidal velocity

field.name: q
field.documentation: Safety factor (only positive when toroidal current and magnetic field are in same direction)

field.name: magnetic_shear
field.documentation: Magnetic shear, defined as rho_tor/q . dq/drho_tor

field.name: profiles_2d
field.documentation: Core plasma quantities in a poloidal cross section, for various time slices

field.name: grid_type
field.documentation: Selection of one of a set of grid types

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: grid
field.documentation: Definition of the 2D grid (the content of dim1 and dim2 is defined by the selected grid_type)

field.name: volume_element
field.documentation: Elementary plasma volume of plasma enclosed in the cell formed by the nodes [dim1(i) dim2(j)], [dim1(i+1) dim2(j)], [dim1(i) dim2(j+1)] and [dim1(i+1) dim2(j+1)]

field.name: ion
field.documentation: 2D quantities related to the different ion species, in the sense of isonuclear or isomolecular sequences. Ionization states (or other types of states) must be differentiated at the state level below. This array doesn't necessarily have the same size as the profiles_1d/ion array, since 2D data may be relevant only for a subset of ion species.

field.documentation: List of elements forming the atom or molecule

field.name: atoms_n
field.documentation: Number of atoms of this element in the molecule

field.name: z_ion
field.documentation: Ion charge (of the dominant ionization state; lumped ions are allowed), volume averaged over plasma radius

field.name: name
field.documentation: String identifying ion (e.g. H, D, T, He, C, D2, ...)

field.name: ion_index
field.documentation: Index of the corresponding ion species in the ../../../profiles_1d/ion array

field.documentation: Density (thermal+non-thermal) (sum over charge states when multiple charge states are considered)

field.name: density_fast

field.documentation: Fast (non-thermal) perpendicular pressure (sum over charge states when multiple charge states are considered)

field.name: pressure_fast_parallel
field.documentation: Fast (non-thermal) parallel pressure (sum over charge states when multiple charge states are considered)

field.name: velocity
field.documentation: Velocity (average over charge states when multiple charge states are considered) at the position of maximum major radius on every flux surface

field.documentation: Minimum Z of the charge state bundle

field.name: z_max
field.documentation: Maximum Z of the charge state bundle (equal to z_min if no bundle)

field.documentation: Cumulative and average ionization potential to reach a given bundle. Defined as sum (x_z* (sum of Epot from z'=0 to z-1)), where Epot is the ionization potential of ion Xz’+, and x_z is the relative concentration of a given charge state in the bundle, i.e. sum(x_z) = 1 over the bundle.

field.name: electron_configuration

field.name: vibrational_mode
field.documentation: Vibrational mode of this state, e.g. "A_g". Need to define, or adopt a standard nomenclature.

field.name: rotation_frequency_tor
field.documentation: Toroidal rotation frequency (i.e. toroidal velocity divided by the major radius at which the toroidal velocity is taken)

field.name: t_i_average
field.documentation: Ion temperature (averaged on states and ion species)

field.name: n_i_total_over_n_e
field.documentation: Ratio of total ion density (sum over species and charge states) over electron density. (thermal+non-thermal)

field.name: n_i_thermal_total
field.documentation: Total ion thermal density (sum over species and charge states)

field.name: momentum_phi
field.documentation: Total plasma toroidal momentum, summed over ion species and electrons weighted by their density and major radius, i.e. sum_over_species(n*R*m*Vphi)

field.name: pressure_ion_total
field.documentation: Total (sum over ion species) thermal ion pressure

field.name: global_quantities
field.documentation: Various global quantities derived from the profiles

field.name: ip
field.documentation: Total plasma current (toroidal component). Positive sign means anti-clockwise when viewed from above.

field.name: current_non_inductive
field.documentation: Total non-inductive current (toroidal component). Positive sign means anti-clockwise when viewed from above.

field.name: current_bootstrap
field.documentation: Bootstrap current (toroidal component). Positive sign means anti-clockwise when viewed from above.

field.name: v_loop
field.documentation: LCFS loop voltage (positive value drives positive ohmic current that flows anti-clockwise when viewed from above)

field.name: li_3
field.documentation: Internal inductance. The li_3 definition is used, i.e. li_3 = 2/R0/mu0^2/Ip^2 * int(Bp^2 dV).

field.name: beta_tor
field.documentation: Toroidal beta, defined as the volume-averaged total perpendicular pressure divided by (B0^2/(2*mu0)), i.e. beta_toroidal = 2 mu0 int(p dV) / V / B0^2

field.name: beta_tor_norm
field.documentation: Normalized toroidal beta, defined as 100 * beta_tor * a[m] * B0 [T] / ip [MA]

field.name: beta_pol
field.documentation: Poloidal beta. Defined as betap = 4 int(p dV) / [R_0 * mu_0 * Ip^2]

field.name: energy_diamagnetic
field.documentation: Plasma energy content = 3/2 * integral over the plasma volume of the total perpendicular pressure

field.name: z_eff_resistive
field.documentation: Volume average plasma effective charge, estimated from the flux consumption in the ohmic phase

field.name: t_e_peaking
field.documentation: Electron temperature peaking factor, defined as the Te value at the magnetic axis divided by the volume averaged Te (average over the plasma volume up to the LCFS)

field.name: t_i_average_peaking
field.documentation: Ion temperature (averaged over ion species and states) peaking factor, defined as the Ti value at the magnetic axis divided by the volume averaged Ti (average over the plasma volume up to the LCFS)

field.name: resistive_psi_losses
field.documentation: Resistive part of the poloidal flux losses, defined as the volume-averaged scalar product of the electric field and the ohmic current density, normalized by the plasma current and integrated in time from the beginning of the plasma discharge: int ( (int(E_field_tor.j_ohm_tor) dV) / Ip ) dt)

field.name: ejima
field.documentation: Ejima coefficient : resistive psi losses divided by (mu0*R*Ip). See S. Ejima et al, Nuclear Fusion, Vol.22, No.10 (1982), 1313

field.name: t_e_volume_average
field.documentation: Volume averaged electron temperature (average over the plasma volume up to the LCFS)

field.name: n_e_volume_average
field.documentation: Volume averaged electron density (average over the plasma volume up to the LCFS)

field.name: ion
field.documentation: Quantities related to the different ion species, in the sense of isonuclear or isomolecular sequences. The set of ion species of this array must be the same as the one defined in profiles_1d/ion, at the time slice indicated in ion_time_slice

field.name: t_i_volume_average
field.documentation: Volume averaged temperature of this ion species (averaged over the plasma volume up to the LCFS)

field.name: n_i_volume_average
field.documentation: Volume averaged density of this ion species (averaged over the plasma volume up to the LCFS)

field.name: ion_time_slice
field.documentation: Time slice of the profiles_1d array used to define the ion composition of the global_quantities/ion array.

field.name: vacuum_toroidal_field
field.documentation: Characteristics of the vacuum toroidal field (used in rho_tor definition and in the normalization of current densities)

field.name: r0

IDS.name: core_transport
IDS.documentation: Core plasma transport of particles, energy, momentum and poloidal flux. The transport of particles, energy and momentum is described by diffusion coefficients, D, and convection velocities, v. These are defined by the total fluxes of particles, energy and momentum, across a flux surface given by : V' [-D Y' <|grad(rho_tor_norm)|^2> + v Y <|grad(rho_tor_norm)|>], where Y represents the particles, energy and momentum density, respectively, while V is the volume inside a flux surface, the primes denote derivatives with respect to rho_tor_norm and < X > is the flux surface average of a quantity X. This formulation remains valid when changing simultaneously rho_tor_norm into rho_tor in the gradient terms and in the derivatives denoted by the prime. The average flux stored in the IDS as sibling of D and v is the total flux described above divided by the flux surface area V' <|grad(rho_tor_norm)|>. Note that the energy flux includes the energy transported by the particle flux, in this form: Q = V' [- n D (T)' <|grad(rho_tor_norm)|^2> + v (nT) <|grad(rho_tor_norm)|>] + flux_multiplier * T * particle_flux

field.name: vacuum_toroidal_field
field.documentation: Characteristics of the vacuum toroidal field (used in Rho_Tor definition and in the normalization of current densities)

field.name: r0
field.documentation: Reference major radius where the vacuum toroidal magnetic field is given (usually a fixed position such as the middle of the vessel at the equatorial midplane)

field.name: b0
field.documentation: Vacuum toroidal field at R0 [T]; Positive sign means anti-clockwise when viewing from above. The product R0B0 must be consistent with the b_tor_vacuum_r field of the tf IDS.

field.name: model
field.documentation: Transport is described by a combination of various transport models

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: flux_multiplier
field.documentation: Multiplier applied to the particule flux when adding its contribution in the expression of the heat flux : can be 0, 3/2 or 5/2

field.name: profiles_1d
field.documentation: Transport coefficient profiles for various time slices. Fluxes and convection are positive (resp. negative) when outwards i.e. towards the LCFS (resp. inwards i.e. towards the magnetic axes).

field.name: grid_d
field.documentation: Grid for effective diffusivities and parallel conductivity

field.name: rho_tor_norm
field.documentation: Normalized toroidal flux coordinate. The normalizing value for rho_tor_norm, is the toroidal flux coordinate at the equilibrium boundary (LCFS or 99.x % of the LCFS in case of a fixed boundary equilibium calculation, see time_slice/boundary/b_flux_pol_norm in the equilibrium IDS)

field.name: rho_tor
field.documentation: Toroidal flux coordinate = sqrt(phi/(pi*b0)), where the toroidal magnetic field, b0, corresponds to that stored in vacuum_toroidal_field/b0 and pi can be found in the IMAS constants

field.name: psi
field.documentation: Poloidal magnetic flux. Integral of magnetic field passing through a contour defined by the intersection of a flux surface passing through the point of interest and a Z=constant plane. If the integration surface is flat, the surface normal vector is in the increasing vertical coordinate direction, Z, namely upwards.

field.name: volume
field.documentation: Volume enclosed inside the magnetic surface

field.name: area
field.documentation: Cross-sectional area of the flux surface

field.name: surface
field.documentation: Surface area of the toroidal flux surface

field.name: psi_magnetic_axis
field.documentation: Value of the poloidal magnetic flux at the magnetic axis (useful to normalize the psi array values when the radial grid doesn't go from the magnetic axis to the plasma boundary)

field.name: psi_boundary
field.documentation: Value of the poloidal magnetic flux at the plasma boundary (useful to normalize the psi array values when the radial grid doesn't go from the magnetic axis to the plasma boundary)

field.name: rho_tor_norm

field.name: cryostat
field.documentation: Mechanical structure of the cryostat. It is described as a set of nested layers with given physics properties; Two representations are admitted for each vessel unit : annular (two contours) or block elements.

field.name: type
field.documentation: Type of the description. index = 0 for the official single/multiple annular representation and 1 for the official block element representation for each unit. Additional representations needed on a code-by-code basis follow same incremental pair tagging starting on index=2

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: name
field.documentation: Short string identifier (unique for a given device)

field.name: description
field.documentation: Description, e.g. “channel viewing the upper divertor”

field.name: annular
field.documentation: Annular representation of a layer by two contours, inner and outer. Alternatively, the layer can be described by a centreline and thickness.

field.name: outline_inner
field.documentation: Inner vessel outline. Repeat the first point in case of a closed contour

field.name: outline_outer
field.documentation: Outer vessel outline. Repeat the first point in case of a closed contour

field.name: centreline
field.documentation: Centreline, i.e. middle of the vessel layer as a series of point. Repeat the first point in case of a closed contour

field.name: thickness
field.documentation: Thickness of the vessel layer in the perpendicular direction to the centreline. Thickness(i) is the thickness of the layer between centreline/r(i),z(i) and centreline/r(i+1),z(i+1), so its size is equal to the length of centreline/r-1 if the thickness is varying. If the thickness is constant for all points, allocate this node to size 1 to store a single value.

field.name: outline
field.documentation: Outline of the block element. Repeat the first point in case of a closed contour

field.name: j_phi
field.documentation: Toroidal current induced in this block element

field.name: power_ohm_halo
field.documentation: Ohmic power in the halo region

field.name: power_parallel_halo
field.documentation: Power of the parallel heat flux in the halo region

field.name: power_radiated_electrons_impurities
field.documentation: Total power radiated by electrons on impurities

field.name: power_radiated_electrons_impurities_halo
field.documentation: Power radiated by electrons on impurities in the halo region

field.name: energy_ohm
field.documentation: Total ohmic cumulated energy (integral of the power over the disruption duration)

field.name: energy_ohm_halo
field.documentation: Ohmic cumulated energy (integral of the power over the disruption duration) in the halo region

field.name: energy_parallel_halo
field.documentation: Cumulated parallel energy (integral of the heat flux parallel power over the disruption duration) in the halo region

field.name: energy_radiated_electrons_impurities
field.documentation: Total cumulated energy (integral of the power over the disruption duration) radiated by electrons on impurities

field.name: energy_radiated_electrons_impurities_halo
field.documentation: Cumulated energy (integral of the power over the disruption duration) radiated by electrons on impurities in the halo region

field.name: psi_halo_boundary
field.documentation: Poloidal flux at halo region boundary

field.name: phi_halo_boundary
field.documentation: Toroidal flux at halo region boundary

field.name: phi_halo_boundary_poloidal_current
field.documentation: Toroidal flux at halo region boundary generated by the plasma poloidal current

field.name: halo_currents
field.documentation: Halo currents geometry and values for a set of time slices

field.name: area
field.documentation: Set of wall areas through which there are halo currents

field.name: start_point
field.documentation: Position of the start point of this area

field.name: end_point
field.documentation: Position of the end point of this area

field.name: current_halo_pol
field.documentation: Poloidal halo current crossing through this area

field.name: active_wall_point
field.documentation: R,Z position of the point of the plasma boundary in contact with the wall

field.name: profiles_1d
field.documentation: Radial profiles for a set of time slices

field.name: rho_tor_norm
field.documentation: Normalized toroidal flux coordinate. The normalizing value for rho_tor_norm, is the toroidal flux coordinate at the equilibrium boundary (LCFS or 99.x % of the LCFS in case of a fixed boundary equilibium calculation, see time_slice/boundary/b_flux_pol_norm in the equilibrium IDS)

field.name: rho_tor
field.documentation: Toroidal flux coordinate = sqrt(phi/(pi*b0)), where the toroidal magnetic field, b0, corresponds to that stored in vacuum_toroidal_field/b0 and pi can be found in the IMAS constants

field.name: psi
field.documentation: Poloidal magnetic flux. Integral of magnetic field passing through a contour defined by the intersection of a flux surface passing through the point of interest and a Z=constant plane. If the integration surface is flat, the surface normal vector is in the increasing vertical coordinate direction, Z, namely upwards.

field.name: volume
field.documentation: Volume enclosed inside the magnetic surface

field.name: area
field.documentation: Cross-sectional area of the flux surface

field.name: surface
field.documentation: Surface area of the toroidal flux surface

field.name: psi_magnetic_axis
field.documentation: Value of the poloidal magnetic flux at the magnetic axis (useful to normalize the psi array values when the radial grid doesn't go from the magnetic axis to the plasma boundary)

field.name: psi_boundary
field.documentation: Value of the poloidal magnetic flux at the plasma boundary (useful to normalize the psi array values when the radial grid doesn't go from the magnetic axis to the plasma boundary)

field.name: j_runaways
field.documentation: Runaways parallel current density = average(j.B) / B0, where B0 = Disruption/Vacuum_Toroidal_Field/ B0

field.name: power_density_conductive_losses
field.documentation: Power density of conductive losses to the wall (positive sign for losses)

field.name: power_density_radiative_losses
field.documentation: Power density of radiative losses (positive sign for losses)

field.name: vacuum_toroidal_field
field.documentation: Characteristics of the vacuum toroidal field (used in rho_tor definition and in the normalization of current densities)

field.name: r0
field.documentation: Reference major radius where the vacuum toroidal magnetic field is given (usually a fixed position such as the middle of the vessel at the equatorial midplane)

field.name: b0
field.documentation: Vacuum toroidal field at R0 [T]; Positive sign means anti-clockwise when viewing from above. The product R0B0 must be consistent with the b_tor_vacuum_r field of the tf IDS.

field.documentation: Generic decription of the code-specific parameters for the code that has produced this IDS

field.name: output_flag
field.documentation: Output flag : 0 means the run is successful, other values mean some difficulty has been encountered, the exact meaning is then code specific. Negative values mean the result shall not be used.

field.name: source
field.documentation: Set of source/sink terms. A source/sink term corresponds to the particle source due to an NBI injection unit, a nuclear reaction or any combination of them (described in "identifier")

field.name: process
field.documentation: Set of processes (NBI units, fusion reactions, ...) that provide the source.

field.name: type
field.documentation: Process type. index=1 for NBI; index=2 for nuclear reaction (reaction unspecified); index=3 for nuclear reaction: T(d,n)4He [D+T->He4+n]; index=4 for nuclear reaction: He3(d,p)4He [He3+D->He4+p]; index=5 for nuclear reaction: D(d,p)T [D+D->T+p]; index=6 for nuclear reaction: D(d,n)3He [D+D->He3+n]; index=7 for runaway processes

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: reactant_energy
field.documentation: For nuclear reaction source, energy of the reactants. index = 0 for a sum over all energies; index = 1 for thermal-thermal; index = 2 for beam-beam; index = 3 for beam-thermal

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: nbi_energy
field.documentation: For NBI source, energy of the accelerated species considered. index = 0 for a sum over all energies; index = 1 for full energiy; index = 2 for half energy; index = 3 for third energy

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: nbi_unit
field.documentation: Index of the NBI unit considered. Refers to the "unit" array of the NBI IDS. 0 means sum over all NBI units.

field.name: nbi_beamlets_group
field.documentation: Index of the NBI beamlets group considered. Refers to the "unit/beamlets_group" array of the NBI IDS. 0 means sum over all beamlets groups.

field.name: gyro_type
field.documentation: Defines how to interpret the spatial coordinates: 1 = given at the actual particle birth point; 2 =given at the gyro centre of the birth point

field.name: species
field.documentation: Species injected or consumed by this source/sink

field.name: type
field.documentation: Species type. index=1 for electron; index=2 for ion species in a single/average state (refer to ion structure); index=3 for ion species in a particular state (refer to ion/state structure); index=4 for neutral species in a single/average state (refer to neutral structure); index=5 for neutral species in a particular state (refer to neutral/state structure); index=6 for neutron; index=7 for photon

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: ion
field.documentation: Description of the ion or neutral species, used if type/index = 2 or 3

field.name: element
field.documentation: List of elements forming the atom or molecule

field.name: atoms_n
field.documentation: Number of atoms of this element in the molecule

field.name: z_ion
field.documentation: Ion charge (of the dominant ionization state; lumped ions are allowed)

field.name: name
field.documentation: String identifying ion (e.g. H+, D+, T+, He+2, C+, ...)

field.name: state
field.documentation: Quantities related to the different states of the species (ionization, energy, excitation, ...)

field.name: z_min
field.documentation: Minimum Z of the charge state bundle (z_min = z_max = 0 for a neutral)

field.name: z_max
field.documentation: Maximum Z of the charge state bundle (equal to z_min if no bundle)

field.name: name
field.documentation: String identifying ion state (e.g. C+, C+2 , C+3, C+4, C+5, C+6, ...)

field.name: electron_configuration
field.documentation: Configuration of atomic orbitals of this state, e.g. 1s2-2s1

field.name: vibrational_mode
field.documentation: Vibrational mode of this state, e.g. "A_g". Need to define, or adopt a standard nomenclature.

field.name: neutral
field.documentation: Description of the neutral species, used if type/index = 4 or 5

field.name: element
field.documentation: List of elements forming the atom or molecule

field.name: atoms_n
field.documentation: Number of atoms of this element in the molecule

field.name: name
field.documentation: String identifying neutral (e.g. H, D, T, He, C, ...)

field.name: electron_configuration
field.documentation: Configuration of atomic orbitals of this state, e.g. 1s2-2s1

field.name: vibrational_mode
field.documentation: Vibrational mode of this state, e.g. "A_g". Need to define, or adopt a standard nomenclature.

field.name: neutral_type
field.documentation: Neutral type, in terms of energy. ID =1: cold; 2: thermal; 3: fast; 4: NBI

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: global_quantities
field.documentation: Global quantities for various time slices

field.name: torque_phi
field.documentation: Total toroidal torque of the source

field.name: torque_phi
field.documentation: Toroidal torque losses due to shinethrough

field.name: profiles_1d
field.documentation: Source radial profiles (flux surface averaged quantities) for various time slices

field.name: rho_tor_norm
field.documentation: Normalized toroidal flux coordinate. The normalizing value for rho_tor_norm, is the toroidal flux coordinate at the equilibrium boundary (LCFS or 99.x % of the LCFS in case of a fixed boundary equilibium calculation, see time_slice/boundary/b_flux_pol_norm in the equilibrium IDS)

field.name: rho_tor
field.documentation: Toroidal flux coordinate = sqrt(phi/(pi*b0)), where the toroidal magnetic field, b0, corresponds to that stored in vacuum_toroidal_field/b0 and pi can be found in the IMAS constants

field.name: psi
field.documentation: Poloidal magnetic flux. Integral of magnetic field passing through a contour defined by the intersection of a flux surface passing through the point of interest and a Z=constant plane. If the integration surface is flat, the surface normal vector is in the increasing vertical coordinate direction, Z, namely upwards.

field.name: volume
field.documentation: Volume enclosed inside the magnetic surface

field.name: area
field.documentation: Cross-sectional area of the flux surface

field.name: surface
field.documentation: Surface area of the toroidal flux surface

field.name: psi_magnetic_axis
field.documentation: Value of the poloidal magnetic flux at the magnetic axis (useful to normalize the psi array values when the radial grid doesn't go from the magnetic axis to the plasma boundary)

field.name: psi_boundary
field.documentation: Value of the poloidal magnetic flux at the plasma boundary (useful to normalize the psi array values when the radial grid doesn't go from the magnetic axis to the plasma boundary)

field.name: energy
field.documentation: Source term for the energy transport equation

field.name: momentum_phi
field.documentation: Source term for the toroidal momentum equation

field.name: particles
field.documentation: Source term for the density transport equation

field.name: ggd
field.documentation: Source terms in phase space (real space, velocity space, spin state), represented using the ggd, for various time slices

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: path
field.documentation: Path of the grid, including the IDS name, in case of implicit reference to a grid_ggd node described in another IDS. To be filled only if the grid is not described explicitly in this grid_ggd structure. Example syntax: #wall:2/description_ggd(1)/grid_ggd, means that the grid is located in the wall IDS, occurrence 2, with relative path description_ggd(1)/grid_ggd, using Fortran index convention (here : first index of the array)

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: geometry_type
field.documentation: Type of space geometry (0: standard, 1:Fourier, >1: Fourier with periodicity)

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: coordinates_type
field.documentation: Type of coordinates describing the physical space, for every coordinate of the space. The size of this node therefore defines the dimension of the space.

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: objects_per_dimension
field.documentation: Definition of the space objects for every dimension (from one to the dimension of the highest-dimensional objects). The index correspond to 1=nodes, 2=edges, 3=faces, 4=cells/volumes, .... For every index, a collection of objects of that dimension is described.

field.name: object
field.documentation: Set of objects for a given dimension

field.name: boundary
field.documentation: Set of (n-1)-dimensional objects defining the boundary of this n-dimensional object

field.name: neighbours
field.documentation: List of indices of the n-dimensional objects adjacent to the given n-dimensional object. An object can possibly have multiple neighbours on a boundary

field.name: geometry
field.documentation: Geometry data associated with the object, its detailed content is defined by ../../geometry_content. Its dimension depends on the type of object, geometry and coordinate considered.

field.name: nodes
field.documentation: List of nodes forming this object (indices to objects_per_dimension(1)%object(:) in Fortran notation)

field.name: measure
field.documentation: Measure of the space object, i.e. physical size (length for 1d, area for 2d, volume for 3d objects,...)

field.name: geometry_2d
field.documentation: 2D geometry data associated with the object. Its dimension depends on the type of object, geometry and coordinate considered. Typically, the first dimension represents the object coordinates, while the second dimension would represent the values of the various degrees of freedom of the finite element attached to the object.

field.name: geometry_content
field.documentation: Content of the ../object/geometry node for this dimension

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: dimension
field.documentation: Space dimension of the grid subset elements, using the convention 1=nodes, 2=edges, 3=faces, 4=cells/volumes

field.name: element
field.documentation: Set of elements defining the grid subset. An element is defined by a combination of objects from potentially all spaces

field.name: object
field.documentation: Set of objects defining the element

field.name: space
field.documentation: Index of the space from which that object is taken

field.name: dimension
field.documentation: Dimension of the object - using the convention 1=nodes, 2=edges, 3=faces, 4=cells/volumes

field.name: base
field.documentation: Set of bases for the grid subset. For each base, the structure describes the projection of the base vectors on the canonical frame of the grid.

field.name: tensor_covariant
field.documentation: Covariant metric tensor, given on each element of the subgrid (first dimension)

field.name: tensor_contravariant
field.documentation: Contravariant metric tensor, given on each element of the subgrid (first dimension)

field.name: metric
field.documentation: Metric of the canonical frame onto Cartesian coordinates

field.name: tensor_covariant
field.documentation: Covariant metric tensor, given on each element of the subgrid (first dimension)

field.name: tensor_contravariant
field.documentation: Contravariant metric tensor, given on each element of the subgrid (first dimension)

field.name: particles
field.documentation: Source density of particles in phase space, for various grid subsets

field.name: grid_index
field.documentation: Index of the grid used to represent this quantity

field.name: grid_subset_index
field.documentation: Index of the grid subset the data is provided on. Corresponds to the index used in the grid subset definition: grid_subset(:)/identifier/index

field.name: values
field.documentation: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.

field.name: coefficients
field.documentation: Interpolation coefficients, to be used for a high precision evaluation of the physical quantity with finite elements, provided per element in the grid subset (first dimension).

field.name: discrete
field.documentation: List of indices of grid spaces (refers to ../grid/space) for which the source is discretely distributed. For example consider a source of 3.5 MeV alpha particles provided on a grid with two coordinates (spaces); rho_tor and energy. To specify that the source is given at energies exactly equal to 3.5 MeV, let discret have length 1 and set discrete(1)=2 since energy is dimension number 2. The source is then proportional to delta( 1 - energy / 3.5MeV ), where delta is the direct delta distribution. Discrete dimensions can only be used when the grid is rectangular.

field.name: markers
field.documentation: Source given as a group of markers (test particles) born per second, for various time slices

field.name: coordinate_identifier
field.documentation: Set of coordinate identifiers, coordinates on which the markers are represented

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: weights
field.documentation: Weight of the markers, i.e. number of real particles represented by each marker. The dimension of the vector correspond to the number of markers

field.name: positions
field.documentation: Position of the markers in the set of coordinates. The first dimension corresponds to the number of markers, the second dimension to the set of coordinates

field.name: orbit_integrals
field.documentation: Integrals along the markers orbit. These dimensionless expressions are of the form: (1/tau) integral (f(n_tor,m_pol,k,eq,...) dt) from time - tau to time, where tau is the transit/trapping time of the marker and f() a dimensionless function (phase factor,drift,etc) of the equilibrium (e.g. q) and perturbation (Fourier harmonics n_tor,m_pol and bounce harmonic k) along the particles orbits. In fact the integrals are taken during the last orbit of each marker at the time value of the time node below

field.name: expressions
field.documentation: List of the expressions f(n_tor,m_pol,k,q,...) used in the orbit integrals

field.name: n_phi
field.documentation: Array of toroidal mode numbers, where quantities vary as exp(i.n_phi.phi) and phi runs anticlockwise when viewed from above

field.name: m_pol
field.documentation: Array of poloidal mode numbers, where quantities vary as exp(-i.m_pol.theta) and theta is the angle defined by the choice of ../../coordinate_identifier, with its centre at the magnetic axis recalled at the root of this IDS

field.name: orbit_integrals_instant
field.documentation: Integrals/quantities along the markers orbit. These dimensionless expressions are of the form: (1/tau) integral ( f(eq) dt) from time - tau to time_orbit for different values of time_orbit in the interval from time - tau to time, where tau is the transit/trapping time of the marker and f(eq) a dimensionless function (phase, drift,q,etc) of the equilibrium along the markers orbits. The integrals are taken during the last orbit of each marker at the time value of the time node below

field.name: expressions
field.documentation: List of the expressions f(eq) used in the orbit integrals

field.name: time_orbit
field.documentation: Time array along the markers last orbit

field.name: toroidal_mode
field.documentation: In case the orbit integrals are calculated for a given MHD perturbation, index of the toroidal mode considered. Refers to the time_slice/toroidal_mode array of the MHD_LINEAR IDS in which this perturbation is described

field.name: vacuum_toroidal_field
field.documentation: Characteristics of the vacuum toroidal field (used in rho_tor definition)

field.name: r0
field.documentation: Reference major radius where the vacuum toroidal magnetic field is given (usually a fixed position such as the middle of the vessel at the equatorial midplane)

field.name: b0
field.documentation: Vacuum toroidal field at R0 [T]; Positive sign means anti-clockwise when viewing from above. The product R0B0 must be consistent with the b_tor_vacuum_r field of the tf IDS.

field.name: magnetic_axis
field.documentation: Magnetic axis position (used to define a poloidal angle for the 2D profiles)

field.name: code
field.documentation: Generic decription of the code-specific parameters for the code that has produced this IDS

field.name: description
field.documentation: Short description of the software (type, purpose)

field.name: parameters
field.documentation: List of the code specific parameters in XML format

field.name: output_flag
field.documentation: Output flag : 0 means the run is successful, other values mean some difficulty has been encountered, the exact meaning is then code specific. Negative values mean the result shall not be used.

field.name: library
field.documentation: List of external libraries used by the code that has produced this IDS

field.name: description
field.documentation: Short description of the software (type, purpose)

field.name: parameters
field.documentation: List of the code specific parameters in XML format

IDS.name: distributions
IDS.documentation: Distribution function(s) of one or many particle species. This structure is specifically designed to handle non-Maxwellian distribution function generated during heating and current drive, typically solved using a Fokker-Planck calculation perturbed by a heating scheme (e.g. IC, EC, LH, NBI, or alpha heating) and then relaxed by Coloumb collisions.

field.name: ids_properties
field.documentation: Interface Data Structure properties. This element identifies the node above as an IDS

field.name: comment
field.documentation: Any comment describing the content of this IDS

field.name: name
field.documentation: User-defined name for this IDS occurrence

field.name: homogeneous_time
field.documentation: This node must be filled (with 0, 1, or 2) for the IDS to be valid. If 1, the time of this IDS is homogeneous, i.e. the time values for this IDS are stored in the time node just below the root of this IDS. If 0, the time values are stored in the various time fields at lower levels in the tree. In the case only constant or static nodes are filled within the IDS, homogeneous_time must be set to 2

field.name: occurrence_type
field.documentation: Type of data contained in this occurrence

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: provider
field.documentation: Name of the person in charge of producing this data

field.name: creation_date
field.documentation: Date at which this data has been produced

field.name: version_put
field.documentation: Version of the access layer package used to PUT this IDS

field.name: data_dictionary
field.documentation: Version of Data Dictionary used to PUT this IDS

field.name: access_layer
field.documentation: Version of Access Layer used to PUT this IDS

field.name: access_layer_language
field.documentation: Programming language of the Access Layer high level API used to PUT this IDS

field.name: node
field.documentation: Set of IDS nodes for which the provenance is given. The provenance information applies to the whole structure below the IDS node. For documenting provenance information for the whole IDS, set the size of this array of structure to 1 and leave the child "path" node empty

field.name: path
field.documentation: Path of the node within the IDS, following the syntax given in the link below. If empty, means the provenance information applies to the whole IDS.

field.name: reference
field.documentation: List of references used to populate or calculate this node, identified as explained below. In case the node is the result of of a calculation / data processing, the reference is an input to the process described in the "code" structure at the root of the IDS. The reference can be an IDS (identified by a URI or a persitent identifier, see syntax in the link below) or non-IDS data imported directly from an non-IMAS database (identified by the command used to import the reference, or the persistent identifier of the data reference). Often data are obtained by a chain of processes, however only the last process input are recorded here. The full chain of provenance has then to be reconstructed recursively from the provenance information contained in the data references.

field.name: timestamp
field.documentation: Date and time (UTC) at which the reference was created, expressed in a human readable form (ISO 8601) : the format of the string shall be : YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ. Example : 2020-07-24T14:19:00Z

field.name: plugins
field.documentation: Information about the plugins used to write/read this IDS. This structure is filled automatically by the Access Layer at GET/PUT time, no need to fill it via a user program.

field.name: node
field.documentation: Set of IDS nodes for which a plugin has been applied

field.name: path
field.documentation: Path of the node within the IDS, following the syntax given in the link below. If empty, means the plugin applies to the whole IDS.

field.name: put_operation
field.documentation: Plugins used to PUT a node (potentially, multiple plugins can be applied, if so they are listed by order of application)

field.documentation: List of external libraries used by the code that has produced this IDS

field.name: parameters
field.documentation: List of the code specific parameters in XML format

field.name: readback
field.documentation: Plugins to be used to read back a node (potentially, multiple plugins can be applied, listed in reverse order of application)

field.documentation: Short description of the software (type, purpose)

field.name: parameters
field.documentation: List of the code specific parameters in XML format

field.name: library
field.documentation: List of external libraries used by the code that has produced this IDS

field.name: description

field.name: get_operation
field.documentation: Plugins actually used to read back a node (potentially, multiple plugins can be applied, listed in reverse order of application). This information is filled by the plugin infrastructure during the GET operation.

field.documentation: Plugin infrastructure used to GET the data
