field.documentation: Short description of the software (type, purpose)

field.name: distribution
field.documentation: Set of distribution functions. Every distribution function has to be associated with only one particle species, specified in distri_vec/species/, but there could be multiple distribution function for each species. In this case, the fast particle populations should be superposed

field.name: wave
field.documentation: List all waves affecting the distribution, identified as in waves/coherent_wave(i)/identifier in the waves IDS

field.name: type
field.documentation: Wave/antenna type. index=1 for name=EC; index=2 for name=IC; index=3 for name=LH

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: antenna_name
field.documentation: Name of the antenna that launches this wave. Corresponds to the name specified in antennas/ec(i)/name, or antennas/ic(i)/name or antennas/lh(i)/name (depends of antenna/wave type) in the ANTENNAS IDS.

field.name: index_in_antenna
field.documentation: Index of the wave (starts at 1), separating different waves generated from a single antenna.

field.name: process
field.documentation: List all processes (NBI units, fusion reactions, ...) affecting the distribution, identified as in distribution_sources/source(i)/process in the DISTRIBUTION_SOURCES IDS

field.name: type
field.documentation: Process type. index=1 for NBI; index=2 for nuclear reaction (reaction unspecified); index=3 for nuclear reaction: T(d,n)4He [D+T->He4+n]; index=4 for nuclear reaction: He3(d,p)4He [He3+D->He4+p]; index=5 for nuclear reaction: D(d,p)T [D+D->T+p]; index=6 for nuclear reaction: D(d,n)3He [D+D->He3+n]; index=7 for runaway processes

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: reactant_energy
field.documentation: For nuclear reaction source, energy of the reactants. index = 0 for a sum over all energies; index = 1 for thermal-thermal; index = 2 for beam-beam; index = 3 for beam-thermal

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: nbi_energy
field.documentation: For NBI source, energy of the accelerated species considered. index = 0 for a sum over all energies; index = 1 for full energiy; index = 2 for half energy; index = 3 for third energy

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: nbi_unit
field.documentation: Index of the NBI unit considered. Refers to the "unit" array of the NBI IDS. 0 means sum over all NBI units.

field.name: nbi_beamlets_group
field.documentation: Index of the NBI beamlets group considered. Refers to the "unit/beamlets_group" array of the NBI IDS. 0 means sum over all beamlets groups.

field.name: gyro_type
field.documentation: Defines how to interpret the spatial coordinates: 1 = given at the actual particle birth point; 2 =given at the gyro centre of the birth point

field.name: type
field.documentation: Species type. index=1 for electron; index=2 for ion species in a single/average state (refer to ion structure); index=3 for ion species in a particular state (refer to ion/state structure); index=4 for neutral species in a single/average state (refer to neutral structure); index=5 for neutral species in a particular state (refer to neutral/state structure); index=6 for neutron; index=7 for photon

field.name: index

field.documentation: Minimum Z of the charge state bundle (z_min = z_max = 0 for a neutral)

field.name: z_max
field.documentation: Maximum Z of the charge state bundle (equal to z_min if no bundle)

field.name: name
field.documentation: String identifying ion state (e.g. C+, C+2 , C+3, C+4, C+5, C+6, ...)

field.name: electron_configuration
field.documentation: Configuration of atomic orbitals of this state, e.g. 1s2-2s1

field.name: vibrational_mode
field.documentation: Vibrational mode of this state, e.g. "A_g". Need to define, or adopt a standard nomenclature.

field.name: neutral

field.name: element
field.documentation: List of elements forming the atom or molecule

field.name: atoms_n

field.name: electron_configuration
field.documentation: Configuration of atomic orbitals of this state, e.g. 1s2-2s1

field.name: vibrational_mode
field.documentation: Vibrational mode of this state, e.g. "A_g". Need to define, or adopt a standard nomenclature.

field.name: neutral_type
field.documentation: Neutral type, in terms of energy. ID =1: cold; 2: thermal; 3: fast; 4: NBI

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: global_quantities
field.documentation: Global quantities (integrated over plasma volume for moments of the distribution, collisional exchange and source terms), for various time slices

field.name: particles_n
field.documentation: Number of particles in the distribution, i.e. the volume integral of the density (note: this is the number of real particles and not markers)

field.name: particles_fast_n
field.documentation: Number of fast particles in the distribution, i.e. the volume integral of the density (note: this is the number of real particles and not markers)

field.name: energy_fast
field.documentation: Total energy of the fast particles in the distribution

field.name: energy_fast_parallel
field.documentation: Parallel energy of the fast particles in the distribution

field.name: torque_tor_j_radial
field.documentation: Toroidal torque due to radial currents

field.name: current_phi
field.documentation: Toroidal current driven by the distribution

field.name: power_first_orbit
field.documentation: Power loss due to first orbit losses

field.name: power_rotation
field.documentation: Power going to plasma rotation. This power goes into sustaining the plasma rotation rather than heating the plasma. This is given because the injection energy in the rotating plasma frame is (assuming rotation in the same direction of the NB injection) lower than in the lab-frame.

field.name: power_charge_exchange

field.name: collisions
field.documentation: Power and torque exchanged between the species described by the distribution and the different plasma species through collisions

field.name: power_thermal
field.documentation: Collisional power to the thermal particle population

field.name: power_fast

field.documentation: Multiple state calculation flag : 0-Only one state is considered; 1-Multiple states are considered and are described in the state structure

field.name: state
field.documentation: Collisional exchange with the various states of the ion species (ionization, energy, excitation, ...)

field.name: z_min
field.documentation: Minimum Z of the charge state bundle (z_min = z_max = 0 for a neutral)

field.name: z_max
field.documentation: Maximum Z of the charge state bundle (equal to z_min if no bundle)

field.name: name
field.documentation: String identifying charge state (e.g. C+, C+2 , C+3, C+4, C+5, C+6, ...)

field.name: electron_configuration
field.documentation: Configuration of atomic orbitals of this state, e.g. 1s2-2s1

field.name: vibrational_mode
field.documentation: Vibrational mode of this state, e.g. "A_g". Need to define, or adopt a standard nomenclature.

field.name: power_thermal
field.documentation: Collisional power to the thermal particle population

field.name: power_fast
field.documentation: Collisional power to the fast particle population

field.name: torque_thermal_phi
field.documentation: Collisional toroidal torque to the thermal particle population

field.name: torque_fast_phi
field.documentation: Collisional toroidal torque to the fast particle population

field.name: thermalization
field.documentation: Volume integrated source of thermal particles, momentum and energy due to thermalization. Here thermalization refers to non-thermal particles, sufficiently assimilated to the thermal background to be re-categorized as thermal particles. Note that this source may also be negative if thermal particles are being accelerated such that they form a distinct non-thermal contribution, e.g. due run-away of RF interactions.

field.name: particles
field.documentation: Source rate of thermal particles due to the thermalization of fast particles

field.name: power
field.documentation: Power input to the thermal particle population due to the thermalization of fast particles

field.name: torque
field.documentation: Torque input to the thermal particle population due to the thermalization of fast particles

field.name: source
field.documentation: Set of volume integrated sources and sinks of particles, momentum and energy included in the Fokker-Planck modelling, related to the various waves or particle source processes affecting the distribution

field.name: identifier
field.documentation: Identifier of the wave or particle source process, defined respectively in distribution/wave or distribution/process

field.name: type
field.documentation: Type of the source term. Index = 1 for a wave, index = 2 for a particle source process

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: torque_phi
field.documentation: Total toroidal torque of the source

field.name: profiles_1d
field.documentation: Radial profiles (flux surface averaged quantities) for various time slices

field.name: rho_tor_norm
field.documentation: Normalized toroidal flux coordinate. The normalizing value for rho_tor_norm, is the toroidal flux coordinate at the equilibrium boundary (LCFS or 99.x % of the LCFS in case of a fixed boundary equilibium calculation, see time_slice/boundary/b_flux_pol_norm in the equilibrium IDS)

field.name: rho_tor
field.documentation: Toroidal flux coordinate = sqrt(phi/(pi*b0)), where the toroidal magnetic field, b0, corresponds to that stored in vacuum_toroidal_field/b0 and pi can be found in the IMAS constants

field.name: psi
field.documentation: Poloidal magnetic flux. Integral of magnetic field passing through a contour defined by the intersection of a flux surface passing through the point of interest and a Z=constant plane. If the integration surface is flat, the surface normal vector is in the increasing vertical coordinate direction, Z, namely upwards.

field.name: volume
field.documentation: Volume enclosed inside the magnetic surface

field.name: area
field.documentation: Cross-sectional area of the flux surface

field.name: surface
field.documentation: Surface area of the toroidal flux surface

field.name: psi_magnetic_axis
field.documentation: Value of the poloidal magnetic flux at the magnetic axis (useful to normalize the psi array values when the radial grid doesn't go from the magnetic axis to the plasma boundary)

field.name: psi_boundary
field.documentation: Value of the poloidal magnetic flux at the plasma boundary (useful to normalize the psi array values when the radial grid doesn't go from the magnetic axis to the plasma boundary)

field.name: fast_filter
field.documentation: Description of how the fast and the thermal particle populations are separated

field.name: method
field.documentation: Method used to separate the fast and thermal particle population (indices TBD)

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: energy
field.documentation: Energy at which the fast and thermal particle populations were separated, as a function of radius

field.name: pressure_fast_parallel
field.documentation: Pressure of fast particles in the parallel direction

field.name: pressure_fast_perpendicular
field.documentation: Pressure of fast particles in the perpendicular direction

field.name: current_phi
field.documentation: Total toroidal driven current density (including electron and thermal ion back-current, or drag-current)

field.name: current_fast_phi
field.documentation: Total toroidal driven current density of fast (non-thermal) particles (excluding electron and thermal ion back-current, or drag-current)

field.name: torque_phi_j_radial
field.documentation: Toroidal torque due to radial currents

field.name: collisions
field.documentation: Power and torque exchanged between the species described by the distribution and the different plasma species through collisions

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: path
field.documentation: Path of the grid, including the IDS name, in case of implicit reference to a grid_ggd node described in another IDS. To be filled only if the grid is not described explicitly in this grid_ggd structure. Example syntax: #wall:2/description_ggd(1)/grid_ggd, means that the grid is located in the wall IDS, occurrence 2, with relative path description_ggd(1)/grid_ggd, using Fortran index convention (here : first index of the array)

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: geometry_type
field.documentation: Type of space geometry (0: standard, 1:Fourier, >1: Fourier with periodicity)

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: coordinates_type
field.documentation: Type of coordinates describing the physical space, for every coordinate of the space. The size of this node therefore defines the dimension of the space.

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: objects_per_dimension
field.documentation: Definition of the space objects for every dimension (from one to the dimension of the highest-dimensional objects). The index correspond to 1=nodes, 2=edges, 3=faces, 4=cells/volumes, .... For every index, a collection of objects of that dimension is described.

field.name: object
field.documentation: Set of objects for a given dimension

field.name: boundary
field.documentation: Set of (n-1)-dimensional objects defining the boundary of this n-dimensional object

field.name: neighbours
field.documentation: List of indices of the n-dimensional objects adjacent to the given n-dimensional object. An object can possibly have multiple neighbours on a boundary

field.name: geometry
field.documentation: Geometry data associated with the object, its detailed content is defined by ../../geometry_content. Its dimension depends on the type of object, geometry and coordinate considered.

field.name: nodes
field.documentation: List of nodes forming this object (indices to objects_per_dimension(1)%object(:) in Fortran notation)

field.name: measure
field.documentation: Measure of the space object, i.e. physical size (length for 1d, area for 2d, volume for 3d objects,...)

field.name: geometry_2d
field.documentation: 2D geometry data associated with the object. Its dimension depends on the type of object, geometry and coordinate considered. Typically, the first dimension represents the object coordinates, while the second dimension would represent the values of the various degrees of freedom of the finite element attached to the object.

field.name: geometry_content
field.documentation: Content of the ../object/geometry node for this dimension

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: dimension
field.documentation: Space dimension of the grid subset elements, using the convention 1=nodes, 2=edges, 3=faces, 4=cells/volumes

field.name: element
field.documentation: Set of elements defining the grid subset. An element is defined by a combination of objects from potentially all spaces

field.name: object
field.documentation: Set of objects defining the element

field.name: space
field.documentation: Index of the space from which that object is taken

field.name: dimension
field.documentation: Dimension of the object - using the convention 1=nodes, 2=edges, 3=faces, 4=cells/volumes

field.name: base
field.documentation: Set of bases for the grid subset. For each base, the structure describes the projection of the base vectors on the canonical frame of the grid.

field.name: tensor_covariant
field.documentation: Covariant metric tensor, given on each element of the subgrid (first dimension)

field.name: tensor_contravariant
field.documentation: Contravariant metric tensor, given on each element of the subgrid (first dimension)

field.name: metric
field.documentation: Metric of the canonical frame onto Cartesian coordinates

field.name: tensor_covariant
field.documentation: Covariant metric tensor, given on each element of the subgrid (first dimension)

field.name: tensor_contravariant
field.documentation: Contravariant metric tensor, given on each element of the subgrid (first dimension)

field.name: temperature
field.documentation: Reference temperature profile used to define the local thermal energy and the thermal velocity (for normalization of the grid coordinates)

field.name: orbit_frequency_pol
field.documentation: Poloidal orbit frequency (transit or bounce) at the grid location (in phase space)

field.name: grid_index
field.documentation: Index of the grid used to represent this quantity

field.name: grid_subset_index
field.documentation: Index of the grid subset the data is provided on. Corresponds to the index used in the grid subset definition: grid_subset(:)/identifier/index

field.name: values
field.documentation: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.

field.name: coefficients
field.documentation: Interpolation coefficients, to be used for a high precision evaluation of the physical quantity with finite elements, provided per element in the grid subset (first dimension).

field.name: orbit_frequency_tor
field.documentation: Toroidal orbit frequency (transit or precession) at the grid location (in phase space)

field.name: grid_index
field.documentation: Index of the grid used to represent this quantity

field.name: grid_subset_index
field.documentation: Index of the grid subset the data is provided on. Corresponds to the index used in the grid subset definition: grid_subset(:)/identifier/index

field.name: values
field.documentation: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.

field.name: coefficients
field.documentation: Interpolation coefficients, to be used for a high precision evaluation of the physical quantity with finite elements, provided per element in the grid subset (first dimension).

field.name: expansion
field.documentation: Distribution function expanded into a vector of successive approximations. The first element in the vector (expansion(1)) is the zeroth order distribution function, while the K:th element in the vector (expansion(K)) is the K:th correction, such that the total distribution function is a sum over all elements in the expansion vector.

field.name: grid_subset
field.documentation: Values of the distribution function expansion, for various grid subsets

field.name: grid_index
field.documentation: Index of the grid used to represent this quantity

field.name: grid_subset_index
field.documentation: Index of the grid subset the data is provided on. Corresponds to the index used in the grid subset definition: grid_subset(:)/identifier/index

field.name: values
field.documentation: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.

field.name: coefficients
field.documentation: Interpolation coefficients, to be used for a high precision evaluation of the physical quantity with finite elements, provided per element in the grid subset (first dimension).

field.name: expansion_fd3v
field.documentation: Distribution function multiplied by the volume of the local velocity cell d3v, expanded into a vector of successive approximations. The first element in the vector (expansion(1)) is the zeroth order distribution function, while the K:th element in the vector (expansion(K)) is the K:th correction, such that the total distribution function is a sum over all elements in the expansion vector.

field.name: grid_subset
field.documentation: Values of the distribution function expansion, for various grid subsets

field.name: grid_index
field.documentation: Index of the grid used to represent this quantity

field.name: grid_subset_index
field.documentation: Index of the grid subset the data is provided on. Corresponds to the index used in the grid subset definition: grid_subset(:)/identifier/index

field.name: values
field.documentation: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.

field.name: coefficients
field.documentation: Interpolation coefficients, to be used for a high precision evaluation of the physical quantity with finite elements, provided per element in the grid subset (first dimension).

field.name: amplitude
field.documentation: Value of the distribution function at the grid position in phase space. The interpolation coefficients refer to a C-2 spline.

field.name: grid_index
field.documentation: Index of the grid used to represent this quantity

field.name: grid_subset_index
field.documentation: Index of the grid subset the data is provided on. Corresponds to the index used in the grid subset definition: grid_subset(:)/identifier/index

field.name: values
field.documentation: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.

field.name: coefficients
field.documentation: Interpolation coefficients, to be used for a high precision evaluation of the physical quantity with finite elements, provided per element in the grid subset (first dimension).

field.documentation: Orbit description of the particle at this position in phase space. First dimension is the element index. Second dimension is the time along the orbit. Third dimension contains the particle phase space coordinates.

field.name: grid_index
field.documentation: Index of the grid used to represent this quantity

field.name: grid_subset_index
field.documentation: Index of the grid subset the data is provided on. Corresponds to the index used in the grid subset definition: grid_subset(:)/identifier/index

field.name: values
field.documentation: List of matrix components, one list per element in the grid subset. First dimension: element index. Second dimension: first matrix index. Third dimension: second matrix index.

field.name: coefficients
field.documentation: Interpolation coefficients, to be used for a high precision evaluation of the physical quantity with finite elements, provided per element in the grid subset (first dimension). Second dimension: first matrix index. Third dimension: second matrix index. Fourth dimension: coefficient index

field.name: grid_index
field.documentation: Index of the grid used to represent this quantity

field.name: grid_subset_index
field.documentation: Index of the grid subset the data is provided on. Corresponds to the index used in the grid subset definition: grid_subset(:)/identifier/index

field.name: values
field.documentation: One integer value is provided per element in the grid subset.

field.name: markers
field.documentation: Distribution represented by a set of markers (test particles)

field.name: coordinate_identifier
field.documentation: Set of coordinate identifiers, coordinates on which the markers are represented

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: weights
field.documentation: Weight of the markers, i.e. number of real particles represented by each marker. The dimension of the vector correspond to the number of markers

field.name: positions
field.documentation: Position of the markers in the set of coordinates. The first dimension corresponds to the number of markers, the second dimension to the set of coordinates

field.name: orbit_integrals
field.documentation: Integrals along the markers orbit. These dimensionless expressions are of the form: (1/tau) integral (f(n_tor,m_pol,k,eq,...) dt) from time - tau to time, where tau is the transit/trapping time of the marker and f() a dimensionless function (phase factor,drift,etc) of the equilibrium (e.g. q) and perturbation (Fourier harmonics n_tor,m_pol and bounce harmonic k) along the particles orbits. In fact the integrals are taken during the last orbit of each marker at the time value of the time node below

field.name: expressions
field.documentation: List of the expressions f(n_tor,m_pol,k,q,...) used in the orbit integrals

field.name: n_phi
field.documentation: Array of toroidal mode numbers, where quantities vary as exp(i.n_phi.phi) and phi runs anticlockwise when viewed from above

field.name: m_pol
field.documentation: Array of poloidal mode numbers, where quantities vary as exp(-i.m_pol.theta) and theta is the angle defined by the choice of ../../coordinate_identifier, with its centre at the magnetic axis recalled at the root of this IDS

field.name: orbit_integrals_instant
field.documentation: Integrals/quantities along the markers orbit. These dimensionless expressions are of the form: (1/tau) integral ( f(eq) dt) from time - tau to time_orbit for different values of time_orbit in the interval from time - tau to time, where tau is the transit/trapping time of the marker and f(eq) a dimensionless function (phase, drift,q,etc) of the equilibrium along the markers orbits. The integrals are taken during the last orbit of each marker at the time value of the time node below

field.name: expressions
field.documentation: List of the expressions f(eq) used in the orbit integrals

field.name: time_orbit
field.documentation: Time array along the markers last orbit

field.name: toroidal_mode
field.documentation: In case the orbit integrals are calculated for a given MHD perturbation, index of the toroidal mode considered. Refers to the time_slice/toroidal_mode array of the MHD_LINEAR IDS in which this perturbation is described

field.name: vacuum_toroidal_field
field.documentation: Characteristics of the vacuum toroidal field (used in rho_tor definition and in the normalization of current densities)

field.name: r0
field.documentation: Reference major radius where the vacuum toroidal magnetic field is given (usually a fixed position such as the middle of the vessel at the equatorial midplane)

field.name: b0
field.documentation: Vacuum toroidal field at R0 [T]; Positive sign means anti-clockwise when viewing from above. The product R0B0 must be consistent with the b_tor_vacuum_r field of the tf IDS.

field.name: magnetic_axis
field.documentation: Magnetic axis position (used to define a poloidal angle for the 2D profiles)

field.name: reference

In case the node is the result of of a calculation / data processing, the reference is an input to the process described in the "code" structure at the root of the IDS. The reference can be an IDS (identified by a URI or a persitent identifier, see syntax in the link below) or non-IDS data imported directly from an non-IMAS database (identified by the command used to import the reference, or the persistent identifier of the data reference). Often data are obtained by a chain of processes, however only the last process input are recorded here. The full chain of provenance has then to be reconstructed recursively from the provenance information contained in the data references.

field.documentation: Maximum surface target temperature allowed to prevent damage (melting, recrystallization, sublimation, etc...)

field.name: t_e_target_sputtering_limit_max
field.documentation: Maximum plasma temperature allowed on the divertor target to avoid excessive sputtering

field.name: power_flux_peak

field.documentation: Magnetic flux expansion as defined by Stangeby : ratio between the poloidal field at the midplane separatrix and the poloidal field at the strike-point see formula attached, where u means upstream (midplane separatrix) and t means at divertor target (downstream).

field.name: sol_heat_decay_length
field.documentation: Heat flux decay length in SOL at divertor entrance, mapped to the mid-plane, this is the lambda_q parameter defined in reference T. Eich et al, Nucl. Fusion 53 (2013) 093031

field.name: sol_heat_spreading_length
field.documentation: Heat flux spreading length in SOL at equatorial mid-plane, this is the S power spreading parameter defined in reference T. Eich et al, Nucl. Fusion 53 (2013) 093031. Relevant only for attached plasmas.

field.name: tilt_angle_pol
field.documentation: Angle between field lines projected in poloidal plane and target, measured clockwise from the target to the projected field lines

field.name: extension_r
field.documentation: Target length projected on the major radius axis

field.name: extension_z
field.documentation: Target length projected on the height axis

field.name: wetted_area
field.documentation: Wetted area of the target, defined by the SOL heat flux decay length (lambda_q) mapped to the target using flux expansion and spreading factor and the target toroidal circumference. In other words, this is the area getting heat flux from the maximum value down to one e-fold decay.

field.name: power_incident_fraction
field.documentation: Power fraction incident on the target (normalized to the total power incident on the divertor)

field.name: power_incident
field.documentation: Total power incident on this target. This power is split in the various physical categories listed below

field.name: power_conducted
field.documentation: Power conducted by the plasma on this divertor target

field.name: power_convected
field.documentation: Power convected by the plasma on this divertor target

field.name: power_radiated
field.documentation: Net radiated power on this divertor target (incident - reflected)

field.name: power_black_body
field.documentation: Black body radiated power emitted from this divertor target (emissivity is included)

field.name: power_neutrals
field.documentation: Net power from neutrals on this divertor target (positive means power is deposited on the target)

field.name: power_recombination_plasma
field.documentation: Power deposited on this divertor target due to recombination of plasma ions

field.name: power_recombination_neutrals
field.documentation: Power deposited on this divertor target due to recombination of neutrals into a ground state (e.g. molecules)

field.name: power_currents
field.documentation: Power deposited on this divertor target due to electric currents (positive means power is deposited on the target)

field.name: current_incident
field.documentation: Total current incident on this target

field.name: tile
field.documentation: Set of divertor tiles belonging to this target

field.name: name
field.documentation: Short string identifier (unique for a given device)

field.name: description
field.documentation: Description, e.g. “channel viewing the upper divertor”

field.name: surface_outline
field.documentation: Outline of the tile surface facing the plasma

field.name: phi
field.documentation: Toroidal angle (oriented counter-clockwise when viewing from above)

field.name: surface_area
field.documentation: Area of the tile surface facing the plasma

field.name: current_incident
field.documentation: Total current incident on this tile

field.name: shunt_index
field.documentation: If the tile carries a measurement shunt, index of that shunt (in the magnetics IDS shunt array)

field.name: wetted_area
field.documentation: Wetted area of the divertor (sum over all targets)

field.name: power_incident
field.documentation: Total power incident on the divertor (sum over all targets). This power is split in the various physical categories listed below

field.name: power_conducted
field.documentation: Power conducted by the plasma on the divertor targets (sum over all targets)

field.name: power_convected
field.documentation: Power convected by the plasma on the divertor targets (sum over all targets)

field.name: power_radiated
field.documentation: Net radiated power on the divertor targets (incident - reflected) (sum over all targets)

field.name: power_black_body
field.documentation: Black body radiated power emitted from the divertor targets (emissivity is included) (sum over all targets)

field.name: power_neutrals
field.documentation: Net power from neutrals on the divertor targets (positive means power is deposited on the target) (sum over all targets)

field.name: power_recombination_plasma
field.documentation: Power deposited on the divertor targets due to recombination of plasma ions (sum over all targets)

field.name: power_recombination_neutrals
field.documentation: Power deposited on the divertor targets due to recombination of neutrals into a ground state (e.g. molecules) (sum over all targets)

field.name: power_currents
field.documentation: Power deposited on the divertor targets due to electric currents (positive means power is deposited on the target) (sum over all targets)

field.name: particle_flux_recycled_total
field.documentation: Total recycled particle flux from the divertor (in equivalent electrons)

field.name: current_incident
field.documentation: Total current incident on this divertor

The reference can be an IDS (identified by a URI or a persitent identifier, see syntax in the link below) or non-IDS data imported directly from an non-IMAS database (identified by the command used to import the reference, or the persistent identifier of the data reference). Often data are obtained by a chain of processes, however only the last process input are recorded here. field.name: power_launched
field.documentation: Beam power launched into the vacuum vessel

field.name: mode
field.documentation: Identifier for the main plasma wave mode excited by the EC beam. For the ordinary mode (O-mode), mode=1. For the extraordinary mode (X-mode), mode=-1

field.name: o_mode_fraction
field.documentation: Fraction of EC beam power launched in ordinary (O) mode. If all power is launched in ordinary mode (O-mode), o_mode_fraction = 1.0. If all power is launched in extraordinary mode (X-mode), o_mode_fraction = 0.0

field.name: r_limit_min
field.documentation: Major radius lower limit for the system

field.name: r_limit_max
field.documentation: Major radius upper limit for the system

field.name: steering_angle_pol
field.documentation: Steering angle of the EC beam in the R,Z plane (from the -R axis towards the -Z axis), angle_pol=atan2(-k_Z,-k_R), where k_Z and k_R are the Z and R components of the mean wave vector in the EC beam

field.name: steering_angle_tor
field.documentation: Steering angle of the EC beam away from the poloidal plane that is increasing towards the positive phi axis, angle_tor=arcsin(k_phi/k), where k_phi is the component of the wave vector in the phi direction and k is the length of the wave vector. Here the term wave vector refers to the mean wave vector in the EC beam

field.name: size
field.documentation: Size of the spot ellipse: distance between the central ray and the peripheral rays in the horizontal (first index of the first coordinate) and vertical direction (second index of the first coordinate)

field.name: angle
field.documentation: Rotation angle for the spot ellipse

field.name: curvature
field.documentation: Inverse curvature radii for the phase ellipse, positive/negative for divergent/convergent beams, in the horizontal direction (first index of the first coordinate) and in the vertical direction (second index of the first coordinate)

field.name: angle
field.documentation: Rotation angle for the phase ellipse

field.name: time
field.documentation: Time base used for launching_position, o_mode_fraction, angle, spot and phase quantities

field.name: latency
field.documentation: Upper bound of the delay between input command received from the RT network and actuator starting to react. Applies globally to the system described by this IDS unless specific latencies (e.g. channel-specific or antenna-specific) are provided at a deeper level in the IDS structure.

field.documentation: Calibration factor, used as t_radiation = calibration_factor * (voltage_t_radiation - calibration_offset)

field.name: calibration_offset
field.documentation: Calibration offset, may be re-evaluated dynamically during long pulses on some experiments

field.name: beam
field.documentation: ECE Gaussian optics parameters taken at the line_of_sight/first_point position (for synthetic modelling of the ECE emission)

field.name: angle
field.documentation: Rotation angle for the spot ellipse

field.name: curvature
field.documentation: Inverse curvature radii for the phase ellipse, positive/negative for divergent/convergent beams

field.name: angle
field.documentation: Rotation angle for the phase ellipse

field.name: beam_tracing
field.documentation: Beam tracing calculations, for various time slices

field.name: beam
field.documentation: Set of rays/beams describing the wave propagation

field.name: mode
field.documentation: X or O mode for this beam

field.name: position
field.documentation: Position of the ray/beam along its path

field.name: theta
field.documentation: Poloidal angle (oriented clockwise when viewing the poloidal cross section on the right hand side of the tokamak axis of symmetry, with the origin placed on the plasma magnetic axis)

field.name: wave_vector
field.documentation: Wave vector of the ray/beam along its path

field.name: k_r
field.documentation: Wave vector component in the major radius direction

field.name: k_z
field.documentation: Wave vector component in the vertical direction

field.name: k_phi
field.documentation: Wave vector component in the toroidal direction

field.name: k_r_norm
field.documentation: Normalized wave vector component in the major radius direction = k_r / norm(k)

field.name: k_z_norm
field.documentation: Normalized wave vector component in the vertical direction = k_z / norm(k)

field.name: k_phi_norm
field.documentation: Normalized wave vector component in the toroidal direction = k_phi / norm(k)

field.name: n_phi
field.documentation: Toroidal wave number, contains a single value if varying_n_phi = 0 to avoid useless repetition of constant values. The wave vector toroidal component is defined as k_phi = n_phi grad phi where phi is the toroidal angle so that a positive n_phi means a wave propagating in the positive phi direction

field.name: varying_n_phi
field.documentation: Flag telling whether n_phi is constant along the ray path (0) or varying (1)

field.name: e_field
field.documentation: Electric field polarization of the ray/beam along its path

field.name: plus
field.documentation: Left hand polarised electric field component

field.name: minus
field.documentation: Right hand polarised electric field component

field.name: parallel
field.documentation: Parallel to magnetic field polarised electric field component

field.name: perpendicular
field.documentation: Normalized power flow in the direction perpendicular to the magnetic field

field.name: parallel
field.documentation: Normalized power flow in the direction parallel to the magnetic field

field.name: power
field.documentation: Power absorbed along the beam by the species

field.name: size
field.documentation: Size of the spot ellipse: distance between the central ray and the peripheral rays in the horizontal (first index of the first coordinate) and vertical direction (second index of the first coordinate)

field.name: angle
field.documentation: Rotation angle for the spot ellipse

field.name: curvature
field.documentation: Inverse curvature radii for the phase ellipse, positive/negative for divergent/convergent beams, in the horizontal direction (first index of the first coordinate) and in the vertical direction (second index of the first coordinate)

field.name: angle
field.documentation: Rotation angle for the phase ellipse

field.name: polarizer
field.documentation: Set of polarizers placed in front of the diagnostic (if any). Polarizers are assumed to be orthogonal to the line of sight, so that the x3 unit vector is aligned with the line of sight

field.name: centre
field.documentation: If geometry_type=2, coordinates of the centre of the circle. If geometry_type=1 or 3, coordinates of the origin of the local coordinate system (X1,X2,X3) describing the plane polarizer. This origin is located within the polarizer area. Note that there is some flexibility here and the data provider should choose the most convenient coordinate system for the object, respecting the definitions of (X1,X2,X3) indicated below.

field.name: phi
field.documentation: Toroidal angle (oriented counter-clockwise when viewing from above)

field.name: radius
field.documentation: Radius of the circle, used only if geometry_type = 2

field.name: x1_unit_vector
field.documentation: Components of the X1 direction unit vector in the (X,Y,Z) coordinate system, where X is the major radius axis for phi = 0, Y is the major radius axis for phi = pi/2, and Z is the height axis. The X1 vector is more horizontal than X2 (has a smaller abs(Z) component) and oriented in the positive phi direction (counter-clockwise when viewing from above).

field.name: x2_unit_vector
field.documentation: Components of the X2 direction unit vector in the (X,Y,Z) coordinate system, where X is the major radius axis for phi = 0, Y is the major radius axis for phi = pi/2, and Z is the height axis. The X2 axis is orthonormal so that uX2 = uX3 x uX1.

field.name: x3_unit_vector
field.documentation: Components of the X3 direction unit vector in the (X,Y,Z) coordinate system, where X is the major radius axis for phi = 0, Y is the major radius axis for phi = pi/2, and Z is the height axis. The X3 axis is normal to the polarizer plane and oriented towards the plasma.

field.name: polarization_angle
field.documentation: Alignment angle of the polarizer in the (x1,x2) plane. Electric fields parallel to the polarizer angle will be reflected. The angle is defined with respect to the x1 unit vector, positive in the counter-clockwise direction when looking towards the plasma

field.name: psi_normalization
field.documentation: Quantities to use to normalize psi, as a function of time

field.name: psi_magnetic_axis
field.documentation: Value of the poloidal magnetic flux at the magnetic axis

field.name: psi_boundary
field.documentation: Value of the poloidal magnetic flux at the plasma boundary

field.name: latency
field.documentation: Upper bound of the delay between physical information received by the detector and data available on the real-time (RT) network.

field.name: code
field.documentation: Generic decription of the code-specific parameters for the code that has produced this IDS

field.name: description
field.documentation: Short description of the software (type, purpose)

field.name: parameters
field.documentation: List of the code specific parameters in XML format

field.name: output_flag
field.documentation: Output flag : 0 means the run is successful, other values mean some difficulty has been encountered, the exact meaning is then code specific. Negative values mean the result shall not be used.

field.name: library
field.documentation: List of external libraries used by the code that has produced this IDS

field.name: description
field.documentation: Short description of the software (type, purpose)

field.name: parameters
field.documentation: List of the code specific parameters in XML format

IDS.name: edge_profiles
IDS.documentation: Edge plasma profiles (includes the scrape-off layer and possibly part of the confined plasma)

field.name: ids_properties
field.documentation: Interface Data Structure properties. This element identifies the node above as an IDS

field.name: comment
field.documentation: Any comment describing the content of this IDS

field.name: name
field.documentation: User-defined name for this IDS occurrence

field.name: homogeneous_time
field.documentation: This node must be filled (with 0, 1, or 2) for the IDS to be valid. If 1, the time of this IDS is homogeneous, i.e. the time values for this IDS are stored in the time node just below the root of this IDS. If 0, the time values are stored in the various time fields at lower levels in the tree. In the case only constant or static nodes are filled within the IDS, homogeneous_time must be set to 2

field.name: occurrence_type
field.documentation: Type of data contained in this occurrence

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: provider
field.documentation: Name of the person in charge of producing this data

field.name: creation_date
field.documentation: Date at which this data has been produced

field.name: version_put
field.documentation: Version of the access layer package used to PUT this IDS

field.name: data_dictionary
field.documentation: Version of Data Dictionary used to PUT this IDS

field.name: access_layer
field.documentation: Version of Access Layer used to PUT this IDS

field.name: access_layer_language
field.documentation: Programming language of the Access Layer high level API used to PUT this IDS

field.name: node
field.documentation: Set of IDS nodes for which the provenance is given. The provenance information applies to the whole structure below the IDS node. For documenting provenance information for the whole IDS, set the size of this array of structure to 1 and leave the child "path" node empty

field.name: path
field.documentation: Path of the node within the IDS, following the syntax given in the link below. If empty, means the provenance information applies to the whole IDS.

field.name: reference
field.documentation: List of references used to populate or calculate this node, identified as explained below. In case the node is the result of of a calculation / data processing, the reference is an input to the process described in the "code" structure at the root of the IDS. The reference can be an IDS (identified by a URI or a persitent identifier, see syntax in the link below) or non-IDS data imported directly from an non-IMAS database (identified by the command used to import the reference, or the persistent identifier of the data reference). Often data are obtained by a chain of processes, however only the last process input are recorded here. The full chain of provenance has then to be reconstructed recursively from the provenance information contained in the data references.

field.name: timestamp
field.documentation: Date and time (UTC) at which the reference was created, expressed in a human readable form (ISO 8601) : the format of the string shall be : YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ. Example : 2020-07-24T14:19:00Z

field.name: plugins
field.documentation: Information about the plugins used to write/read this IDS. This structure is filled automatically by the Access Layer at GET/PUT time, no need to fill it via a user program.

field.name: node
field.documentation: Set of IDS nodes for which a plugin has been applied

field.name: path
field.documentation: Path of the node within the IDS, following the syntax given in the link below. If empty, means the plugin applies to the whole IDS.

field.name: put_operation
field.documentation: Plugins used to PUT a node (potentially, multiple plugins can be applied, if so they are listed by order of application)

field.name: description
field.documentation: Short description of the software (type, purpose)

field.name: parameters
field.documentation: List of the code specific parameters in XML format

field.name: library
field.documentation: List of external libraries used by the code that has produced this IDS

field.name: description
field.documentation: Short description of the software (type, purpose)

field.name: parameters
field.documentation: List of the code specific parameters in XML format

field.name: readback
field.documentation: Plugins to be used to read back a node (potentially, multiple plugins can be applied, listed in reverse order of application)

field.name: description
field.documentation: Short description of the software (type, purpose)

field.name: parameters
field.documentation: List of the code specific parameters in XML format

field.name: library
field.documentation: List of external libraries used by the code that has produced this IDS

field.name: description
field.documentation: Short description of the software (type, purpose)

field.name: parameters
field.documentation: List of the code specific parameters in XML format

field.name: get_operation
field.documentation: Plugins actually used to read back a node (potentially, multiple plugins can be applied, listed in reverse order of application). This information is filled by the plugin infrastructure during the GET operation.

field.name: description
field.documentation: Short description of the software (type, purpose)

field.name: parameters

field.name: library
field.documentation: List of external libraries used by the code that has produced this IDS

field.documentation: Short description of the software (type, purpose)

field.name: parameters
field.documentation: List of the code specific parameters in XML format

field.name: infrastructure_put
field.documentation: Plugin infrastructure used to PUT the data

field.name: description
field.documentation: Short description of the software (type, purpose)

field.name: infrastructure_get
field.documentation: Plugin infrastructure used to GET the data

field.name: description
field.documentation: Short description of the software (type, purpose)

field.name: vacuum_toroidal_field
field.documentation: Characteristics of the vacuum toroidal field (used in rho_tor definition and in the normalization of current densities)

field.name: r0
field.documentation: Reference major radius where the vacuum toroidal magnetic field is given (usually a fixed position such as the middle of the vessel at the equatorial midplane)

field.name: b0
field.documentation: Vacuum toroidal field at R0 [T]; Positive sign means anti-clockwise when viewing from above. The product R0B0 must be consistent with the b_tor_vacuum_r field of the tf IDS.

field.name: midplane
field.documentation: Choice of midplane definition (use the lowest index number if more than one value is relevant)

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: profiles_1d
field.documentation: SOL radial profiles for various time slices, taken on outboard equatorial mid-plane

field.name: psi
field.documentation: Poloidal magnetic flux. Integral of magnetic field passing through a contour defined by the intersection of a flux surface passing through the point of interest and a Z=constant plane. If the integration surface is flat, the surface normal vector is in the increasing vertical coordinate direction, Z, namely upwards.

field.name: rho_tor_norm
field.documentation: Normalized toroidal flux coordinate. The normalizing value for rho_tor_norm, is the toroidal flux coordinate at the equilibrium boundary (LCFS or 99.x % of the LCFS in case of a fixed boundary equilibium calculation, see time_slice/boundary/b_flux_pol_norm in the equilibrium IDS)

field.name: rho_tor
field.documentation: Toroidal flux coordinate. rho_tor = sqrt(b_flux_tor/(pi*b0)) ~ sqrt(pi*r^2*b0/(pi*b0)) ~ r [m]. The toroidal field used in its definition is indicated under vacuum_toroidal_field/b0

field.name: volume
field.documentation: Volume enclosed inside the magnetic surface

field.name: area
field.documentation: Cross-sectional area of the flux surface

field.name: psi_magnetic_axis
field.documentation: Value of the poloidal magnetic flux at the magnetic axis (useful to normalize the psi array values when the radial grid doesn't go from the magnetic axis to the plasma boundary)

field.name: psi_boundary
field.documentation: Value of the poloidal magnetic flux at the plasma boundary (useful to normalize the psi array values when the radial grid doesn't go from the magnetic axis to the plasma boundary)

field.name: temperature_validity
field.documentation: Indicator of the validity of the temperature profile. 0: valid from automated processing, 1: valid and certified by the RO; - 1 means problem identified in the data processing (request verification by the RO), -2: invalid data, should not be used

field.name: temperature_fit
field.documentation: Information on the fit used to obtain the temperature profile

field.name: measured
field.documentation: Measured values. Units are: as_parent for a local measurement, as_parent.m for a line integrated measurement.

field.name: source
field.documentation: Path to the source data for each measurement in the IMAS data dictionary, e.g. ece/channel(i)/t_e for the electron temperature on the i-th channel in the ECE IDS

field.name: time_measurement
field.documentation: Exact time slices used from the time array of the measurement source data. If the time slice does not exist in the time array of the source data, it means linear interpolation has been used

field.name: time_measurement_slice_method
field.documentation: Method used to slice the data : index = 0 means using exact time slice of the measurement, 1 means linear interpolation, ...

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: time_measurement_width
field.documentation: In case the measurements are averaged over a time interval, this node is the full width of this time interval (empty otherwise). In case the slicing/averaging method doesn't use a hard time interval cutoff, this width is the characteristic time span of the slicing/averaging method. By convention, the time interval starts at time_measurement-time_width and ends at time_measurement.

field.name: local
field.documentation: Integer flag : 1 means local measurement, 0 means line-integrated measurement

field.name: rho_tor_norm
field.documentation: Normalized toroidal flux coordinate of each measurement (local value for a local measurement, minimum value reached by the line of sight for a line measurement)

field.name: rho_pol_norm
field.documentation: Normalized poloidal flux coordinate of each measurement (local value for a local measurement, minimum value reached by the line of sight for a line measurement)

field.name: weight
field.documentation: Weight given to each measured value

field.name: reconstructed
field.documentation: Value reconstructed from the fit. Units are: as_parent for a local measurement, as_parent.m for a line integrated measurement.

field.name: chi_squared
field.documentation: Squared error normalized by the weighted standard deviation considered in the minimization process : chi_squared = weight^2 *(reconstructed - measured)^2 / sigma^2, where sigma is the standard deviation of the measurement error

field.name: parameters
field.documentation: List of the fit specific parameters in XML format

field.name: density_validity
field.documentation: Indicator of the validity of the density profile. 0: valid from automated processing, 1: valid and certified by the RO; - 1 means problem identified in the data processing (request verification by the RO), -2: invalid data, should not be used

field.name: density_fit

field.name: atoms_n
field.documentation: Number of atoms of this element in the molecule

field.name: z_ion
field.documentation: Ion charge (of the dominant ionization state; lumped ions are allowed), volume averaged over plasma radius

field.documentation: String identifying ion (e.g. H, D, T, He, C, D2, ...)

field.name: neutral_index
field.documentation: Index of the corresponding neutral species in the ../../neutral array

field.name: z_ion_1d
field.documentation: Average charge of the ion species (sum of states charge weighted by state density and divided by ion density)

field.name: z_ion_square_1d
field.documentation: Average square charge of the ion species (sum of states square charge weighted by state density and divided by ion density)

field.name: density_thermal
field.documentation: Density (thermal) (sum over charge states when multiple charge states are considered)

field.name: density_fast
field.documentation: Density of fast (non-thermal) particles (sum over charge states when multiple charge states are considered)

field.name: pressure
field.documentation: Pressure (thermal+non-thermal) (sum over charge states when multiple charge states are considered)

field.name: pressure_thermal
field.documentation: Pressure (thermal) associated with random motion ~average((v-average(v))^2) (sum over charge states when multiple charge states are considered)

field.name: pressure_fast_perpendicular
field.documentation: Fast (non-thermal) perpendicular pressure (sum over charge states when multiple charge states are considered)

field.name: pressure_fast_parallel
field.documentation: Fast (non-thermal) parallel pressure (sum over charge states when multiple charge states are considered)

field.name: rotation_frequency_tor
field.documentation: Toroidal rotation frequency (i.e. toroidal velocity divided by the major radius at which the toroidal velocity is taken) (average over charge states when multiple charge states are considered)

field.name: velocity
field.documentation: Velocity (average over charge states when multiple charge states are considered) at the position of maximum major radius on every flux surface

field.name: multiple_states_flag
field.documentation: Multiple states calculation flag : 0-Only the 'ion' level is considered and the 'state' array of structure is empty; 1-Ion states are considered and are described in the 'state' array of structure

field.name: state
field.documentation: Quantities related to the different states of the species (ionization, energy, excitation, ...)

field.name: z_min
field.documentation: Minimum Z of the charge state bundle

field.name: z_max
field.documentation: Maximum Z of the charge state bundle (equal to z_min if no bundle)

field.name: z_average
field.documentation: Average Z of the charge state bundle, volume averaged over the plasma radius (equal to z_min if no bundle), = sum (Z*x_z) where x_z is the relative concentration of a given charge state in the bundle, i.e. sum(x_z) = 1 over the bundle.

field.name: z_square_average
field.documentation: Average Z square of the charge state bundle, volume averaged over the plasma radius (equal to z_min squared if no bundle), = sum (Z^2*x_z) where x_z is the relative concentration of a given charge state in the bundle, i.e. sum(x_z) = 1 over the bundle.

field.name: z_average_1d
field.documentation: Average charge profile of the charge state bundle (equal to z_min if no bundle), = sum (Z*x_z) where x_z is the relative concentration of a given charge state in the bundle, i.e. sum(x_z) = 1 over the bundle.

field.name: z_average_square_1d
field.documentation: Average square charge profile of the charge state bundle (equal to z_min squared if no bundle), = sum (Z^2*x_z) where x_z is the relative concentration of a given charge state in the bundle, i.e. sum(x_z) = 1 over the bundle.

field.name: ionization_potential
field.documentation: Cumulative and average ionization potential to reach a given bundle. Defined as sum (x_z* (sum of Epot from z'=0 to z-1)), where Epot is the ionization potential of ion Xz_+, and x_z is the relative concentration of a given charge state in the bundle, i.e. sum(x_z) = 1 over the bundle.

field.name: name
field.documentation: String identifying state (e.g. C+, C+2 , C+3, C+4, C+5, C+6, ...)

field.name: electron_configuration
field.documentation: Configuration of atomic orbitals of this state, e.g. 1s2-2s1

field.name: vibrational_mode
field.documentation: Vibrational mode of this state, e.g. "A_g". Need to define, or adopt a standard nomenclature.

field.name: rotation_frequency_tor
field.documentation: Toroidal rotation frequency (i.e. toroidal velocity divided by the major radius at which the toroidal velocity is taken)

field.name: density_fit
field.documentation: Information on the fit used to obtain the density profile

field.name: measured
field.documentation: Measured values. Units are: as_parent for a local measurement, as_parent.m for a line integrated measurement.

field.name: source
field.documentation: Path to the source data for each measurement in the IMAS data dictionary, e.g. ece/channel(i)/t_e for the electron temperature on the i-th channel in the ECE IDS

field.name: time_measurement
field.documentation: Exact time slices used from the time array of the measurement source data. If the time slice does not exist in the time array of the source data, it means linear interpolation has been used

field.name: time_measurement_slice_method
field.documentation: Method used to slice the data : index = 0 means using exact time slice of the measurement, 1 means linear interpolation, ...

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: time_measurement_width
field.documentation: In case the measurements are averaged over a time interval, this node is the full width of this time interval (empty otherwise). In case the slicing/averaging method doesn't use a hard time interval cutoff, this width is the characteristic time span of the slicing/averaging method. By convention, the time interval starts at time_measurement-time_width and ends at time_measurement.

field.name: local
field.documentation: Integer flag : 1 means local measurement, 0 means line-integrated measurement

field.name: rho_tor_norm
field.documentation: Normalized toroidal flux coordinate of each measurement (local value for a local measurement, minimum value reached by the line of sight for a line measurement)

field.name: rho_pol_norm
field.documentation: Normalized poloidal flux coordinate of each measurement (local value for a local measurement, minimum value reached by the line of sight for a line measurement)

field.name: weight
field.documentation: Weight given to each measured value

field.name: reconstructed
field.documentation: Value reconstructed from the fit. Units are: as_parent for a local measurement, as_parent.m for a line integrated measurement.

field.name: chi_squared
field.documentation: Squared error normalized by the weighted standard deviation considered in the minimization process : chi_squared = weight^2 *(reconstructed - measured)^2 / sigma^2, where sigma is the standard deviation of the measurement error

field.name: parameters
field.documentation: List of the fit specific parameters in XML format

field.name: neutral
field.documentation: Quantities related to the different neutral species

field.name: element
field.documentation: List of elements forming the atom or molecule

field.name: atoms_n
field.documentation: Number of atoms of this element in the molecule

field.name: name
field.documentation: String identifying the species (e.g. H, D, T, He, C, D2, DT, CD4, ...)

field.name: ion_index
field.documentation: Index of the corresponding ion species in the ../../ion array

field.name: temperature
field.documentation: Temperature (average over charge states when multiple charge states are considered)

field.name: density
field.documentation: Density (thermal+non-thermal) (sum over charge states when multiple charge states are considered)

field.name: density_thermal
field.documentation: Density (thermal) (sum over charge states when multiple charge states are considered)

field.name: density_fast
field.documentation: Density of fast (non-thermal) particles (sum over charge states when multiple charge states are considered)

field.name: pressure
field.documentation: Pressure (thermal+non-thermal) (sum over charge states when multiple charge states are considered)

field.name: pressure_thermal
field.documentation: Pressure (thermal) associated with random motion ~average((v-average(v))^2) (sum over charge states when multiple charge states are considered)

field.name: pressure_fast_perpendicular
field.documentation: Fast (non-thermal) perpendicular pressure (sum over charge states when multiple charge states are considered)

field.name: pressure_fast_parallel
field.documentation: Fast (non-thermal) parallel pressure (sum over charge states when multiple charge states are considered)

field.name: multiple_states_flag
field.documentation: Multiple states calculation flag : 0-Only one state is considered; 1-Multiple states are considered and are described in the state structure

field.name: state
field.documentation: Quantities related to the different states of the species (energy, excitation, ...)

field.name: electron_configuration
field.documentation: Configuration of atomic orbitals of this state, e.g. 1s2-2s1

field.name: vibrational_mode
field.documentation: Vibrational mode of this state, e.g. "A_g". Need to define, or adopt a standard nomenclature.

field.name: neutral_type
field.documentation: Neutral type (if the considered state is a neutral), in terms of energy. ID =1: cold; 2: thermal; 3: fast; 4: NBI

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: t_i_average

field.name: pressure_ion_total
field.documentation: Total (sum over ion species) thermal ion pressure

field.name: j_total
field.documentation: Total parallel current density = average(jtot.B) / B0, where B0 = edge_profiles/Vacuum_Toroidal_Field/ B0

field.name: current_parallel_inside
field.documentation: Parallel current driven inside the flux surface. Cumulative surface integral of j_total

field.name: j_phi
field.documentation: Total toroidal current density = average(J_phi/R) / average(1/R)

field.name: j_ohmic
field.documentation: Ohmic parallel current density = average(J_Ohmic.B) / B0, where B0 = edge_profiles/Vacuum_Toroidal_Field/ B0

field.name: j_non_inductive
field.documentation: Non-inductive (includes bootstrap) parallel current density = average(jni.B) / B0, where B0 = edge_profiles/Vacuum_Toroidal_Field/ B0

field.name: j_bootstrap
field.documentation: Bootstrap current density = average(J_Bootstrap.B) / B0, where B0 = edge_profiles/Vacuum_Toroidal_Field/ B0

field.name: e_field
field.documentation: Electric field, averaged on the magnetic surface. E.g for the parallel component, average(E.B) / B0, using edge_profiles/vacuum_toroidal_field/b0

field.name: phi_potential
field.documentation: Electrostatic potential, averaged on the magnetic flux surface

field.name: rotation_frequency_tor_sonic
field.documentation: Derivative of the flux surface averaged electrostatic potential with respect to the poloidal flux, multiplied by -1. This quantity is the toroidal angular rotation frequency due to the ExB drift, introduced in formula (43) of Hinton and Wong, Physics of Fluids 3082 (1985), also referred to as sonic flow in regimes in which the toroidal velocity is dominant over the poloidal velocity

field.name: magnetic_shear
field.documentation: Magnetic shear, defined as rho_tor/q . dq/drho_tor

field.name: grid_ggd
field.documentation: Grid (using the Generic Grid Description), for various time slices. The timebase of this array of structure must be a subset of the ggd timebase

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: path
field.documentation: Path of the grid, including the IDS name, in case of implicit reference to a grid_ggd node described in another IDS. To be filled only if the grid is not described explicitly in this grid_ggd structure. Example syntax: #wall:2/description_ggd(1)/grid_ggd, means that the grid is located in the wall IDS, occurrence 2, with relative path description_ggd(1)/grid_ggd, using Fortran index convention (here : first index of the array)

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: geometry_type
field.documentation: Type of space geometry (0: standard, 1:Fourier, >1: Fourier with periodicity)

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: coordinates_type
field.documentation: Type of coordinates describing the physical space, for every coordinate of the space. The size of this node therefore defines the dimension of the space.

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: objects_per_dimension
field.documentation: Definition of the space objects for every dimension (from one to the dimension of the highest-dimensional objects). The index correspond to 1=nodes, 2=edges, 3=faces, 4=cells/volumes, .... For every index, a collection of objects of that dimension is described.

field.name: object
field.documentation: Set of objects for a given dimension

field.name: boundary
field.documentation: Set of (n-1)-dimensional objects defining the boundary of this n-dimensional object

field.name: neighbours
field.documentation: List of indices of the n-dimensional objects adjacent to the given n-dimensional object. An object can possibly have multiple neighbours on a boundary

field.name: geometry
field.documentation: Geometry data associated with the object, its detailed content is defined by ../../geometry_content. Its dimension depends on the type of object, geometry and coordinate considered.

field.name: nodes
field.documentation: List of nodes forming this object (indices to objects_per_dimension(1)%object(:) in Fortran notation)

field.name: measure
field.documentation: Measure of the space object, i.e. physical size (length for 1d, area for 2d, volume for 3d objects,...)

field.name: geometry_2d
field.documentation: 2D geometry data associated with the object. Its dimension depends on the type of object, geometry and coordinate considered. Typically, the first dimension represents the object coordinates, while the second dimension would represent the values of the various degrees of freedom of the finite element attached to the object.

field.name: geometry_content
field.documentation: Content of the ../object/geometry node for this dimension

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: dimension
field.documentation: Space dimension of the grid subset elements, using the convention 1=nodes, 2=edges, 3=faces, 4=cells/volumes

field.name: element
field.documentation: Set of elements defining the grid subset. An element is defined by a combination of objects from potentially all spaces

field.name: object
field.documentation: Set of objects defining the element

field.name: space
field.documentation: Index of the space from which that object is taken

field.name: dimension
field.documentation: Dimension of the object - using the convention 1=nodes, 2=edges, 3=faces, 4=cells/volumes

field.name: base
field.documentation: Set of bases for the grid subset. For each base, the structure describes the projection of the base vectors on the canonical frame of the grid.

field.name: tensor_covariant
field.documentation: Covariant metric tensor, given on each element of the subgrid (first dimension)

field.name: tensor_contravariant
field.documentation: Contravariant metric tensor, given on each element of the subgrid (first dimension)

field.name: metric
field.documentation: Metric of the canonical frame onto Cartesian coordinates

field.name: tensor_covariant

field.name: tensor_contravariant

field.name: values
field.documentation: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.

If 0, the time values are stored in the various time fields at lower levels in the tree. In the case only constant or static nodes are filled within the IDS, homogeneous_time must be set to 2

field.name: reference
field.documentation: List of references used to populate or calculate this node, identified as explained below. In case the node is the result of of a calculation / data processing, the reference is an input to the process described in the "code" structure at the root of the IDS. The reference can be an IDS (identified by a URI or a persitent identifier, see syntax in the link below) or non-IDS data imported directly from an non-IMAS database (identified by the command used to import the reference, or the persistent identifier of the data reference). Often data are obtained by a chain of processes, however only the last process input are recorded here. The full chain of provenance has then to be reconstructed recursively from the provenance information contained in the data references.

field.name: timestamp

field.name: index

field.name: object

field.name: boundary

field.name: geometry
field.documentation: Geometry data associated with the object, its detailed content is defined by ../../geometry_content. Its dimension depends on the type of object, geometry and coordinate considered.

field.name: nodes

field.name: measure
field.documentation: Measure of the space object, i.e. physical size (length for 1d, area for 2d, volume for 3d objects,...)

field.name: geometry_2d
field.documentation: 2D geometry data associated with the object. Its dimension depends on the type of object, geometry and coordinate considered. Typically, the first dimension represents the object coordinates, while the second dimension would represent the values of the various degrees of freedom of the finite element attached to the object.

field.name: geometry_content

field.name: dimension
field.documentation: Dimension of the object - using the convention 1=nodes, 2=edges, 3=faces, 4=cells/volumes

field.name: base
field.documentation: Set of bases for the grid subset. For each base, the structure describes the projection of the base vectors on the canonical frame of the grid.

field.name: tensor_covariant
field.documentation: Covariant metric tensor, given on each element of the subgrid (first dimension)

field.name: tensor_contravariant
field.documentation: Contravariant metric tensor, given on each element of the subgrid (first dimension)

field.name: metric
field.documentation: Metric of the canonical frame onto Cartesian coordinates

field.name: tensor_covariant
field.documentation: Covariant metric tensor, given on each element of the subgrid (first dimension)

field.name: tensor_contravariant
field.documentation: Contravariant metric tensor, given on each element of the subgrid (first dimension)

field.documentation: Source term identifier (process causing this source term)

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: species
field.documentation: Species causing this source term (if relevant, e.g. a particular ion or neutral state in case of line radiation)

field.name: type
field.documentation: Species type. index=1 for electron; index=2 for ion species in a single/average state (refer to ion structure); index=3 for ion species in a particular state (refer to ion/state structure); index=4 for neutral species in a single/average state (refer to neutral structure); index=5 for neutral species in a particular state (refer to neutral/state structure); index=6 for neutron; index=7 for photon

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: ion

field.documentation: List of elements forming the atom or molecule

field.name: atoms_n
field.documentation: Number of atoms of this element in the molecule

field.name: z_ion
field.documentation: Ion charge (of the dominant ionization state; lumped ions are allowed)

field.name: name
field.documentation: String identifying ion (e.g. H+, D+, T+, He+2, C+, ...)

field.name: state
field.documentation: Quantities related to the different states of the species (ionization, energy, excitation, ...)

field.name: z_min
field.documentation: Minimum Z of the charge state bundle (z_min = z_max = 0 for a neutral)

field.name: z_max
field.documentation: Maximum Z of the charge state bundle (equal to z_min if no bundle)
