IDS.name: edge_transport
IDS.documentation: Edge plasma transport. Energy terms correspond to the full kinetic energy equation (i.e. the energy flux takes into account the energy transported by the particle flux)

field.name: ids_properties
field.documentation: Interface Data Structure properties. This element identifies the node above as an IDS

field.name: comment
field.documentation: Any comment describing the content of this IDS

field.name: name
field.documentation: User-defined name for this IDS occurrence

field.name: homogeneous_time
field.documentation: This node must be filled (with 0, 1, or 2) for the IDS to be valid. If 1, the time of this IDS is homogeneous, i.e. the time values for this IDS are stored in the time node just below the root of this IDS. If 0, the time values are stored in the various time fields at lower levels in the tree. In the case only constant or static nodes are filled within the IDS, homogeneous_time must be set to 2

field.name: occurrence_type
field.documentation: Type of data contained in this occurrence

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: provider
field.documentation: Name of the person in charge of producing this data

field.name: creation_date
field.documentation: Date at which this data has been produced

field.name: version_put
field.documentation: Version of the access layer package used to PUT this IDS

field.name: data_dictionary
field.documentation: Version of Data Dictionary used to PUT this IDS

field.name: access_layer
field.documentation: Version of Access Layer used to PUT this IDS

field.name: access_layer_language
field.documentation: Programming language of the Access Layer high level API used to PUT this IDS

field.name: node
field.documentation: Set of IDS nodes for which the provenance is given. The provenance information applies to the whole structure below the IDS node. For documenting provenance information for the whole IDS, set the size of this array of structure to 1 and leave the child "path" node empty

field.name: path
field.documentation: Path of the node within the IDS, following the syntax given in the link below. If empty, means the provenance information applies to the whole IDS.

field.name: reference
field.documentation: List of references used to populate or calculate this node, identified as explained below. In case the node is the result of of a calculation / data processing, the reference is an input to the process described in the "code" structure at the root of the IDS. The reference can be an IDS (identified by a URI or a persitent identifier, see syntax in the link below) or non-IDS data imported directly from an non-IMAS database (identified by the command used to import the reference, or the persistent identifier of the data reference). Often data are obtained by a chain of processes, however only the last process input are recorded here. The full chain of provenance has then to be reconstructed recursively from the provenance information contained in the data references.

field.name: timestamp
field.documentation: Date and time (UTC) at which the reference was created, expressed in a human readable form (ISO 8601) : the format of the string shall be : YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ. Example : 2020-07-24T14:19:00Z

field.name: plugins
field.documentation: Information about the plugins used to write/read this IDS. This structure is filled automatically by the Access Layer at GET/PUT time, no need to fill it via a user program.

field.name: node
field.documentation: Set of IDS nodes for which a plugin has been applied

field.name: path
field.documentation: Path of the node within the IDS, following the syntax given in the link below. If empty, means the plugin applies to the whole IDS.

field.documentation: Short description of the software (type, purpose)

field.name: midplane
field.documentation: Choice of midplane definition (use the lowest index number if more than one value is relevant)

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: grid_ggd
field.documentation: Grid (using the Generic Grid Description), for various time slices. The timebase of this array of structure must be a subset of the ggd timebases

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: path
field.documentation: Path of the grid, including the IDS name, in case of implicit reference to a grid_ggd node described in another IDS. To be filled only if the grid is not described explicitly in this grid_ggd structure. Example syntax: #wall:2/description_ggd(1)/grid_ggd, means that the grid is located in the wall IDS, occurrence 2, with relative path description_ggd(1)/grid_ggd, using Fortran index convention (here : first index of the array)

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: geometry_type
field.documentation: Type of space geometry (0: standard, 1:Fourier, >1: Fourier with periodicity)

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: coordinates_type
field.documentation: Type of coordinates describing the physical space, for every coordinate of the space. The size of this node therefore defines the dimension of the space.

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: objects_per_dimension
field.documentation: Definition of the space objects for every dimension (from one to the dimension of the highest-dimensional objects). The index correspond to 1=nodes, 2=edges, 3=faces, 4=cells/volumes, .... For every index, a collection of objects of that dimension is described.

field.name: object
field.documentation: Set of objects for a given dimension

field.name: boundary
field.documentation: Set of (n-1)-dimensional objects defining the boundary of this n-dimensional object

field.name: neighbours
field.documentation: List of indices of the n-dimensional objects adjacent to the given n-dimensional object. An object can possibly have multiple neighbours on a boundary

field.name: geometry
field.documentation: Geometry data associated with the object, its detailed content is defined by ../../geometry_content. Its dimension depends on the type of object, geometry and coordinate considered.

field.name: nodes
field.documentation: List of nodes forming this object (indices to objects_per_dimension(1)%object(:) in Fortran notation)

field.name: measure
field.documentation: Measure of the space object, i.e. physical size (length for 1d, area for 2d, volume for 3d objects,...)

field.name: geometry_2d
field.documentation: 2D geometry data associated with the object. Its dimension depends on the type of object, geometry and coordinate considered. Typically, the first dimension represents the object coordinates, while the second dimension would represent the values of the various degrees of freedom of the finite element attached to the object.

field.name: geometry_content
field.documentation: Content of the ../object/geometry node for this dimension

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: dimension
field.documentation: Space dimension of the grid subset elements, using the convention 1=nodes, 2=edges, 3=faces, 4=cells/volumes

field.name: element
field.documentation: Set of elements defining the grid subset. An element is defined by a combination of objects from potentially all spaces

field.name: object
field.documentation: Set of objects defining the element

field.name: space
field.documentation: Index of the space from which that object is taken

field.name: dimension
field.documentation: Dimension of the object - using the convention 1=nodes, 2=edges, 3=faces, 4=cells/volumes

field.name: base
field.documentation: Set of bases for the grid subset. For each base, the structure describes the projection of the base vectors on the canonical frame of the grid.

field.name: tensor_covariant
field.documentation: Covariant metric tensor, given on each element of the subgrid (first dimension)

field.name: tensor_contravariant
field.documentation: Contravariant metric tensor, given on each element of the subgrid (first dimension)

field.name: metric
field.documentation: Metric of the canonical frame onto Cartesian coordinates

field.name: tensor_covariant
field.documentation: Covariant metric tensor, given on each element of the subgrid (first dimension)

field.name: tensor_contravariant
field.documentation: Contravariant metric tensor, given on each element of the subgrid (first dimension)

field.name: model
field.documentation: Transport is described by a combination of various transport models

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: flux_multiplier
field.documentation: Multiplier applied to the particule flux when adding its contribution in the expression of the heat flux : can be 0, 3/2 or 5/2

field.name: ggd
field.documentation: Transport coefficients represented using the general grid description, for various time slices. Fluxes are given in the direction perpendicular to the edges or faces of the grid (flow crossing that surface divided by its actual area). Radial fluxes are positive when they are directed away from the magnetic axis. Poloidal fluxes are positive when they are directed in such a way that they travel clockwise around the magnetic axis (poloidal plane viewed such that the centerline of the tokamak is on the left). Parallel fluxes are positive when they are co-directed with the magnetic field. Toroidal fluxes are positive if travelling counter-clockwise when looking at the plasma from above

field.name: grid_index
field.documentation: Index of the grid used to represent this quantity

field.name: grid_subset_index
field.documentation: Index of the grid subset the data is provided on. Corresponds to the index used in the grid subset definition: grid_subset(:)/identifier/index

field.name: radial
field.documentation: Radial component, one scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.

field.name: radial_coefficients
field.documentation: Interpolation coefficients for the radial component, to be used for a high precision evaluation of the physical quantity with finite elements, provided per element in the grid subset (first dimension).

field.name: diamagnetic

field.name: diamagnetic_coefficients

field.name: z_coefficients

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: dimension
field.documentation: Space dimension of the grid subset elements, using the convention 1=nodes, 2=edges, 3=faces, 4=cells/volumes

field.name: element
field.documentation: Set of elements defining the grid subset. An element is defined by a combination of objects from potentially all spaces

field.name: object
field.documentation: Set of objects defining the element

field.name: space
field.documentation: Index of the space from which that object is taken

field.name: dimension
field.documentation: Dimension of the object - using the convention 1=nodes, 2=edges, 3=faces, 4=cells/volumes

field.name: base
field.documentation: Set of bases for the grid subset. For each base, the structure describes the projection of the base vectors on the canonical frame of the grid.

field.name: tensor_covariant
field.documentation: Covariant metric tensor, given on each element of the subgrid (first dimension)

field.name: tensor_contravariant
field.documentation: Contravariant metric tensor, given on each element of the subgrid (first dimension)

field.name: metric
field.documentation: Metric of the canonical frame onto Cartesian coordinates

field.name: tensor_covariant
field.documentation: Covariant metric tensor, given on each element of the subgrid (first dimension)

field.name: tensor_contravariant
field.documentation: Contravariant metric tensor, given on each element of the subgrid (first dimension)

field.name: time_slice
field.documentation: Set of equilibria at various time slices

field.name: boundary
field.documentation: Description of the plasma boundary. The boundary can be either the real separatrix (provided by a free boundary equilibrium solver) or the 0.99x psi_norm flux surface provided by a fixed boundary equilibrium

field.name: outline
field.documentation: RZ outline of the plasma boundary

field.name: psi_norm
field.documentation: Value of the normalized poloidal flux at which the boundary is taken, the flux being normalized to its value at the separatrix (so psi_norm = 1 if the boundary is the separatrix)

field.name: psi
field.documentation: Value of the poloidal flux at which the boundary is taken

field.name: geometric_axis
field.documentation: RZ position of the geometric axis (defined as (Rmin+Rmax) / 2 and (Zmin+Zmax) / 2 of the boundary)

field.name: minor_radius
field.documentation: Minor radius of the plasma boundary (defined as (Rmax-Rmin) / 2 of the boundary)

field.name: triangularity_upper
field.documentation: Upper triangularity of the plasma boundary

field.name: triangularity_lower
field.documentation: Lower triangularity of the plasma boundary

field.name: squareness_upper_inner
field.documentation: Upper inner squareness of the plasma boundary (definition from T. Luce, Plasma Phys. Control. Fusion 55 (2013) 095009)

field.name: squareness_upper_outer
field.documentation: Upper outer squareness of the plasma boundary (definition from T. Luce, Plasma Phys. Control. Fusion 55 (2013) 095009)

field.name: squareness_lower_inner
field.documentation: Lower inner squareness of the plasma boundary (definition from T. Luce, Plasma Phys. Control. Fusion 55 (2013) 095009)

field.name: squareness_lower_outer
field.documentation: Lower outer squareness of the plasma boundary (definition from T. Luce, Plasma Phys. Control. Fusion 55 (2013) 095009)

field.name: closest_wall_point
field.documentation: Position and distance to the plasma boundary of the point of the first wall which is the closest to plasma boundary

field.name: dr_dz_zero_point
field.documentation: Outboard point on the separatrix on which dr/dz = 0 (local maximum of the major radius of the separatrix). In case of multiple local maxima, the closest one from z=z_magnetic_axis is chosen.

field.name: gap
field.documentation: Set of gaps, defined by a reference point and a direction.

field.name: name
field.documentation: Short string identifier (unique for a given device)

field.name: r
field.documentation: Major radius of the reference point

field.name: angle
field.documentation: Angle measured clockwise from radial cylindrical vector (grad R) to gap vector (pointing away from reference point)

field.name: value
field.documentation: Value of the gap, i.e. distance between the reference point and the separatrix along the gap direction

field.name: rho_tor
field.documentation: Toroidal flux coordinate at the selected plasma boundary

field.name: phi
field.documentation: Toroidal flux at the selected plasma boundary

field.name: phi_poloidal_current
field.documentation: Toroidal flux at the selected plasma boundary generated by the plasma poloidal current

field.name: contour_tree
field.documentation: Description of the topological connectivity of the poloidal flux map critical points as an undirected graph. Critical points are ether local extremum (o-points) or saddle points (x-points) of the poloidal flux map. X-points have zero gradients in orthogonal directions but are not local extremum of the poloidal flux map whilst O-points are.

field.name: node
field.documentation: Set of nodes. A contour tree node is defined by its critical type and position within the poloidal plane. A critical type of 1 references an x-point whilst a critical type of 0 or 2 references an o-point. Both X-points and O-points are rarely coincident with nodes defining the poloidal upon which the poloidal flux map is defined. The order in which the critical points are stored in the nodes array of structure is only important for the primary plasma O-point and X-points. If present, the primary plasma O-point should be placed as the first element of the nodes array of structure. If present, the primary plasma X-point should be the second element in the nodes structure

field.name: psi
field.documentation: Value of the poloidal flux at the node

field.name: levelset
field.documentation: Single poloidal flux contour including critical point (x-point only)

field.name: edges
field.documentation: Edges connect nodes to one another. A single node may connect to multiple edges such as the case where a single maximum (a hill) may topologically link to multiple minima (the floors of different valleys). For each edge (1st dimension), the index of the two connected nodes are listed (index referring to the ../node array)

field.name: constraints
field.documentation: In case of equilibrium reconstruction under constraints, measurements used to constrain the equilibrium, reconstructed values and accuracy of the fit. The names of the child nodes correspond to the following definition: the solver aims at minimizing a cost function defined as : J=1/2*sum_i [ weight_i^2 (reconstructed_i - measured_i)^2 / sigma_i^2 ]. in which sigma_i is the standard deviation of the measurement error (to be found in the IDS of the measurement)

field.name: b_field_tor_vacuum_r
field.documentation: Vacuum field times major radius in the toroidal field magnet. Positive sign means anti-clockwise when viewed from above

field.name: source
field.documentation: Path to the source data for this measurement in the IMAS data dictionary

field.name: time_measurement
field.documentation: Exact time slice used from the time array of the measurement source data. If the time slice does not exist in the time array of the source data, it means linear interpolation has been used

field.name: exact
field.documentation: Integer flag : 1 means exact data, taken as an exact input without being fitted; 0 means the equilibrium code does a least square fit

field.name: reconstructed
field.documentation: Value calculated from the reconstructed equilibrium

field.name: chi_squared
field.documentation: Squared error normalized by the variance considered in the minimization process : chi_squared = weight^2 *(reconstructed - measured)^2 / sigma^2, where sigma is the standard deviation of the measurement error

field.name: freedom_degrees_n
field.documentation: Number of degrees of freedom of the identification model

field.name: constraints_n
field.documentation: Number of constraints used (i.e. having a non-zero weight)

field.name: beta_pol
field.documentation: Poloidal beta. Defined as betap = 4 int(p dV) / [R_0 * mu_0 * Ip^2]

field.name: beta_tor
field.documentation: Toroidal beta, defined as the volume-averaged total perpendicular pressure divided by (B0^2/(2*mu0)), i.e. beta_toroidal = 2 mu0 int(p dV) / V / B0^2

field.name: beta_tor_norm
field.documentation: Normalized toroidal beta, defined as 100 * beta_tor * a[m] * B0 [T] / ip [MA]

field.name: ip
field.documentation: Plasma current (toroidal component). Positive sign means anti-clockwise when viewed from above.

field.name: area
field.documentation: Area of the LCFS poloidal cross section

field.name: surface
field.documentation: Surface area of the toroidal flux surface

field.name: length_pol
field.documentation: Poloidal length of the magnetic surface

field.documentation: Poloidal flux at the magnetic axis

field.documentation: Poloidal flux at the selected plasma boundary

field.documentation: Magnetic axis position and toroidal field

field.name: r
field.documentation: Major radius of the magnetic axis

field.name: b_field_phi
field.documentation: Total toroidal magnetic field at the magnetic axis

field.name: current_centre
field.documentation: Position and vertical velocity of the current centre

field.name: r
field.documentation: Major radius of the current center, defined as integral over the poloidal cross section of (j_tor*r*dS) / Ip

field.name: z
field.documentation: Height of the current center, defined as integral over the poloidal cross section of (j_tor*z*dS) / Ip

field.name: velocity_z
field.documentation: Vertical velocity of the current center

field.name: q_95
field.documentation: q at the 95% poloidal flux surface (only positive when toroidal current and magnetic field are in same direction)

field.name: rho_tor_norm
field.documentation: Minimum q position in normalized toroidal flux coordinate

field.name: psi_norm
field.documentation: Minimum q position in normalised poloidal flux

field.name: psi
field.documentation: Minimum q position in poloidal flux

field.name: energy_mhd
field.documentation: Plasma energy content = 3/2 * int(p,dV) with p being the total pressure (thermal + fast particles) [J]. Time-dependent; Scalar

field.name: psi_external_average
field.documentation: Average (over the plasma poloidal cross section) plasma poloidal magnetic flux produced by all external circuits (CS and PF coils, eddy currents, VS in-vessel coils), given by the following formula : int(psi_external.j_tor.dS) / Ip

field.name: v_external
field.documentation: External voltage, i.e. time derivative of psi_external_average (with a minus sign : - d_psi_external_average/d_time)

field.name: plasma_inductance
field.documentation: Plasma inductance 2 E_magnetic/Ip^2, where E_magnetic = 1/2 * int(psi.j_tor.dS) (integral over the plasma poloidal cross-section)

field.name: profiles_1d
field.documentation: Equilibrium profiles (1D radial grid) as a function of the poloidal flux

field.name: psi
field.documentation: Poloidal flux. Integral of magnetic field passing through a contour defined by the intersection of a flux surface passing through the point of interest and a Z=constant plane. If the integration surface is flat, the surface normal vector is in the increasing vertical coordinate direction, Z, namely upwards.

field.name: f_df_dpsi
field.documentation: Derivative of F w.r.t. Psi, multiplied with F

field.name: j_phi
field.documentation: Flux surface averaged toroidal current density = average(j_tor/R) / average(1/R)

field.name: j_parallel
field.documentation: Flux surface averaged approximation to parallel current density = average(j.B) / B0, where B0 = /vacuum_toroidal_field/b0

field.name: q
field.documentation: Safety factor (only positive when toroidal current and magnetic field are in same direction)

field.name: magnetic_shear
field.documentation: Magnetic shear, defined as rho_tor/q . dq/drho_tor

field.name: r_inboard
field.documentation: Radial coordinate (major radius) on the inboard side of the magnetic axis

field.name: r_outboard
field.documentation: Radial coordinate (major radius) on the outboard side of the magnetic axis

field.name: rho_tor
field.documentation: Toroidal flux coordinate = sqrt(phi/(pi*b0)), where the toroidal flux, phi, corresponds to time_slice/profiles_1d/phi, the toroidal magnetic field, b0, corresponds to that stored in vacuum_toroidal_field/b0 and pi can be found in the IMAS constants

field.name: rho_tor_norm
field.documentation: Normalized toroidal flux coordinate. The normalizing value for rho_tor_norm, is the toroidal flux coordinate at the equilibrium boundary (LCFS or 99.x % of the LCFS in case of a fixed boundary equilibium calculation). Namely (rho_tor(rho)-rho_tor(magnetic_axis)) / (rho_tor(boundary)-rho_tor(magnetic_axis))

field.name: dpsi_drho_tor
field.documentation: Derivative of Psi with respect to Rho_Tor

field.name: geometric_axis
field.documentation: RZ position of the geometric axis of the magnetic surfaces (defined as (Rmin+Rmax) / 2 and (Zmin+Zmax) / 2 of the surface)

field.name: squareness_upper_inner
field.documentation: Upper inner squareness (definition from T. Luce, Plasma Phys. Control. Fusion 55 (2013) 095009)

field.name: squareness_upper_outer
field.documentation: Upper outer squareness (definition from T. Luce, Plasma Phys. Control. Fusion 55 (2013) 095009)

field.name: squareness_lower_inner
field.documentation: Lower inner squareness (definition from T. Luce, Plasma Phys. Control. Fusion 55 (2013) 095009)

field.name: squareness_lower_outer
field.documentation: Lower outer squareness (definition from T. Luce, Plasma Phys. Control. Fusion 55 (2013) 095009)

field.name: volume
field.documentation: Volume enclosed in the flux surface

field.name: rho_volume_norm
field.documentation: Normalized square root of enclosed volume (radial coordinate). The normalizing value is the enclosed volume at the equilibrium boundary (LCFS or 99.x % of the LCFS in case of a fixed boundary equilibium calculation)

field.name: dvolume_dpsi
field.documentation: Radial derivative of the volume enclosed in the flux surface with respect to Psi

field.name: dvolume_drho_tor
field.documentation: Radial derivative of the volume enclosed in the flux surface with respect to Rho_Tor

field.name: area
field.documentation: Cross-sectional area of the flux surface

field.name: darea_dpsi
field.documentation: Radial derivative of the cross-sectional area of the flux surface with respect to psi

field.name: darea_drho_tor
field.documentation: Radial derivative of the cross-sectional area of the flux surface with respect to rho_tor

field.name: surface
field.documentation: Surface area of the toroidal flux surface

field.name: b_field_average
field.documentation: Flux surface averaged modulus of B (always positive, irrespective of the sign convention for the B-field direction).

field.name: b_field_min
field.documentation: Minimum(modulus(B)) on the flux surface (always positive, irrespective of the sign convention for the B-field direction)

field.name: b_field_max
field.documentation: Maximum(modulus(B)) on the flux surface (always positive, irrespective of the sign convention for the B-field direction)

field.name: beta_pol
field.documentation: Poloidal beta profile. Defined as betap = 4 int(p dV) / [R_0 * mu_0 * Ip^2]

field.name: profiles_2d
field.documentation: Equilibrium 2D profiles in the poloidal plane. Multiple 2D representations of the equilibrium can be stored here.

field.name: type
field.documentation: Type of profiles (distinguishes contribution from plasma, vaccum fields and total fields)

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: grid_type
field.documentation: Selection of one of a set of grid types

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: grid
field.documentation: Definition of the 2D grid (the content of dim1 and dim2 is defined by the selected grid_type)

field.name: volume_element
field.documentation: Elementary plasma volume of plasma enclosed in the cell formed by the nodes [dim1(i) dim2(j)], [dim1(i+1) dim2(j)], [dim1(i) dim2(j+1)] and [dim1(i+1) dim2(j+1)]

field.name: r
field.documentation: Values of the major radius on the grid

field.name: z
field.documentation: Values of the Height on the grid

field.name: psi
field.documentation: Values of the poloidal flux at the grid in the poloidal plane. The poloidal flux is integral of magnetic field passing through a contour defined by the intersection of a flux surface passing through the point of interest and a Z=constant plane. If the integration surface is flat, the surface normal vector is in the increasing vertical coordinate direction, Z, namely upwards.

field.name: theta
field.documentation: Values of poloidal angle on the grid. The poloidal angle is centered on the magnetic axis and oriented such that (grad rho_tor_norm, grad theta, grad phi) form a right-handed set where grad rho_tor_norm points away from the magnetic axis.

field.name: j_parallel
field.documentation: Defined as (j.B)/B0 where j and B are the current density and magnetic field vectors and B0 is the (signed) vacuum toroidal magnetic field strength at the geometric reference point (R0,Z0). It is formally not the component of the plasma current density parallel to the magnetic field

field.name: b_field_r
field.documentation: R component of the poloidal magnetic field

field.name: b_field_phi
field.documentation: Toroidal component of the magnetic field

field.name: b_field_z
field.documentation: Z component of the magnetic field

field.name: ggd
field.documentation: Set of equilibrium representations using the generic grid description

field.name: r
field.documentation: Values of the major radius on various grid subsets

field.name: grid_index
field.documentation: Index of the grid used to represent this quantity

field.name: grid_subset_index
field.documentation: Index of the grid subset the data is provided on. Corresponds to the index used in the grid subset definition: grid_subset(:)/identifier/index

field.name: values
field.documentation: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.

field.name: coefficients
field.documentation: Interpolation coefficients, to be used for a high precision evaluation of the physical quantity with finite elements, provided per element in the grid subset (first dimension).

field.documentation: Expression for calculating the residual deviation between the left and right hand side of the Grad Shafranov equation

field.name: output_flag

field.name: comment

field.name: homogeneous_time
field.documentation: This node must be filled (with 0, 1, or 2) for the IDS to be valid. If 1, the time of this IDS is homogeneous, i.e. the time values for this IDS are stored in the time node just below the root of this IDS. If 0, the time values are stored in the various time fields at lower levels in the tree. In the case only constant or static nodes are filled within the IDS, homogeneous_time must be set to 2

field.name: occurrence_type
field.documentation: Type of data contained in this occurrence

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: provider
field.documentation: Name of the person in charge of producing this data

field.name: creation_date
field.documentation: Date at which this data has been produced

field.name: version_put
field.documentation: Version of the access layer package used to PUT this IDS

field.name: data_dictionary
field.documentation: Version of Data Dictionary used to PUT this IDS

field.name: access_layer
field.documentation: Version of Access Layer used to PUT this IDS

field.name: access_layer_language
field.documentation: Programming language of the Access Layer high level API used to PUT this IDS

field.name: node
field.documentation: Set of IDS nodes for which the provenance is given. The provenance information applies to the whole structure below the IDS node. For documenting provenance information for the whole IDS, set the size of this array of structure to 1 and leave the child "path" node empty

field.name: path
field.documentation: Path of the node within the IDS, following the syntax given in the link below. If empty, means the provenance information applies to the whole IDS.

field.name: reference
field.documentation: List of references used to populate or calculate this node, identified as explained below. In case the node is the result of of a calculation / data processing, the reference is an input to the process described in the "code" structure at the root of the IDS. The reference can be an IDS (identified by a URI or a persitent identifier, see syntax in the link below) or non-IDS data imported directly from an non-IMAS database (identified by the command used to import the reference, or the persistent identifier of the data reference). Often data are obtained by a chain of processes, however only the last process input are recorded here. The full chain of provenance has then to be reconstructed recursively from the provenance information contained in the data references.

field.name: timestamp
field.documentation: Date and time (UTC) at which the reference was created, expressed in a human readable form (ISO 8601) : the format of the string shall be : YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ. Example : 2020-07-24T14:19:00Z

field.name: plugins

field.name: object
field.documentation: Set of n objects characterized by a list of centroids, volumes, and permeabilities. Optionally a full 3D description of the n volumes may be given in ../grid_ggd. Here the index for each element given in the grid_ggd should be referenced by the object set.

field.name: centroid
field.documentation: List of positions of the centroids, in Cartesian coordinates

field.name: volume
field.documentation: Volume of each element of this object

field.name: saturated_relative_permeability
field.documentation: Saturated relative magnetic permeability of each element

field.name: permeability_table_index
field.documentation: Index of permeability table to be used for each element. If not allocated or if an element is equal to EMPTY_INT, use the sibling saturated relative permeability instead ../relative_permeability, for that element

field.name: axisymmetric
field.documentation: Optional equivalent axisymmetric representation of the geometry of each element (e.g. for each iron core segment), typically used to represent iron core in axisymmetric equilibrium solvers

field.name: geometry_type
field.documentation: Type used to describe the element shape (1:'outline', 2:'rectangle', 3:'oblique', 4:'arcs of circle, 5: 'annulus', 6 : 'thick line')

field.name: outline
field.documentation: Irregular outline of the element. Repeat the first point since this is a closed contour

field.name: r
field.documentation: Major radius of the reference point (from which the alpha and beta angles are defined, marked by a + on the diagram)

field.name: z
field.documentation: Height of the reference point (from which the alpha and beta angles are defined, marked by a + on the diagram)

field.name: length_alpha
field.documentation: Length of the parallelogram side inclined with angle alpha with respect to the major radius axis

field.name: length_beta
field.documentation: Length of the parallelogram side inclined with angle beta with respect to the height axis

field.name: alpha
field.documentation: Inclination of first angle measured counter-clockwise from horizontal outwardly directed radial vector (grad R).

field.name: beta
field.documentation: Inclination of second angle measured counter-clockwise from vertically upwards directed vector (grad Z). If both alpha and beta are zero (rectangle) then the simpler rectangular elements description should be used.

field.name: arcs_of_circle
field.documentation: Description of the element contour by a set of arcs of circle. For each of these, the position of the start point is given together with the curvature radius. The end point is given by the start point of the next arc of circle.

field.name: r
field.documentation: Major radii of the start point of each arc of circle

field.name: z
field.documentation: Height of the start point of each arc of circle

field.name: curvature_radii
field.documentation: Curvature radius of each arc of circle

field.name: annulus
field.documentation: The element is an annulus of centre R, Z, with inner radius radius_inner and outer radius radius_outer

field.name: thick_line
field.documentation: The element is approximated by a rectangle defined by a central segment and a thickness in the direction perpendicular to the segment

field.name: ggd_object_index
field.documentation: Index of GGD volumic object corresponding to each element. Refers to the array /grid_ggd/space(1)/objects_per_dimension(4)/object

field.name: b_field_r
field.documentation: R component of the magnetic field at each centroid

field.name: b_field_phi
field.documentation: Toroidal component of the magnetic field at each centroid

field.name: b_field_z
field.documentation: Z component of the magnetic field at each centroid

field.name: magnetic_moment_r
field.documentation: R component of the magnetic moment of each element

field.name: magnetic_moment_phi
field.documentation: Toroidal component of the magnetic moment of each element

field.name: magnetic_moment_z
field.documentation: Z component of the magnetic moment of each element

field.name: permeability_table
field.documentation: Set of tables for relative permeability as a function of the magnetic field

field.name: b_field
field.documentation: Array of magnetic field values, for each of which the relative permeability is given

field.name: relative_permeability
field.documentation: Relative permeability as a function of the magnetic field

field.name: grid_ggd
field.documentation: GGD for describing the 3D geometry of the various objects and their elements

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: path
field.documentation: Path of the grid, including the IDS name, in case of implicit reference to a grid_ggd node described in another IDS. To be filled only if the grid is not described explicitly in this grid_ggd structure. Example syntax: #wall:2/description_ggd(1)/grid_ggd, means that the grid is located in the wall IDS, occurrence 2, with relative path description_ggd(1)/grid_ggd, using Fortran index convention (here : first index of the array)

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: geometry_type
field.documentation: Type of space geometry (0: standard, 1:Fourier, >1: Fourier with periodicity)

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: coordinates_type
field.documentation: Type of coordinates describing the physical space, for every coordinate of the space. The size of this node therefore defines the dimension of the space.

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: objects_per_dimension
field.documentation: Definition of the space objects for every dimension (from one to the dimension of the highest-dimensional objects). The index correspond to 1=nodes, 2=edges, 3=faces, 4=cells/volumes, .... For every index, a collection of objects of that dimension is described.

field.name: object
field.documentation: Set of objects for a given dimension

field.name: boundary
field.documentation: Set of (n-1)-dimensional objects defining the boundary of this n-dimensional object

field.name: neighbours
field.documentation: List of indices of the n-dimensional objects adjacent to the given n-dimensional object. An object may have multiple neighbours on a boundary

field.name: geometry
field.documentation: Geometry data associated with the object. Its detailed content is defined by ../../geometry_content. Its dimension depends on the type of object, geometry and coordinate considered.

field.name: nodes
field.documentation: List of nodes forming this object (indices to objects_per_dimension(1)%object(:) in Fortran notation)

field.name: measure
field.documentation: Measure of the space object, i.e. physical size (length for 1d, area for 2d, volume for 3d objects,...)

field.name: geometry_2d
field.documentation: 2D geometry data associated with the object. Its dimension depends on the type of object, geometry and coordinate considered. Typically, the first dimension represents the object coordinates, while the second dimension would represent the values of the various degrees of freedom of the finite element attached to the object.

field.name: geometry_content
field.documentation: Content of the ../object/geometry node for this dimension

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: dimension
field.documentation: Space dimension of the grid subset elements. This must be equal to the sum of the dimensions of the individual objects forming the element.

field.name: element
field.documentation: Set of elements defining the grid subset. An element is defined by a combination of objects from potentially all spaces

field.name: object
field.documentation: Set of objects defining the element

field.name: space
field.documentation: Index of the space from which that object is taken

field.name: base

The full chain of provenance has then to be reconstructed recursively from the provenance information contained in the data references.

field.name: timestamp
field.documentation: Date and time (UTC) at which the reference was created, expressed in a human readable form (ISO 8601) : the format of the string shall be : YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ. Example : 2020-07-24T14:19:00Z

field.name: plugins
field.documentation: Information about the plugins used to write/read this IDS. This structure is filled automatically by the Access Layer at GET/PUT time, no need to fill it via a user program.

field.name: node
field.documentation: Set of IDS nodes for which a plugin has been applied

field.name: path
field.documentation: Path of the node within the IDS, following the syntax given in the link below. If empty, means the plugin applies to the whole IDS.

field.name: put_operation
field.documentation: Plugins used to PUT a node (potentially, multiple plugins can be applied, if so they are listed by order of application)

field.name: description
field.documentation: Short description of the software (type, purpose)

field.name: parameters
field.documentation: List of the code specific parameters in XML format

field.name: library
field.documentation: List of external libraries used by the code that has produced this IDS

field.name: normalizing_quantities
field.documentation: Physical quantities used for normalization (useful to link to the original simulation/experience)

field.name: t_e
field.documentation: Electron temperature at outboard equatorial midplane of the flux surface (angle_pol = 0)

field.name: n_e
field.documentation: Electron density at outboard equatorial midplane of the flux surface (angle_pol = 0)

field.name: r
field.documentation: Major radius of the flux surface of interest, defined as (min(R)+max(R))/2

field.name: b_field_phi
field.documentation: Toroidal magnetic field at major radius r

field.name: r_minor_norm
field.documentation: normalized minor radius of the flux surface of interest = 1/2 * (max(R) - min(R))/L_ref

field.name: delongation_dr_minor_norm
field.documentation: Derivative of the elongation with respect to r_minor_norm

field.name: dgeometric_axis_r_dr_minor
field.documentation: Derivative of the major radius of the surface geometric axis with respect to r_minor

field.name: dgeometric_axis_z_dr_minor
field.documentation: Derivative of the height of the surface geometric axis with respect to r_minor

field.name: magnetic_shear_r_minor
field.documentation: Magnetic shear, defined as r_minor_norm/q . dq/dr_minor_norm (different definition from the equilibrium IDS)

field.name: pressure_gradient_norm
field.documentation: normalized pressure gradient (derivative with respect to r_minor_norm)

field.name: b_field_phi_sign
field.documentation: Sign of the toroidal magnetic field

field.name: shape_coefficients_c
field.documentation: 'c' coefficients in the formula defining the shape of the flux surface

field.name: dc_dr_minor_norm
field.documentation: Derivative of the 'c' shape coefficients with respect to r_minor_norm

field.name: shape_coefficients_s
field.documentation: 's' coefficients in the formula defining the shape of the flux surface

field.name: ds_dr_minor_norm
field.documentation: Derivative of the 's' shape coefficients with respect to r_minor_norm

field.name: radial_wavevector_norm
field.documentation: normalized radial component of the wavevector

field.name: binormal_wavevector_norm
field.documentation: normalized binormal component of the wavevector

field.name: eigenmode
field.documentation: Set of eigenmode for this wavector

field.name: poloidal_turns
field.documentation: Number of poloidal turns considered in the flux-tube simulation

field.name: growth_rate_tolerance
field.documentation: Relative tolerance on the growth rate (convergence of the simulation)

field.name: angle_pol
field.documentation: Poloidal angle grid. The angle is defined with respect to (R0,Z0) with R0=(Rmax-Rmin)/2 and Z0=(Zmax-Zmin)/2. It is increasing clockwise. So (r,theta,phi) is right-handed. theta=0 for Z=Z0 and R>R0 (LFS)

field.name: time_norm
field.documentation: normalized time of the gyrokinetic simulation

field.name: fields
field.documentation: Electrostatic potential, magnetic field and magnetic vector potential

field.name: phi_potential_perturbed_weight
field.documentation: Amplitude of the perturbed electrostatic potential normalized to the sum of amplitudes of all perturbed fields

field.name: phi_potential_perturbed_parity
field.documentation: Parity of the perturbed electrostatic potential with respect to theta = 0 (poloidal angle)

field.name: a_field_parallel_perturbed_weight
field.documentation: Amplitude of the perturbed parallel vector potential normalized to the sum of amplitudes of all perturbed fields

field.name: a_field_parallel_perturbed_parity
field.documentation: Parity of the perturbed parallel vector potential with respect to theta = 0 (poloidal angle)

field.name: b_field_parallel_perturbed_weight
field.documentation: Amplitude of the perturbed parallel magnetic field normalized to the sum of amplitudes of all perturbed fields

field.name: b_field_parallel_perturbed_parity
field.documentation: Parity of the perturbed parallel magnetic field with respect to theta = 0 (poloidal angle)

field.name: code
field.documentation: Code-specific parameters used for this eigenmode

field.name: parameters
field.documentation: List of the code specific parameters in XML format

field.name: output_flag
field.documentation: Output flag : 0 means the run is successful, other values mean some difficulty has been encountered, the exact meaning is then code specific. Negative values mean the result shall not be used.

field.name: initial_value_run
field.documentation: Flag = 1 if this is an initial value run, 0 for an eigenvalue run

field.name: include_a_field_parallel
field.documentation: Flag = 1 if fluctuations of the parallel vector potential are retained, 0 otherwise

field.name: include_b_field_parallel
field.documentation: Flag = 1 if fluctuations of the parallel magnetic field are retained, 0 otherwise

field.name: use_mhd_approximation
field.documentation: Flag = 1 if the geometric dependence of the grad-B drift is approximated to be that of the curvature drift (including the pressure gradient contribution), 0 otherwise. Using this approximation (Flag=1) is only recommended together with the neglect of parallel magnetic field fluctuations

field.name: include_coriolis_drift
field.documentation: Flag = 1 if Coriolis drift is included, 0 otherwise

field.name: include_centrifugal_effects
field.documentation: Flag = 1 if centrifugal effects are retained, 0 otherwise

field.name: collisions_pitch_only
field.documentation: Flag = 1 if only pitch-angle scattering is retained, 0 otherwise

field.name: collisions_momentum_conservation
field.documentation: Flag = 1 if the collision operator conserves momentum, 0 otherwise

field.name: collisions_energy_conservation
field.documentation: Flag = 1 if the collision operator conserves energy, 0 otherwise

field.name: collisions_finite_larmor_radius
field.documentation: Flag = 1 if finite larmor radius effects are retained in the collision operator, 0 otherwise

field.name: adiabatic_electrons
field.documentation: Flag = 1 if electrons are adiabatic, 0 otherwise

field.name: species_all
field.documentation: Physical quantities common to all species

field.name: beta_reference
field.documentation: Reference plasma beta (see detailed documentation at the root of the IDS)

field.name: velocity_phi_norm
field.documentation: normalized toroidal velocity of species (all species are assumed to have a purely toroidal velocity with a common toroidal angular frequency)

field.name: debye_length_norm
field.documentation: Debye length computed from the reference quantities (see detailed documentation at the root of the IDS)

field.name: shearing_rate_norm
field.documentation: normalized ExB shearing rate (for non-linear runs only)

field.name: angle_pol_equilibrium
field.documentation: Poloidal angle grid, from -pi to pi, on which the species dependent effective potential energy (which determines the poloidal variation of the density) is expressed. The angle is defined with respect to (R0,Z0) with R0=(Rmax-Rmin)/2 and Z0=(Zmax-Zmin)/2. It is increasing clockwise. So (r,theta,phi) is right-handed. theta=0 for Z=Z0 and R>R0 (LFS)

field.name: species
field.documentation: Set of species (including electrons) used in the calculation and related quantities

field.name: density_log_gradient_norm
field.documentation: normalized logarithmic gradient (with respect to r_minor_norm) of the density

field.name: temperature_log_gradient_norm
field.documentation: normalized logarithmic gradient (with respect to r_minor_norm) of the temperature

field.name: velocity_phi_gradient_norm
field.documentation: Normalized gradient (with respect to r_minor_norm) of the toroidal velocity

field.name: potential_energy_norm
field.documentation: normalized gradient (with respect to r_minor_norm) of the effective potential energy

field.name: potential_energy_gradient_norm
field.documentation: Effective potential energy determining the poloidal variation of the species background density

field.name: channel
field.documentation: Set of channels (detector or pixel of a camera)

field.name: name
field.documentation: Short string identifier (unique for a given device)

field.name: description
field.documentation: Description, e.g. “channel viewing the upper divertor”

field.name: geometry_type
field.documentation: Type of geometry used to describe the surface of the detector or aperture (1:'outline', 2:'circular', 3:'rectangle'). In case of 'outline', the surface is described by an outline of point in a local coordinate system defined by a centre and three unit vectors X1, X2, X3. Note that there is some flexibility here and the data provider should choose the most convenient coordinate system for the object, respecting the definitions of (X1,X2,X3) indicated below. In case of 'circular', the surface is a circle defined by its centre, radius, and normal vector oriented towards the plasma X3. In case of 'rectangle', the surface is a rectangle defined by its centre, widths in the X1 and X2 directions, and normal vector oriented towards the plasma X3.

field.name: centre
field.documentation: If geometry_type=2, coordinates of the centre of the circle. If geometry_type=1 or 3, coordinates of the origin of the local coordinate system (X1,X2,X3) describing the plane detector/aperture. This origin is located within the detector/aperture area.

field.name: phi
field.documentation: Toroidal angle (oriented counter-clockwise when viewing from above)

field.name: radius
field.documentation: Radius of the circle, used only if geometry_type = 2

field.name: x1_unit_vector
field.documentation: Components of the X1 direction unit vector in the (X,Y,Z) coordinate system, where X is the major radius axis for phi = 0, Y is the major radius axis for phi = pi/2, and Z is the height axis. The X1 vector is more horizontal than X2 (has a smaller abs(Z) component) and oriented in the positive phi direction (counter-clockwise when viewing from above).

field.name: x2_unit_vector
field.documentation: Components of the X2 direction unit vector in the (X,Y,Z) coordinate system, where X is the major radius axis for phi = 0, Y is the major radius axis for phi = pi/2, and Z is the height axis. The X2 axis is orthonormal so that uX2 = uX3 x uX1.

field.name: x3_unit_vector
field.documentation: Components of the X3 direction unit vector in the (X,Y,Z) coordinate system, where X is the major radius axis for phi = 0, Y is the major radius axis for phi = pi/2, and Z is the height axis. The X3 axis is normal to the detector/aperture plane and oriented towards the plasma.

field.name: x1_width
field.documentation: Full width of the aperture in the X1 direction, used only if geometry_type = 3

field.name: x2_width
field.documentation: Full width of the aperture in the X2 direction, used only if geometry_type = 3

field.name: outline
field.documentation: Irregular outline of the detector/aperture in the (X1, X2) coordinate system. Repeat the first point since this is a closed contour

field.name: surface
field.documentation: Surface of the detector/aperture, derived from the above geometric data

field.name: radiance

field.name: validity

field.documentation: Type of the matching element. Index = 1 : capacitor (fill capacitance); Index = 2 : stub (fill phase)

field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: phase
field.documentation: Phase delay induced by the stub

field.name: description
field.documentation: Description, e.g. “channel viewing the upper divertor”

field.name: phi
field.documentation: Toroidal angle (oriented counter-clockwise when viewing from above)

field.name: width_phi
field.documentation: Width of strap in the toroidal direction

field.name: distance_to_conductor
field.documentation: Distance to conducting wall or other conductor behind the antenna strap

field.name: geometry_type
field.documentation: Type used to describe the element shape (1:'outline', 2:'rectangle', 3:'oblique', 4:'arcs of circle, 5: 'annulus', 6 : 'thick line')

field.name: outline
field.documentation: Irregular outline of the element. Repeat the first point since this is a closed contour

field.name: r
field.documentation: Major radius of the reference point (from which the alpha and beta angles are defined, marked by a + on the diagram)

field.name: z
field.documentation: Height of the reference point (from which the alpha and beta angles are defined, marked by a + on the diagram)

field.name: length_alpha
field.documentation: Length of the parallelogram side inclined with angle alpha with respect to the major radius axis

field.name: length_beta
field.documentation: Length of the parallelogram side inclined with angle beta with respect to the height axis

field.name: alpha
field.documentation: Inclination of first angle measured counter-clockwise from horizontal outwardly directed radial vector (grad R).

field.name: beta
field.documentation: Inclination of second angle measured counter-clockwise from vertically upwards directed vector (grad Z). If both alpha and beta are zero (rectangle) then the simpler rectangular elements description should be used.

field.name: arcs_of_circle
field.documentation: Description of the element contour by a set of arcs of circle. For each of these, the position of the start point is given together with the curvature radius. The end point is given by the start point of the next arc of circle.

field.name: r
field.documentation: Major radii of the start point of each arc of circle

field.name: z
field.documentation: Height of the start point of each arc of circle

field.name: curvature_radii
field.documentation: Curvature radius of each arc of circle

field.name: annulus
field.documentation: The element is an annulus of centre R, Z, with inner radius radius_inner and outer radius radius_outer

field.name: thick_line
field.documentation: The element is approximated by a rectangle defined by a central segment and a thickness in the direction perpendicular to the segment

field.name: current
field.documentation: Root mean square current flowing along the strap

field.name: surface_current
field.documentation: Description of the IC surface current on the antenna straps and on passive components, for every time slice

field.name: m_pol
field.documentation: Poloidal mode numbers, used to describe the spectrum of the antenna current. The poloidal angle is defined from the reference point; the angle at a point (R,Z) is given by atan((Z-Zref)/(R-Rref)), where Rref=reference_point/r and Zref=reference_point/z

field.name: n_phi
field.documentation: Toroidal mode numbers, used to describe the spectrum of the antenna current. The wave vector toroidal component is defined as k_phi = n_phi grad phi where phi is the toroidal angle so that a positive n_phi means a wave propagating in the positive phi direction

field.name: spectrum
field.documentation: Spectrum of the total surface current on the antenna strap and passive components expressed in poloidal and toroidal modes

field.name: power_launched
field.documentation: Power launched into the vacuum vessel by the whole ICRH system (sum over antennas)

field.name: latency
field.documentation: Upper bound of the delay between input command received from the RT network and actuator starting to react. Applies globally to the system described by this IDS unless specific latencies (e.g. channel-specific or antenna-specific) are provided at a deeper level in the IDS structure.

field.name: segment
field.documentation: The iron core is describred as a set of segments

field.name: name
field.documentation: Short string identifier (unique for a given device)

field.name: description
field.documentation: Description, e.g. “channel viewing the upper divertor”

field.name: b_field
field.documentation: Array of magnetic field values, for each of which the relative permeability is given

field.name: permeability_relative
field.documentation: Relative permeability of the iron segment

field.name: geometry_type
field.documentation: Type used to describe the element shape (1:'outline', 2:'rectangle', 3:'oblique', 4:'arcs of circle, 5: 'annulus', 6 : 'thick line')

field.name: outline
field.documentation: Irregular outline of the element. Repeat the first point since this is a closed contour

field.name: r
field.documentation: Major radius of the reference point (from which the alpha and beta angles are defined, marked by a + on the diagram)

field.name: z
field.documentation: Height of the reference point (from which the alpha and beta angles are defined, marked by a + on the diagram)

field.name: length_alpha
field.documentation: Length of the parallelogram side inclined with angle alpha with respect to the major radius axis

field.name: length_beta
field.documentation: Length of the parallelogram side inclined with angle beta with respect to the height axis

field.name: alpha
field.documentation: Inclination of first angle measured counter-clockwise from horizontal outwardly directed radial vector (grad R).

field.name: beta
field.documentation: Inclination of second angle measured counter-clockwise from vertically upwards directed vector (grad Z). If both alpha and beta are zero (rectangle) then the simpler rectangular elements description should be used.

field.name: arcs_of_circle
field.documentation: Description of the element contour by a set of arcs of circle. For each of these, the position of the start point is given together with the curvature radius. The end point is given by the start point of the next arc of circle.

field.name: r
field.documentation: Major radii of the start point of each arc of circle

field.name: z
field.documentation: Height of the start point of each arc of circle

field.name: curvature_radii
field.documentation: Curvature radius of each arc of circle

field.name: annulus
field.documentation: The element is an annulus of centre R, Z, with inner radius radius_inner and outer radius radius_outer

field.name: thick_line
field.documentation: The element is approximated by a rectangle defined by a central segment and a thickness in the direction perpendicular to the segment

field.name: magnetization_r
field.documentation: Magnetization M of the iron segment along the major radius axis, assumed to be constant inside a given iron segment. Reminder : H = 1/mu0 * B - mur * M;

field.name: magnetization_z
field.documentation: Magnetization M of the iron segment along the vertical axis, assumed to be constant inside a given iron segment. Reminder : H = 1/mu0 * B - mur * M;

field.name: ids_properties
field.documentation: Interface Data Structure properties. This element identifies the node above as an IDS

field.name: comment
field.documentation: Any comment describing the content of this IDS

field.name: name
field.documentation: User-defined name for this IDS occurrence

field.name: homogeneous_time
field.documentation: This node must be filled (with 0, 1, or 2) for the IDS to be valid. If 1, the time of this IDS is homogeneous, i.e. the time values for this IDS are stored in the time node just below the root of this IDS. If 0, the time values are stored in the various time fields at lower levels in the tree. In the case only constant or static nodes are filled within the IDS, homogeneous_time must be set to 2

field.name: occurrence_type
field.documentation: Type of data contained in this occurrence

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: provider
field.documentation: Name of the person in charge of producing this data

field.name: creation_date
field.documentation: Date at which this data has been produced

field.name: version_put
field.documentation: Version of the access layer package used to PUT this IDS

field.name: data_dictionary
field.documentation: Version of Data Dictionary used to PUT this IDS

field.name: access_layer
field.documentation: Version of Access Layer used to PUT this IDS

field.name: access_layer_language
field.documentation: Programming language of the Access Layer high level API used to PUT this IDS

field.name: node
field.documentation: Set of IDS nodes for which the provenance is given. The provenance information applies to the whole structure below the IDS node. For documenting provenance information for the whole IDS, set the size of this array of structure to 1 and leave the child "path" node empty

field.name: path
field.documentation: Path of the node within the IDS, following the syntax given in the link below. If empty, means the provenance information applies to the whole IDS.

field.name: reference
field.documentation: List of references used to populate or calculate this node, identified as explained below. In case the node is the result of of a calculation / data processing, the reference is an input to the process described in the "code" structure at the root of the IDS. The reference can be an IDS (identified by a URI or a persitent identifier, see syntax in the link below) or non-IDS data imported directly from an non-IMAS database (identified by the command used to import the reference, or the persistent identifier of the data reference). Often data are obtained by a chain of processes, however only the last process input are recorded here. The full chain of provenance has then to be reconstructed recursively from the provenance information contained in the data references.

field.name: timestamp
field.documentation: Date and time (UTC) at which the reference was created, expressed in a human readable form (ISO 8601) : the format of the string shall be : YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ. Example : 2020-07-24T14:19:00Z

IDS.name: lh_antennas
IDS.documentation: Antenna systems for heating and current drive in the Lower Hybrid (LH) frequencies. In the definitions below, the front (or mouth) of the antenna refers to the plasma facing side of the antenna, while the back refers to the waveguides connected side of the antenna (towards the RF generators).

field.name: ids_properties
field.documentation: Interface Data Structure properties. This element identifies the node above as an IDS

field.name: comment
field.documentation: Any comment describing the content of this IDS

field.name: name
field.documentation: User-defined name for this IDS occurrence

field.name: homogeneous_time
field.documentation: This node must be filled (with 0, 1, or 2) for the IDS to be valid. If 1, the time of this IDS is homogeneous, i.e. the time values for this IDS are stored in the time node just below the root of this IDS. If 0, the time values are stored in the various time fields at lower levels in the tree. In the case only constant or static nodes are filled within the IDS, homogeneous_time must be set to 2

field.documentation: Set of IDS nodes for which the provenance is given. The provenance information applies to the whole structure below the IDS node. For documenting provenance information for the whole IDS, set the size of this array of structure to 1 and leave the child "path" node empty

field.name: path
field.documentation: Path of the node within the IDS, following the syntax given in the link below. If empty, means the provenance information applies to the whole IDS.

field.name: reference
field.documentation: List of references used to populate or calculate this node, identified as explained below. In case the node is the result of of a calculation / data processing, the reference is an input to the process described in the "code" structure at the root of the IDS. The reference can be an IDS (identified by a URI or a persitent identifier, see syntax in the link below) or non-IDS data imported directly from an non-IMAS database (identified by the command used to import the reference, or the persistent identifier of the data reference). Often data are obtained by a chain of processes, however only the last process input are recorded here. The full chain of provenance has then to be reconstructed recursively from the provenance information contained in the data references.

field.documentation: Date and time (UTC) at which the reference was created, expressed in a human readable form (ISO 8601) : the format of the string shall be : YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ. Example : 2020-07-24T14:19:00Z

field.name: reference_point
field.documentation: Reference point used to define the poloidal angle, e.g. the geometrical centre of the vacuum vessel. Used to define the poloidal refraction index under antenna/row

field.name: name
field.documentation: Short string identifier (unique for a given device)

field.name: description
field.documentation: Description, e.g. “channel viewing the upper divertor”

field.name: model_name
field.documentation: Name of the antenna model used for antenna spectrum computation

field.name: power_launched
field.documentation: Power launched from this antenna into the vacuum vessel

field.name: power_forward
field.documentation: Forward power arriving at the back of the antenna

field.name: reflection_coefficient
field.documentation: Power reflection coefficient, averaged over modules

field.name: phase_average
field.documentation: Phase difference between two neighbouring modules (average over modules), at the mouth (front) of the antenna

field.name: n_parallel_peak
field.documentation: Peak parallel refractive index of the launched wave spectrum (simple estimate based on the measured phase difference)

field.name: position
field.documentation: Position of a reference point on the antenna (allowing also tracking the possible movements of the antenna)

field.name: phi
field.documentation: Toroidal angle (oriented counter-clockwise when viewing from above)

field.name: pressure_tank
field.documentation: Pressure in the vacuum tank of the antenna

field.name: distance_to_antenna
field.documentation: Radial distance to the antenna mouth (grid for the electron density profile). 0 at antenna mouth, increasing towards the plasma

field.name: n_e
field.documentation: Electron density profile in front of the antenna

field.name: power_launched
field.documentation: Power launched from this module into the vacuum vessel

field.name: power_forward
field.documentation: Forward power arriving to the back of the module

field.name: phase
field.documentation: Phase of the forward power arriving at the back of this module

field.name: row
field.documentation: Set of horizontal rows of waveguides (corresponding to different poloidal positions). A power spectrum is provided for each row.

field.name: position
field.documentation: Position of the middle on the row

field.name: n_phi
field.documentation: Refraction index in the toroidal direction

field.name: n_pol
field.documentation: Refraction index in the poloidal direction. The poloidal angle is defined from the reference point; the angle at a point (R,Z) is given by atan((Z-Zref)/(R-Rref)), where Rref=reference_point/r and Zref=reference_point/z

field.name: power_density_spectrum_1d
field.documentation: 1D power density spectrum dP/dn_phi, as a function of time

field.name: power_density_spectrum_2d
field.documentation: 2D power density spectrum d2P/(dn_tor.dn_pol), as a function of time

field.name: time
field.documentation: Timebase for the dynamic nodes of this probe located at this level of the IDS structure

field.name: power_launched
field.documentation: Power launched into the vacuum vessel by the whole LH system (sum over antennas)

field.name: latency
field.documentation: Upper bound of the delay between input command received from the RT network and actuator starting to react. Applies globally to the system described by this IDS unless specific latencies (e.g. channel-specific or antenna-specific) are provided at a deeper level in the IDS structure.

field.name: flux_loop
field.documentation: Flux loops; partial flux loops can be described

field.name: name
field.documentation: Short string identifier (unique for a given device)

field.name: description
field.documentation: Description, e.g. “channel viewing the upper divertor”

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: position
field.documentation: List of (R,Z,phi) points defining the position of the loop (see data structure documentation FLUXLOOPposition.pdf)

field.name: phi
field.documentation: Toroidal angle (oriented counter-clockwise when viewing from above)

field.name: indices_differential
field.documentation: Indices (from the flux_loop array of structure) of the two flux loops used to build the flux difference flux(second index) - flux(first index). Use only if ../type/index = 6, leave empty otherwise

field.name: area
field.documentation: Effective area (ratio between flux and average magnetic field over the loop)

field.name: gm9
field.documentation: Integral of 1/R over the loop area (ratio between flux and magnetic rigidity R0.B0). Use only if ../type/index = 3 to 6, leave empty otherwise.

field.name: flux
field.documentation: Measured magnetic flux through loop with normal to enclosed surface determined by order of points

field.name: validity_timed
field.documentation: Indicator of the validity of the data for each time slice. 0: valid from automated processing, 1: valid and certified by the diagnostic RO; - 1 means problem identified in the data processing (request verification by the diagnostic RO), -2: invalid data, should not be used (values lower than -2 have a code-specific meaning detailing the origin of their invalidity)

field.name: validity
field.documentation: Indicator of the validity of the data for the whole acquisition period. 0: valid from automated processing, 1: valid and certified by the diagnostic RO; - 1 means problem identified in the data processing (request verification by the diagnostic RO), -2: invalid data, should not be used (values lower than -2 have a code-specific meaning detailing the origin of their invalidity)

field.name: voltage
field.documentation: Measured voltage between the loop terminals

field.name: name
field.documentation: Short string identifier (unique for a given device)

field.name: description
field.documentation: Description, e.g. “channel viewing the upper divertor”

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: position
field.documentation: R, Z, Phi position of the coil centre

field.name: phi
field.documentation: Toroidal angle (oriented counter-clockwise when viewing from above)

field.name: poloidal_angle
field.documentation: Angle of the sensor normal vector (vector parallel to the the axis of the coil, n on the diagram) with respect to horizontal plane (clockwise theta-like angle). Zero if sensor normal vector fully in the horizontal plane and oriented towards increasing major radius. Values in [0 , 2Pi]

field.name: toroidal_angle
field.documentation: Angle of the projection of the sensor normal vector (n) in the horizontal plane with the increasing R direction (i.e. grad(R)) (angle is counter-clockwise from above). Values should be taken modulo pi with values within (-pi/2,pi/2]. Zero if projected sensor normal is parallel to grad(R), pi/2 if it is parallel to grad(phi).

field.name: indices_differential
field.documentation: Indices (from the b_field_pol_probe array of structure) of the two probes used to build the field difference field(second index) - field(first index). Use only if ../type/index = 6, leave empty otherwise

field.name: bandwidth_3db
field.documentation: 3dB bandwith (first index : lower frequency bound, second index : upper frequency bound)

field.name: area
field.documentation: Area of each turn of the sensor; becomes effective area when multiplied by the turns

field.name: length
field.documentation: Length of the sensor along it's normal vector (n)

field.name: turns
field.documentation: Turns in the coil, including sign

field.name: field
field.documentation: Magnetic field component in direction of sensor normal axis (n) averaged over sensor volume defined by area and length, where n = cos(poloidal_angle)*cos(toroidal_angle)*grad(R) - sin(poloidal_angle)*grad(Z) + cos(poloidal_angle)*sin(toroidal_angle)*grad(Phi)/norm(grad(Phi))

field.name: validity_timed
field.documentation: Indicator of the validity of the data for each time slice. 0: valid from automated processing, 1: valid and certified by the diagnostic RO; - 1 means problem identified in the data processing (request verification by the diagnostic RO), -2: invalid data, should not be used (values lower than -2 have a code-specific meaning detailing the origin of their invalidity)

field.name: validity
field.documentation: Indicator of the validity of the data for the whole acquisition period. 0: valid from automated processing, 1: valid and certified by the diagnostic RO; - 1 means problem identified in the data processing (request verification by the diagnostic RO), -2: invalid data, should not be used (values lower than -2 have a code-specific meaning detailing the origin of their invalidity)

field.name: non_linear_response
field.documentation: Non-linear response of the probe (typically in case of a Hall probe)

field.name: b_field_linear
field.documentation: Array of magnetic field values (corresponding to the assumption of a linear relation between magnetic field and probe coil current), for each of which the probe non-linear response is given in ../b_field_non_linear

field.name: b_field_non_linear
field.documentation: Magnetic field value taking into account the non-linear response of the probe

field.name: b_field_pol_probe_equivalent
field.documentation: Indices of equivalent poloidal field probes (from the b_field_pol_probe array) that differ only by their toroidal position and have the same (R,Z) position and the same coil orientation (poloidal and toroidal angles). Sets of equivalent probes (i.e. sets of (R, Z, poloidal_angle and toroidal_angle) values) are grouped by the first coordinate and the coils belonging to a given set are listed along the second coordinate. As an example, if there are N probes in a poloidal cross section that are replicated at the same poloidal positions and with the same orientation at 8 toroidal positions, the matrix will be of size Nx8.

field.name: rogowski_coil
field.documentation: Set of Rogowski coils. If some of the coils form a compound Rogowski sensor, they must be entered in contiguous order

field.name: name
field.documentation: Short string identifier (unique for a given device)

field.name: description
field.documentation: Description, e.g. “channel viewing the upper divertor”

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: position
field.documentation: List of (R,Z,phi) points defining the position of the coil guiding centre. Values defining a single segment must be entered in contiguous order

field.name: phi
field.documentation: Toroidal angle (oriented counter-clockwise when viewing from above)

field.name: indices_compound
field.documentation: Indices (from the rogowski_coil array of structure) of the partial Rogowskis used to build the coumpound signal (sum of the partial Rogowski signals). Can be set to any unique integer value for each section of a compound Rogowski coil. Use only if ../measure_quantity/index = 5, leave empty otherwise

field.name: area
field.documentation: Effective area of the loop wrapped around the guiding centre. In case of multiple layers, sum of the areas of each layer

field.name: turns_per_metre
field.documentation: Number of turns per unit length. In case of multiple layers, turns are counted for a single layer

field.name: current
field.documentation: Measured current inside the Rogowski coil contour. The normal direction to the Rogowski coil is defined by the order of points in the list of guiding centre positions. The current is positive when oriented in the same direction as the normal.

field.name: shunt
field.documentation: Set of shunt resistances through which currents in the divertor structure are measured. Shunts are modelled as piecewise straight line segments in the poloidal plane.

field.name: target_index

field.name: tile_index

field.name: ip
field.documentation: Plasma current. Positive sign means anti-clockwise when viewed from above. The array of structure corresponds to a set of calculation methods (starting with the generally recommended method).
