field.name: homogeneous_time
field.documentation: This node must be filled (with 0, 1, or 2) for the IDS to be valid. If 1, the time of this IDS is homogeneous, i.e. the time values for this IDS are stored in the time node just below the root of this IDS. If 0, the time values are stored in the various time fields at lower levels in the tree. In the case only constant or static nodes are filled within the IDS, homogeneous_time must be set to 2

field.documentation: Set of IDS nodes for which the provenance is given. The provenance information applies to the whole structure below the IDS node. For documenting provenance information for the whole IDS, set the size of this array of structure to 1 and leave the child "path" node empty

field.name: path
field.documentation: Path of the node within the IDS, following the syntax given in the link below. If empty, means the provenance information applies to the whole IDS.

field.name: reference
field.documentation: List of references used to populate or calculate this node, identified as explained below. In case the node is the result of of a calculation / data processing, the reference is an input to the process described in the "code" structure at the root of the IDS. The reference can be an IDS (identified by a URI or a persitent identifier, see syntax in the link below) or non-IDS data imported directly from an non-IMAS database (identified by the command used to import the reference, or the persistent identifier of the data reference). Often data are obtained by a chain of processes, however only the last process input are recorded here. The full chain of provenance has then to be reconstructed recursively from the provenance information contained in the data references.

field.name: timestamp
field.documentation: Date and time (UTC) at which the reference was created, expressed in a human readable form (ISO 8601) : the format of the string shall be : YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ. Example : 2020-07-24T14:19:00Z

field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: path
field.documentation: Path of the grid, including the IDS name, in case of implicit reference to a grid_ggd node described in another IDS. To be filled only if the grid is not described explicitly in this grid_ggd structure. Example syntax: #wall:2/description_ggd(1)/grid_ggd, means that the grid is located in the wall IDS, occurrence 2, with relative path description_ggd(1)/grid_ggd, using Fortran index convention (here : first index of the array)

field.name: index

field.name: geometry_type

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: coordinates_type
field.documentation: Type of coordinates describing the physical space, for every coordinate of the space. The size of this node therefore defines the dimension of the space.

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: objects_per_dimension
field.documentation: Definition of the space objects for every dimension (from one to the dimension of the highest-dimensional objects). The index correspond to 1=nodes, 2=edges, 3=faces, 4=cells/volumes, .... For every index, a collection of objects of that dimension is described.

field.name: object

field.name: boundary

field.name: geometry
field.documentation: Geometry data associated with the object, its detailed content is defined by ../../geometry_content. Its dimension depends on the type of object, geometry and coordinate considered.

field.name: nodes
field.documentation: List of nodes forming this object (indices to objects_per_dimension(1)%object(:) in Fortran notation)

field.name: measure
field.documentation: Measure of the space object, i.e. physical size (length for 1d, area for 2d, volume for 3d objects,...)

field.name: geometry_2d
field.documentation: 2D geometry data associated with the object. Its dimension depends on the type of object, geometry and coordinate considered. Typically, the first dimension represents the object coordinates, while the second dimension would represent the values of the various degrees of freedom of the finite element attached to the object.

field.name: geometry_content

field.name: homogeneous_time
field.documentation: This node must be filled (with 0, 1, or 2) for the IDS to be valid. If 1, the time of this IDS is homogeneous, i.e. the time values for this IDS are stored in the time node just below the root of this IDS. If 0, the time values are stored in the various time fields at lower levels in the tree. In the case only constant or static nodes are filled within the IDS, homogeneous_time must be set to 2

field.name: path
field.documentation: Path of the node within the IDS, following the syntax given in the link below. If empty, means the provenance information applies to the whole IDS.

field.name: reference
field.documentation: List of references used to populate or calculate this node, identified as explained below. In case the node is the result of of a calculation / data processing, the reference is an input to the process described in the "code" structure at the root of the IDS. The reference can be an IDS (identified by a URI or a persitent identifier, see syntax in the link below) or non-IDS data imported directly from an non-IMAS database (identified by the command used to import the reference, or the persistent identifier of the data reference). Often data are obtained by a chain of processes, however only the last process input are recorded here. The full chain of provenance has then to be reconstructed recursively from the provenance information contained in the data references.

field.name: timestamp
field.documentation: Date and time (UTC) at which the reference was created, expressed in a human readable form (ISO 8601) : the format of the string shall be : YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ. Example : 2020-07-24T14:19:00Z

field.name: geometry_type
field.documentation: Type of geometry used to describe the surface of the detector or aperture (1:'outline', 2:'circular', 3:'rectangle'). In case of 'outline', the surface is described by an outline of point in a local coordinate system defined by a centre and three unit vectors X1, X2, X3. Note that there is some flexibility here and the data provider should choose the most convenient coordinate system for the object, respecting the definitions of (X1,X2,X3) indicated below. In case of 'circular', the surface is a circle defined by its centre, radius, and normal vector oriented towards the plasma X3. In case of 'rectangle', the surface is a rectangle defined by its centre, widths in the X1 and X2 directions, and normal vector oriented towards the plasma X3.

field.name: centre
field.documentation: If geometry_type=2, coordinates of the centre of the circle. If geometry_type=1 or 3, coordinates of the origin of the local coordinate system (X1,X2,X3) describing the plane detector/aperture. This origin is located within the detector/aperture area.

field.name: phi
field.documentation: Toroidal angle (oriented counter-clockwise when viewing from above)

field.name: radius
field.documentation: Radius of the circle, used only if geometry_type = 2

field.name: x1_unit_vector
field.documentation: Components of the X1 direction unit vector in the (X,Y,Z) coordinate system, where X is the major radius axis for phi = 0, Y is the major radius axis for phi = pi/2, and Z is the height axis. The X1 vector is more horizontal than X2 (has a smaller abs(Z) component) and oriented in the positive phi direction (counter-clockwise when viewing from above).

field.name: x2_unit_vector
field.documentation: Components of the X2 direction unit vector in the (X,Y,Z) coordinate system, where X is the major radius axis for phi = 0, Y is the major radius axis for phi = pi/2, and Z is the height axis. The X2 axis is orthonormal so that uX2 = uX3 x uX1.

field.name: x3_unit_vector
field.documentation: Components of the X3 direction unit vector in the (X,Y,Z) coordinate system, where X is the major radius axis for phi = 0, Y is the major radius axis for phi = pi/2, and Z is the height axis. The X3 axis is normal to the detector/aperture plane and oriented towards the plasma.

field.name: x1_width
field.documentation: Full width of the aperture in the X1 direction, used only if geometry_type = 3

field.name: x2_width
field.documentation: Full width of the aperture in the X2 direction, used only if geometry_type = 3

field.name: outline
field.documentation: Irregular outline of the detector/aperture in the (X1, X2) coordinate system. Repeat the first point since this is a closed contour

field.name: surface
field.documentation: Surface of the detector/aperture, derived from the above geometric data

field.name: aperture
field.documentation: Description of a set of collimating apertures

field.name: unit
field.documentation: The NBI system is described as a set of units of which the power can be controlled individually.

field.name: name
field.documentation: Short string identifier (unique for a given device)

field.name: description
field.documentation: Description, e.g. “channel viewing the upper divertor”

field.name: name
field.documentation: String identifying the species (e.g. H, D, T, ...)

field.name: power_launched
field.documentation: Power launched from this unit into the vacuum vessel

field.name: energy
field.documentation: Full energy of the injected species (acceleration of a single atom)

field.name: beam_current_fraction
field.documentation: Fractions of beam current distributed among the different energies, the first index corresponds to the fast neutrals energy (1:full, 2: half, 3: one third)

field.name: beam_power_fraction
field.documentation: Fractions of beam power distributed among the different energies, the first index corresponds to the fast neutrals energy (1:full, 2: half, 3: one third)

field.name: beamlets_group
field.documentation: Group of beamlets with common vertical and horizontal focal point. If there are no common focal points, then select small groups of beamlets such that a focal point description of the beamlets group provides a fair description. Beamlet groups are assumed to be Gaussian.

field.name: position
field.documentation: R, Z, Phi position of the beamlet group centre

field.name: phi
field.documentation: Toroidal angle (oriented counter-clockwise when viewing from above)

field.name: tangency_radius
field.documentation: Tangency radius (major radius where the central line of a NBI unit is tangent to a circle around the torus)

field.name: angle
field.documentation: Angle of inclination between a beamlet at the centre of the injection unit surface and the horiontal plane

field.name: tilting
field.documentation: In case of dynamic beam tilting (i.e. during the pulse), e.g. for some Beam Emission Spectroscopy use cases, variations of position, tangency radius and angle with respect to their static value, for various time slices

field.name: delta_position
field.documentation: Variation of the position of the beamlet group centre

field.name: phi
field.documentation: Toroidal angle (oriented counter-clockwise when viewing from above)

field.name: delta_tangency_radius
field.documentation: Variation of the tangency radius (major radius where the central line of a NBI unit is tangent to a circle around the torus)

field.name: delta_angle
field.documentation: Variation of the angle of inclination between a beamlet at the centre of the injection unit surface and the horiontal plane

field.name: direction
field.documentation: Direction of the beam seen from above the torus: -1 = clockwise; 1 = counter clockwise

field.name: width_horizontal
field.documentation: Horizontal width (dimensions of the smallest rectangle that surrounds the outer dimensions of the beamlets) of the beamlet group at the injection unit surface (or grounded grid)

field.name: width_vertical
field.documentation: Vertical width (dimensions of the smallest rectangle that surrounds the outer dimensions of the beamlets) of the beamlet group at the injection unit surface (or grounded grid)

field.name: focus
field.documentation: Describes how the beamlet group is focused. Calculations of width_min_horizontal and width_min_vertical are on a plane defined by the average normal vector of the two constituent accelerator nbi target planes.

field.name: focal_length_horizontal
field.documentation: Horizontal focal length along the beam line, i.e. the point along the centre of the beamlet-group where the beamlet-group has its minimum horizontal width

field.name: focal_length_vertical
field.documentation: Vertical focal length along the beam line, i.e. the point along the centre of the beamlet-group where the beamlet-group has its minimum vertical width

field.name: width_min_horizontal
field.documentation: The horizontal width (Full Width at Half Maximum) of the beamlets group at the horizontal focal point

field.name: width_min_vertical
field.documentation: The vertical width (Full Width at Half Maximum) of the beamlets group at the vertical focal point

field.name: divergence_component
field.documentation: Detailed information on beamlet divergence. Divergence is described as a superposition of Gaussian components with amplitide "particles_fraction" and vertical/horizontal divergence. Note that for positive ion NBI the divergence is well described by a single Gaussian

field.name: particles_fraction
field.documentation: Fraction of injected particles in the component

field.name: vertical
field.documentation: The vertical beamlet divergence of the component. Here the divergence is defined for Gaussian beams as the angel where the beam density is reduced by a factor 1/e compared to the maximum density. For non-Gaussian beams the divergence is sqrt(2)*mean((x-mean(x))**2), where x is the angle and the mean should be performed over the beam density, P(x): mean(y)=int(y*P(x)*dx).

field.name: horizontal
field.documentation: The horiztonal beamlet divergence of the component. Here the divergence is defined for Gaussian beams as the angel where the beam density is reduced by a factor 1/e compared to the maximum density. For non-Gaussian beams the divergence is sqrt(2)*mean((x-mean(x))**2), where x is the angle and the mean should be performed over the beam density, P(x): mean(y)=int(y*P(x)*dx).

field.name: phi
field.documentation: Toroidal angle (oriented counter-clockwise when viewing from above)

field.name: tangency_radii
field.documentation: Tangency radius (major radius where the central line of a beamlet is tangent to a circle around the torus), for each beamlet

field.name: angles
field.documentation: Angle of inclination between a line at the centre of a beamlet and the horizontal plane, for each beamlet

field.name: power_fractions
field.documentation: Fraction of power of a unit injected by each beamlet

field.name: source
field.documentation: Description of the surface of the ion source from which the beam is extracted

field.name: geometry_type
field.documentation: Type of geometry used to describe the surface of the detector or aperture (1:'outline', 2:'circular', 3:'rectangle'). In case of 'outline', the surface is described by an outline of point in a local coordinate system defined by a centre and three unit vectors X1, X2, X3. Note that there is some flexibility here and the data provider should choose the most convenient coordinate system for the object, respecting the definitions of (X1,X2,X3) indicated below. In case of 'circular', the surface is a circle defined by its centre, radius, and normal vector oriented towards the plasma X3. In case of 'rectangle', the surface is a rectangle defined by its centre, widths in the X1 and X2 directions, and normal vector oriented towards the plasma X3.

field.name: centre
field.documentation: If geometry_type=2, coordinates of the centre of the circle. If geometry_type=1 or 3, coordinates of the origin of the local coordinate system (X1,X2,X3) describing the plane detector/aperture. This origin is located within the detector/aperture area.

field.name: phi
field.documentation: Toroidal angle (oriented counter-clockwise when viewing from above)

field.name: radius
field.documentation: Radius of the circle, used only if geometry_type = 2

field.name: x1_unit_vector
field.documentation: Components of the X1 direction unit vector in the (X,Y,Z) coordinate system, where X is the major radius axis for phi = 0, Y is the major radius axis for phi = pi/2, and Z is the height axis. The X1 vector is more horizontal than X2 (has a smaller abs(Z) component) and oriented in the positive phi direction (counter-clockwise when viewing from above).

field.name: x2_unit_vector
field.documentation: Components of the X2 direction unit vector in the (X,Y,Z) coordinate system, where X is the major radius axis for phi = 0, Y is the major radius axis for phi = pi/2, and Z is the height axis. The X2 axis is orthonormal so that uX2 = uX3 x uX1.

field.name: x3_unit_vector
field.documentation: Components of the X3 direction unit vector in the (X,Y,Z) coordinate system, where X is the major radius axis for phi = 0, Y is the major radius axis for phi = pi/2, and Z is the height axis. The X3 axis is normal to the detector/aperture plane and oriented towards the plasma.

field.name: x1_width
field.documentation: Full width of the aperture in the X1 direction, used only if geometry_type = 3

field.name: x2_width
field.documentation: Full width of the aperture in the X2 direction, used only if geometry_type = 3

field.name: outline
field.documentation: Irregular outline of the detector/aperture in the (X1, X2) coordinate system. Repeat the first point since this is a closed contour

field.name: surface
field.documentation: Surface of the detector/aperture, derived from the above geometric data

field.name: aperture

Applies globally to the system described by this IDS unless specific latencies (e.g. channel-specific or antenna-specific) are provided at a deeper level in the IDS structure.

In case the node is the result of of a calculation / data processing, the reference is an input to the process described in the "code" structure at the root of the IDS. The reference can be an IDS (identified by a URI or a persitent identifier, see syntax in the link below) or non-IDS data imported directly from an non-IMAS database (identified by the command used to import the reference, or the persistent identifier of the data reference). Often data are obtained by a chain of processes, however only the last process input are recorded here. The full chain of provenance has then to be reconstructed recursively from the provenance information contained in the data references.

field.documentation: Array of values for the event

field.documentation: Array of flags telling, for each coordinate of the neutron_flux, whether the neutron_flux has been integrated over this coordinate (1) or not (0). If it has been integrated over a coordinate, the size related to this coordinate must be equal to 1

field.name: neutron_flux
field.documentation: Grouped neutron flux in the detector from one neutron energy bin emitted by the current plasma voxel towards the detector

field.name: event_in_detector_response_function
field.documentation: 5th dimension for the response_function Green function representing values of events measured in the detector. The type of events monitored depends on the detector and can be defined by the user. It can be energy of neutrons, or electrical signal, or time of flight ... (defined by type below)

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: values
field.documentation: Array of values for the event

field.name: response_function_integrated_flags
field.documentation: Array of flags telling, for each coordinate of the response_function, whether the response_function has been integrated over this coordinate (1) or not (0). If it has been integrated over a coordinate, the size related to this coordinate must be equal to 1

field.name: response_function
field.documentation: Number of events occurring in the detector from one neutron energy bin emitted by the current plasma voxel towards the detector

field.name: algorithm_type
field.documentation: Algorithm used to reconstruct the emissivity profile

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: rho_tor_norm
field.documentation: Normalized toroidal flux coordinate. The normalizing value for rho_tor_norm, is the toroidal flux coordinate at the equilibrium boundary (LCFS or 99.x % of the LCFS in case of a fixed boundary equilibium calculation, see time_slice/boundary in the equilibrium IDS)

field.name: psi_norm
field.documentation: Normalized poloidal flux coordinate for the reconstructed profiles, the flux being normalized to its value at the separatrix

field.name: emissivity_dd
field.documentation: Emissivity profile due to DD reactions

field.name: emissivity_dt
field.documentation: Emissivity profile due to DT reactions

field.name: emissivity_dd_accuracy
field.documentation: Accuracy profile of reconstructed DD emissivity with respect to true DD emissivity. The accuracy is obtained by comparing the reconstructed emissivity profile and the emissivity profile input to the synthetic diagnostic calculation: relative error = (reconstructed-input)/input

field.name: emissivity_dt_accuracy
field.documentation: Accuracy profile of reconstructed DT emissivity with respect to true DT emissivity. The accuracy is obtained by comparing the reconstructed emissivity profile and the emissivity profile input to the synthetic diagnostic calculation: relative error = (reconstructed-input)/input

field.name: fusion_power_dd
field.documentation: Fusion power profile due to DD reactions

field.name: fusion_power_dt
field.documentation: Fusion power profile due to DT reactions

field.name: fusion_power_dd_accuracy
field.documentation: Accuracy profile of reconstructed DD fusion power with respect to true DD fusion power. The accuracy is obtained by comparing the reconstructed profile and the profile input to the synthetic diagnostic calculation: relative error = (reconstruted-input)/input

field.name: fusion_power_dt_accuracy
field.documentation: Accuracy profile of reconstructed DT fusion power with respect to true DT fusion power. The accuracy is obtained by comparing the reconstructed profile and the profile input to the synthetic diagnostic calculation: relative error = (reconstructed-input)/input

field.name: t_i
field.documentation: Temperature profile of D and T ions (assumed to be equal)

field.name: detectors_used
field.documentation: 1 if the detector is used for the emissivity reconstruction; 0 if the detector is not used

field.name: neutron_flux_total
field.documentation: Total Neutron Flux reconstructed from the detectors signals

field.name: fusion_power
field.documentation: Fusion power reconstructed from the detectors signals

field.name: latency
field.documentation: Upper bound of the delay between physical information received by the detector and data available on the real-time (RT) network.

field.name: time_slice
field.documentation: Description of the pellets launched at various time slices. The time of this structure corresponds to the full ablation of the pellet inside the plasma.

field.name: pellet
field.documentation: Set of pellets ablated in the plasma at a given time

field.name: shape
field.documentation: Initial shape of a pellet at launch

field.name: type
field.documentation: Identifier structure for the shape type: 1-spherical; 2-cylindrical; 3-rectangular

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: size
field.documentation: Size of the pellet in the various dimensions, depending on the shape type. Spherical pellets: size(1) is the radius of the pellet. Cylindrical pellets: size(1) is the radius and size(2) is the height of the cylinder. Rectangular pellets: size(1) is the height, size(2) is the width and size(3) is the length

field.name: species
field.documentation: Set of atomic species included in the pellet composition

field.name: name
field.documentation: String identifying the species (e.g. H, D, T, ...)

field.name: density
field.documentation: Material density of the species in the pellet

field.name: fraction
field.documentation: Atomic fraction of the species in the pellet

field.name: velocity_initial
field.documentation: Initial velocity of the pellet as it enters the vaccum chamber

field.name: path_geometry
field.documentation: Geometry of the pellet path in the vaccuum chamber

field.name: phi
field.documentation: Toroidal angle (oriented counter-clockwise when viewing from above)

field.name: phi
field.documentation: Toroidal angle (oriented counter-clockwise when viewing from above)

field.name: path_profiles
field.documentation: 1-D profiles of plasma and pellet along the pellet path

field.name: distance
field.documentation: Distance along the pellet path, with the origin taken at path_geometry/first_point. Used as the main coordinate for the path_profiles structure

field.name: rho_tor_norm
field.documentation: Normalized toroidal coordinate along the pellet path

field.name: psi
field.documentation: Poloidal flux along the pellet path

field.name: velocity
field.documentation: Pellet velocity along the pellet path

field.name: n_e
field.documentation: Electron density along the pellet path

field.name: t_e
field.documentation: Electron temperature along the pellet path

field.name: ablation_rate
field.documentation: Ablation rate (electrons) along the pellet path

field.name: ablated_particles
field.documentation: Number of ablated particles (electrons) along the pellet path

field.name: rho_tor_norm_drift
field.documentation: Difference to due ExB drifts between the ablation and the final deposition locations, in terms of the normalized toroidal flux coordinate

field.name: phi
field.documentation: Toroidal angle (oriented counter-clockwise when viewing from above)

field.name: element
field.documentation: List of elements forming the gas molecule

field.name: atoms_n
field.documentation: Number of atoms of this element in the molecule

field.name: name
field.documentation: String identifying the neutral molecule (e.g. H2, D2, T2, N2, ...)

field.name: molecules_n
field.documentation: Number of molecules of the propellant gas injected in the vacuum vessel when launching the pellet

field.name: latency
field.documentation: Upper bound of the delay between input command received from the RT network and actuator starting to react. Applies globally to the system described by this IDS unless specific latencies (e.g. channel-specific or antenna-specific) are provided at a deeper level in the IDS structure.

field.name: b_field_max
field.documentation: List of values of the maximum magnetic field on the conductor surface (coordinate for current_limit_max)

field.name: temperature
field.documentation: List of values of the conductor temperature (coordinate for current_limit_max)

field.name: b_field_max_timed
field.documentation: Maximum absolute value of the magnetic field on the conductor surface

field.name: element
field.documentation: Each PF coil is comprised of a number of cross-section elements described individually and connected serially

field.name: name
field.documentation: Short string identifier (unique for a given device)

field.name: description
field.documentation: Description, e.g. “channel viewing the upper divertor”

field.name: turns_with_sign
field.documentation: Number of effective turns in the element for calculating the magnetic field from the coil/loop. Should be positive, unless the coil has elements going in opposite directions.

field.name: geometry_type
field.documentation: Type used to describe the element shape (1:'outline', 2:'rectangle', 3:'oblique', 4:'arcs of circle, 5: 'annulus', 6 : 'thick line')

field.name: outline
field.documentation: Irregular outline of the element. Repeat the first point since this is a closed contour

field.name: r
field.documentation: Major radius of the reference point (from which the alpha and beta angles are defined, marked by a + on the diagram)

field.name: z
field.documentation: Height of the reference point (from which the alpha and beta angles are defined, marked by a + on the diagram)

field.name: length_alpha
field.documentation: Length of the parallelogram side inclined with angle alpha with respect to the major radius axis

field.name: length_beta
field.documentation: Length of the parallelogram side inclined with angle beta with respect to the height axis

field.name: alpha
field.documentation: Inclination of first angle measured counter-clockwise from horizontal outwardly directed radial vector (grad R).

field.name: beta
field.documentation: Inclination of second angle measured counter-clockwise from vertically upwards directed vector (grad Z). If both alpha and beta are zero (rectangle) then the simpler rectangular elements description should be used.

field.name: arcs_of_circle
field.documentation: Description of the element contour by a set of arcs of circle. For each of these, the position of the start point is given together with the curvature radius. The end point is given by the start point of the next arc of circle.

field.name: r
field.documentation: Major radii of the start point of each arc of circle

field.name: z
field.documentation: Height of the start point of each arc of circle

field.name: curvature_radii
field.documentation: Curvature radius of each arc of circle

field.name: annulus
field.documentation: The element is an annulus of centre R, Z, with inner radius radius_inner and outer radius radius_outer

field.name: thick_line
field.documentation: The element is approximated by a rectangle defined by a central segment and a thickness in the direction perpendicular to the segment

field.name: voltage
field.documentation: Voltage on the coil terminals (Vside1-Vside2) - including additional resistors if any

field.name: force_radial
field.documentation: Radial force applied on this coil (positive when outwards)

field.name: force_vertical
field.documentation: Vertical force applied on this coil (positive when upwards)

field.name: force_radial_crushing
field.documentation: Radial crushing force applied on this coil (positive when compressive)

field.name: force_vertical_crushing
field.documentation: Vertical crushing force applied on this coil (positive when compressive)

field.name: force_limits
field.documentation: Description of force limits on the axisymmetric PF coil system

field.name: combination_matrix
field.documentation: Force limits are expressed as a linear combination of the forces on each individual coil. The weights of the linear combination are given by this matrix, while the limits are given by the sibling nodes limit_min and limit_max. Each row of this matrix corresponds to a force limit. The columns represent, for each coil, the 4 types of forces on the coil namely [coil1_radial, coil1_vertical, coil1_radial_crush, coil1_vertical_crush, coil2_radial, coil2_vertical, coil2_radial_crush, coil2_vertical_crush, ...]. There are therefore 4*coils_n columns.

field.name: limit_max
field.documentation: Maximum force limit, for each limit (line of the combination matrix). EMPTY_FLT value means unbounded

field.name: limit_min
field.documentation: Minimum force limit, for each limit (line of the combination matrix). EMPTY_FLT value means unbounded

field.name: force
field.documentation: Force (positive when upwards for a vertical force, positive when outwards for a radial force)

field.name: circuit
field.documentation: Circuits, connecting multiple PF coils to multiple supplies, defining the current and voltage relationships in the system

field.name: name
field.documentation: Short string identifier (unique for a given device)

field.name: description
field.documentation: Description, e.g. “channel viewing the upper divertor”

field.name: connections
field.documentation: Description of the supplies and coils connections (nodes) across the circuit. Nodes of the circuit are listed as the first dimension of the matrix. Supplies (listed first) and coils (listed second) are listed as the second dimension. Thus the second dimension has a size equal to (N_supplies+N_coils). N_supplies (resp. N_coils) is the total number of supplies (resp. coils) listed in the supply (resp.coil) array of structure, i.e. including also supplies/coils that are not part of the actual circuit. The (i,j) matrix elements are 1 if the j-th supply or coil side is connected to the i-th node by its positive side, -1 if connected by its negative side, or 0 if not connected.

field.name: voltage
field.documentation: Voltage on the circuit between the sides of the group of supplies (only for circuits with a single supply or in which supplies are grouped)

field.name: current
field.documentation: Current in the circuit between the sides of the group of supplies (only for circuits with a single supply or in which supplies are grouped)

field.name: name
field.documentation: Short string identifier (unique for a given device)

field.name: description
field.documentation: Description, e.g. “channel viewing the upper divertor”

field.name: type
field.documentation: Type of the supply; TBD add free description of non-linear power supplies

field.name: filter_numerator
field.documentation: Coefficients of the numerator, in increasing order : a0 + a1*s + ... + an*s^n; used for a linear supply description

field.name: filter_denominator
field.documentation: Coefficients of the denominator, in increasing order : b0 + b1*s + ... + bm*s^m; used for a linear supply description

field.name: current_limiter_gain
field.documentation: Gain to prevent overcurrent in a linear model of the supply

field.name: energy_limit_max
field.documentation: Maximum energy to be dissipated in the supply during a pulse

field.name: nonlinear_model
field.documentation: Description of the nonlinear transfer function of the supply

field.name: current
field.documentation: Current at the supply output, defined positive if it flows from point 1 to point 2 in the circuit connected to the supply (outside the supply)

field.name: latency
field.documentation: Upper bound of the delay between input command received from the RT network and actuator starting to react. Applies globally to the system described by this IDS unless specific latencies (e.g. channel-specific or antenna-specific) are provided at a deeper level in the IDS structure.

The reference can be an IDS (identified by a URI or a persitent identifier, see syntax in the link below) or non-IDS data imported directly from an non-IMAS database (identified by the command used to import the reference, or the persistent identifier of the data reference). In case the node is the result of of a calculation / data processing, the reference is an input to the process described in the "code" structure at the root of the IDS. The reference can be an IDS (identified by a URI or a persitent identifier, see syntax in the link below) or non-IDS data imported directly from an non-IMAS database (identified by the command used to import the reference, or the persistent identifier of the data reference). Often data are obtained by a chain of processes, however only the last process input are recorded here. The full chain of provenance has then to be reconstructed recursively from the provenance information contained in the data references.

field.name: timestamp
field.documentation: Date and time (UTC) at which the reference was created, expressed in a human readable form (ISO 8601) : the format of the string shall be : YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ. Example : 2020-07-24T14:19:00Z

field.documentation: Information about the plugins used to write/read this IDS. This structure is filled automatically by the Access Layer at GET/PUT time, no need to fill it via a user program.

field.documentation: Set of IDS nodes for which a plugin has been applied

field.name: path
field.documentation: Path of the node within the IDS, following the syntax given in the link below. If empty, means the plugin applies to the whole IDS.

field.documentation: Plugins used to PUT a node (potentially, multiple plugins can be applied, if so they are listed by order of application)

field.name: b_field_stray
field.documentation: Stray magnetic field at plasma position

field.name: b_field_perpendicular
field.documentation: Perpendicular magnetic field at plasma position. b_field_perpendicular = sqrt(b_field_stray^2+b_field_eddy^2)

field.name: connection_length
field.documentation: Average length of open magnetic field lines. In the case of fully closed field lines, connection_length = 1

field.name: ip
field.documentation: Total plasma current (toroidal component). Positive sign means anti-clockwise when viewed from above.

field.name: t_e_volume_average
field.documentation: Volume averaged electron temperature (average over the plasma volume up to the LCFS)

field.name: n_e_volume_average
field.documentation: Volume averaged electron density (average over the plasma volume up to the LCFS)

field.name: ion
field.documentation: Quantities related to the different ion species, in the sense of isonuclear or isomolecular sequences

field.name: element
field.documentation: List of elements forming the atom or molecule

field.name: atoms_n
field.documentation: Number of atoms of this element in the molecule

field.name: z_ion
field.documentation: Ion charge (of the dominant ionization state; lumped ions are allowed), volume averaged over plasma radius

field.name: name
field.documentation: String identifying the species (e.g. H+, D+, T+, He+2, C+, D2, DT, CD4, ...)

field.name: neutral_index
field.documentation: Index of the corresponding neutral species in the ../../neutral array

field.name: t_i_volume_average
field.documentation: Volume averaged temperature of this ion species (averaged over the plasma volume up to the LCFS)

field.name: n_i_volume_average
field.documentation: Volume averaged density of this ion species (averaged over the plasma volume up to the LCFS)

field.documentation: List of all R, Z grid positions (from ../grid) containing field lines encoutering Townsend condition or being closed field lines

field.name: starting_positions
field.documentation: Starting position to initiate field line tracing, for each field line

field.name: e_field_townsend
field.documentation: Townsend electric field along each field line

field.name: e_field_parallel

field.name: pressure

field.name: open_fraction

IDS.name: plasma_profiles
IDS.documentation: Plasma profiles (core and/or edge). This IDS is a prototype based on the merge of core_profiles, edge_profiles and the MHD IDS, for testing purposes only at this stage. It contains magnetic field maps to describe magnetic field fluctuations, while the equilibrium magnetic field is described in the equilibrium IDS

field.name: ids_properties
field.documentation: Interface Data Structure properties. This element identifies the node above as an IDS

field.name: comment
field.documentation: Any comment describing the content of this IDS

field.name: name
field.documentation: User-defined name for this IDS occurrence

field.name: homogeneous_time
field.documentation: This node must be filled (with 0, 1, or 2) for the IDS to be valid. If 1, the time of this IDS is homogeneous, i.e. the time values for this IDS are stored in the time node just below the root of this IDS. If 0, the time values are stored in the various time fields at lower levels in the tree. In the case only constant or static nodes are filled within the IDS, homogeneous_time must be set to 2

field.name: vacuum_toroidal_field
field.documentation: Characteristics of the vacuum toroidal field (used in rho_tor definition and in the normalization of current densities)

field.name: r0
field.documentation: Reference major radius where the vacuum toroidal magnetic field is given (usually a fixed position such as the middle of the vessel at the equatorial midplane)

field.name: b0
field.documentation: Vacuum toroidal field at R0 [T]; Positive sign means anti-clockwise when viewing from above. The product R0B0 must be consistent with the b_tor_vacuum_r field of the tf IDS.

field.name: midplane
field.documentation: Choice of midplane definition (use the lowest index number if more than one value is relevant)

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: global_quantities
field.documentation: Various global quantities derived from the profiles

field.name: ip
field.documentation: Total plasma current (toroidal component). Positive sign means anti-clockwise when viewed from above.

field.name: current_non_inductive
field.documentation: Total non-inductive current (toroidal component). Positive sign means anti-clockwise when viewed from above.

field.name: current_bootstrap
field.documentation: Bootstrap current (toroidal component). Positive sign means anti-clockwise when viewed from above.

field.name: v_loop
field.documentation: LCFS loop voltage (positive value drives positive ohmic current that flows anti-clockwise when viewed from above)

field.name: li_3
field.documentation: Internal inductance. The li_3 definition is used, i.e. li_3 = 2/R0/mu0^2/Ip^2 * int(Bp^2 dV).

field.name: beta_tor
field.documentation: Toroidal beta, defined as the volume-averaged total perpendicular pressure divided by (B0^2/(2*mu0)), i.e. beta_toroidal = 2 mu0 int(p dV) / V / B0^2

field.name: beta_tor_norm
field.documentation: Normalised toroidal beta, defined as 100 * beta_tor * a[m] * B0 [T] / ip [MA]

field.name: beta_pol
field.documentation: Poloidal beta. Defined as betap = 4 int(p dV) / [R_0 * mu_0 * Ip^2]

field.name: energy_diamagnetic
field.documentation: Plasma energy content = 3/2 * integral over the plasma volume of the total perpendicular pressure

field.name: z_eff_resistive
field.documentation: Volume average plasma effective charge, estimated from the flux consumption in the ohmic phase

field.name: t_e_peaking
field.documentation: Electron temperature peaking factor, defined as the Te value at the magnetic axis divided by the volume averaged Te (average over the plasma volume up to the LCFS)

field.name: t_i_average_peaking
field.documentation: Ion temperature (averaged over ion species and states) peaking factor, defined as the Ti value at the magnetic axis divided by the volume averaged Ti (average over the plasma volume up to the LCFS)

field.name: resistive_psi_losses
field.documentation: Resistive part of the poloidal flux losses, defined as the volume-averaged scalar product of the electric field and the ohmic current density, normalized by the plasma current and integrated in time from the beginning of the plasma discharge: int ( (int(E_field_phi.j_ohm_phi) dV) / Ip ) dt)

field.name: ejima
field.documentation: Ejima coefficient : resistive psi losses divided by (mu0*R*Ip). See S. Ejima et al, Nuclear Fusion, Vol.22, No.10 (1982), 1313

field.name: t_e_volume_average
field.documentation: Volume averaged electron temperature (average over the plasma volume up to the LCFS)

field.name: n_e_volume_average
field.documentation: Volume averaged electron density (average over the plasma volume up to the LCFS)

field.name: ion
field.documentation: Quantities related to the different ion species, in the sense of isonuclear or isomolecular sequences. The set of ion species of this array must be the same as the one defined in profiles_1d/ion, at the time slice indicated in ion_time_slice

field.name: t_i_volume_average
field.documentation: Volume averaged temperature of this ion species (averaged over the plasma volume up to the LCFS)

field.name: n_i_volume_average
field.documentation: Volume averaged density of this ion species (averaged over the plasma volume up to the LCFS)

field.name: ion_time_slice
field.documentation: Time slice of the profiles_1d array used to define the ion composition of the global_quantities/ion array.

field.name: profiles_1d
field.documentation: Radial profiles for various time slices. Flux averaged profiles in the closed field line region (grid/rho_pol_norm <= 1) and taking local values on outboard equatorial mid-plane when in the SOL (grid/rho_pol_norm > 1)

field.name: grid
field.documentation: Radial grid. Note that some of the radial coordinates listed above are undefined outside the last closed flux surface, thus they must be filled with EMPTY_FLOAT values in such locations

field.name: psi
field.documentation: Poloidal magnetic flux. Integral of magnetic field passing through a contour defined by the intersection of a flux surface passing through the point of interest and a Z=constant plane. If the integration surface is flat, the surface normal vector is in the increasing vertical coordinate direction, Z, namely upwards.

field.name: rho_tor_norm
field.documentation: Normalised toroidal flux coordinate. The normalizing value for rho_tor_norm, is the toroidal flux coordinate at the equilibrium boundary (LCFS or 99.x % of the LCFS in case of a fixed boundary equilibium calculation, see time_slice/boundary/b_flux_pol_norm in the equilibrium IDS)

field.name: rho_tor
field.documentation: Toroidal flux coordinate. rho_tor = sqrt(b_flux_tor/(pi*b0)) ~ sqrt(pi*r^2*b0/(pi*b0)) ~ r [m]. The toroidal field used in its definition is indicated under vacuum_toroidal_field/b0

field.name: volume
field.documentation: Volume enclosed inside the magnetic surface

field.name: area
field.documentation: Cross-sectional area of the flux surface

field.name: surface
field.documentation: Surface area of the toroidal flux surface

field.name: psi_magnetic_axis
field.documentation: Value of the poloidal magnetic flux at the magnetic axis (useful to normalize the psi array values when the radial grid doesn't go from the magnetic axis to the plasma boundary)

field.name: psi_boundary
field.documentation: Value of the poloidal magnetic flux at the plasma boundary (useful to normalize the psi array values when the radial grid doesn't go from the magnetic axis to the plasma boundary)

field.name: temperature_validity
field.documentation: Indicator of the validity of the temperature profile. 0: valid from automated processing, 1: valid and certified by the RO; - 1 means problem identified in the data processing (request verification by the RO), -2: invalid data, should not be used

field.name: temperature_fit
field.documentation: Information on the fit used to obtain the temperature profile

field.name: measured
field.documentation: Measured values. Units are: as_parent for a local measurement, as_parent.m for a line integrated measurement.

field.name: source
field.documentation: Path to the source data for each measurement in the IMAS data dictionary, e.g. ece/channel(i)/t_e for the electron temperature on the i-th channel in the ECE IDS

field.name: time_measurement
field.documentation: Exact time slices used from the time array of the measurement source data. If the time slice does not exist in the time array of the source data, it means linear interpolation has been used

field.name: time_measurement_slice_method
field.documentation: Method used to slice the data : index = 0 means using exact time slice of the measurement, 1 means linear interpolation, ...

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: time_measurement_width
field.documentation: In case the measurements are averaged over a time interval, this node is the full width of this time interval (empty otherwise). In case the slicing/averaging method doesn't use a hard time interval cutoff, this width is the characteristic time span of the slicing/averaging method. By convention, the time interval starts at time_measurement-time_width and ends at time_measurement.

field.name: local
field.documentation: Integer flag : 1 means local measurement, 0 means line-integrated measurement

field.name: rho_tor_norm
field.documentation: Normalised toroidal flux coordinate of each measurement (local value for a local measurement, minimum value reached by the line of sight for a line measurement)

field.name: rho_pol_norm
field.documentation: Normalised poloidal flux coordinate of each measurement (local value for a local measurement, minimum value reached by the line of sight for a line measurement)

field.name: weight
field.documentation: Weight given to each measured value

field.name: reconstructed
field.documentation: Value reconstructed from the fit. Units are: as_parent for a local measurement, as_parent.m for a line integrated measurement.

field.name: chi_squared
field.documentation: Squared error normalized by the weighted standard deviation considered in the minimization process : chi_squared = weight^2 *(reconstructed - measured)^2 / sigma^2, where sigma is the standard deviation of the measurement error

field.name: parameters
field.documentation: List of the fit specific parameters in XML format

field.name: density_validity
field.documentation: Indicator of the validity of the density profile. 0: valid from automated processing, 1: valid and certified by the RO; - 1 means problem identified in the data processing (request verification by the RO), -2: invalid data, should not be used

field.name: density_fit
field.documentation: Information on the fit used to obtain the density profile

field.documentation: Collisionality normalised to the bounce frequency

field.name: z_min
field.documentation: Minimum Z of the charge state bundle

field.name: z_max
field.documentation: Maximum Z of the charge state bundle (equal to z_min if no bundle)

field.name: z_average
field.documentation: Average Z of the charge state bundle, volume averaged over the plasma radius (equal to z_min if no bundle), = sum (Z*x_z) where x_z is the relative concentration of a given charge state in the bundle, i.e. sum(x_z) = 1 over the bundle.

field.name: z_square_average
field.documentation: Average Z square of the charge state bundle, volume averaged over the plasma radius (equal to z_min squared if no bundle), = sum (Z^2*x_z) where x_z is the relative concentration of a given charge state in the bundle, i.e. sum(x_z) = 1 over the bundle.

field.name: z_average_1d
field.documentation: Average charge profile of the charge state bundle (equal to z_min if no bundle), = sum (Z*x_z) where x_z is the relative concentration of a given charge state in the bundle, i.e. sum(x_z) = 1 over the bundle.

field.name: z_average_square_1d
field.documentation: Average square charge profile of the charge state bundle (equal to z_min squared if no bundle), = sum (Z^2*x_z) where x_z is the relative concentration of a given charge state in the bundle, i.e. sum(x_z) = 1 over the bundle.

field.name: ionisation_potential
field.documentation: Cumulative and average ionisation potential to reach a given bundle. Defined as sum (x_z* (sum of Epot from z'=0 to z-1)), where Epot is the ionisation potential of ion Xz_+, and x_z is the relative concentration of a given charge state in the bundle, i.e. sum(x_z) = 1 over the bundle.

field.name: pressure_ion_total
field.documentation: Total (sum over ion species) thermal ion pressure

field.name: j_total
field.documentation: Total parallel current density = average(jtot.B) / B0, where B0 = plasma_profiles/Vacuum_Toroidal_Field/ B0

field.name: current_parallel_inside
field.documentation: Parallel current driven inside the flux surface. Cumulative surface integral of j_total

field.name: j_phi
field.documentation: Total toroidal current density = average(j_phi/R) / average(1/R)

field.name: j_ohmic
field.documentation: Ohmic parallel current density = average(J_Ohmic.B) / B0, where B0 = plasma_profiles/Vacuum_Toroidal_Field/ B0

field.name: j_non_inductive
field.documentation: Non-inductive (includes bootstrap) parallel current density = average(jni.B) / B0, where B0 = plasma_profiles/Vacuum_Toroidal_Field/ B0

field.name: j_bootstrap
field.documentation: Bootstrap current density = average(J_Bootstrap.B) / B0, where B0 = plasma_profiles/Vacuum_Toroidal_Field/ B0

field.name: e_field
field.documentation: Electric field, averaged on the magnetic surface. E.g for the parallel component, average(E.B) / B0, using plasma_profiles/vacuum_toroidal_field/b0

field.name: phi_potential
field.documentation: Electrostatic potential, averaged on the magnetic flux surface

field.name: rotation_frequency_tor_sonic
field.documentation: Derivative of the flux surface averaged electrostatic potential with respect to the poloidal flux, multiplied by (-1/2pi). This quantity is the toroidal angular rotation frequency due to the ExB drift, introduced in formula (43) of Hinton and Wong, Physics of Fluids 3082 (1985), also referred to as sonic flow in regimes in which the toroidal velocity is dominant over the poloidal velocity

field.name: magnetic_shear
field.documentation: Magnetic shear, defined as rho_tor/q . dq/drho_tor

field.name: volume_element
field.documentation: Elementary plasma volume of plasma enclosed in the cell formed by the nodes [dim1(i) dim2(j)], [dim1(i+1) dim2(j)], [dim1(i) dim2(j+1)] and [dim1(i+1) dim2(j+1)]

Ionisation states (or other types of states) must be differentiated at the state level below. field.name: grid_ggd
field.documentation: Grid (using the Generic Grid Description), for various time slices. The timebase of this array of structure must be a subset of the ggd timebase

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: path
field.documentation: Path of the grid, including the IDS name, in case of implicit reference to a grid_ggd node described in another IDS. To be filled only if the grid is not described explicitly in this grid_ggd structure. Example syntax: #wall:2/description_ggd(1)/grid_ggd, means that the grid is located in the wall IDS, occurrence 2, with relative path description_ggd(1)/grid_ggd, using Fortran index convention (here : first index of the array)

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: geometry_type
field.documentation: Type of space geometry (0: standard, 1:Fourier, >1: Fourier with periodicity)

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: coordinates_type
field.documentation: Type of coordinates describing the physical space, for every coordinate of the space. The size of this node therefore defines the dimension of the space.

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: objects_per_dimension
field.documentation: Definition of the space objects for every dimension (from one to the dimension of the highest-dimensional objects). The index correspond to 1=nodes, 2=edges, 3=faces, 4=cells/volumes, .... For every index, a collection of objects of that dimension is described.

field.name: object
field.documentation: Set of objects for a given dimension

field.name: boundary
field.documentation: Set of (n-1)-dimensional objects defining the boundary of this n-dimensional object

field.name: neighbours
field.documentation: List of indices of the n-dimensional objects adjacent to the given n-dimensional object. An object can possibly have multiple neighbours on a boundary

field.name: geometry
field.documentation: Geometry data associated with the object, its detailed content is defined by ../../geometry_content. Its dimension depends on the type of object, geometry and coordinate considered.

field.name: nodes
field.documentation: List of nodes forming this object (indices to objects_per_dimension(1)%object(:) in Fortran notation)

field.name: measure
field.documentation: Measure of the space object, i.e. physical size (length for 1d, area for 2d, volume for 3d objects,...)

field.name: geometry_2d
field.documentation: 2D geometry data associated with the object. Its dimension depends on the type of object, geometry and coordinate considered. Typically, the first dimension represents the object coordinates, while the second dimension would represent the values of the various degrees of freedom of the finite element attached to the object.

field.name: geometry_content
field.documentation: Content of the ../object/geometry node for this dimension

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: dimension
field.documentation: Space dimension of the grid subset elements, using the convention 1=nodes, 2=edges, 3=faces, 4=cells/volumes

field.name: element
field.documentation: Set of elements defining the grid subset. An element is defined by a combination of objects from potentially all spaces

field.name: object
field.documentation: Set of objects defining the element

field.name: space
field.documentation: Index of the space from which that object is taken

field.name: dimension
field.documentation: Dimension of the object - using the convention 1=nodes, 2=edges, 3=faces, 4=cells/volumes

field.name: base
field.documentation: Set of bases for the grid subset. For each base, the structure describes the projection of the base vectors on the canonical frame of the grid.

field.name: tensor_covariant
field.documentation: Covariant metric tensor, given on each element of the subgrid (first dimension)

field.name: tensor_contravariant
field.documentation: Contravariant metric tensor, given on each element of the subgrid (first dimension)

field.name: metric
field.documentation: Metric of the canonical frame onto Cartesian coordinates

field.name: tensor_covariant
field.documentation: Covariant metric tensor, given on each element of the subgrid (first dimension)

field.name: tensor_contravariant
field.documentation: Contravariant metric tensor, given on each element of the subgrid (first dimension)

field.name: ggd
field.documentation: Plasma quantities represented using the general grid description, for various time slices. The timebase of this array of structure must be a subset of the ggd_fast timebase (only if the ggd_fast array of structure is used)

field.name: temperature
field.documentation: Temperature, given on various grid subsets

field.name: grid_index
field.documentation: Index of the grid used to represent this quantity

field.name: grid_subset_index
field.documentation: Index of the grid subset the data is provided on. Corresponds to the index used in the grid subset definition: grid_subset(:)/identifier/index

field.name: values

If not all indices of a given node are used, they must be listed explicitly e.g. rows_uri(i) = pf_active:1/coil(i) will refer to a list of indices of the occurrence 1 of the pf_active IDS of this data entry. If the rows correspond to all indices of a given vector it is sufficient to give a single URI where this vector is denoted using the (:) implicit notation, e.g. rows_uri(1) = /grid_ggd(3)/grid_subset(2)/elements(:).

field.name: homogeneous_time
field.documentation: This node must be filled (with 0, 1, or 2) for the IDS to be valid. If 1, the time of this IDS is homogeneous, i.e. the time values for this IDS are stored in the time node just below the root of this IDS. If 0, the time values are stored in the various time fields at lower levels in the tree. In the case only constant or static nodes are filled within the IDS, homogeneous_time must be set to 2

field.documentation: Path of the node within the IDS, following the syntax given in the link below. If empty, means the provenance information applies to the whole IDS.

field.name: reference
field.documentation: List of references used to populate or calculate this node, identified as explained below. In case the node is the result of of a calculation / data processing, the reference is an input to the process described in the "code" structure at the root of the IDS. The reference can be an IDS (identified by a URI or a persitent identifier, see syntax in the link below) or non-IDS data imported directly from an non-IMAS database (identified by the command used to import the reference, or the persistent identifier of the data reference). Often data are obtained by a chain of processes, however only the last process input are recorded here. The full chain of provenance has then to be reconstructed recursively from the provenance information contained in the data references.

field.name: timestamp
field.documentation: Date and time (UTC) at which the reference was created, expressed in a human readable form (ISO 8601) : the format of the string shall be : YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ. Example : 2020-07-24T14:19:00Z

field.documentation: Vacuum toroidal field at R0 [T]; Positive sign means anti-clockwise when viewing from above. The product R0B0 must be consistent with the b_tor_vacuum_r field of the tf IDS.

field.name: grid_ggd
field.documentation: Grid (using the Generic Grid Description), for various time slices. The timebase of this array of structure must be a subset of the ggd timebases

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.documentation: Path of the grid, including the IDS name, in case of implicit reference to a grid_ggd node described in another IDS. To be filled only if the grid is not described explicitly in this grid_ggd structure. Example syntax: #wall:2/description_ggd(1)/grid_ggd, means that the grid is located in the wall IDS, occurrence 2, with relative path description_ggd(1)/grid_ggd, using Fortran index convention (here : first index of the array)

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: geometry_type
field.documentation: Type of space geometry (0: standard, 1:Fourier, >1: Fourier with periodicity)

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: coordinates_type
field.documentation: Type of coordinates describing the physical space, for every coordinate of the space. The size of this node therefore defines the dimension of the space.

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: objects_per_dimension
field.documentation: Definition of the space objects for every dimension (from one to the dimension of the highest-dimensional objects). The index correspond to 1=nodes, 2=edges, 3=faces, 4=cells/volumes, .... For every index, a collection of objects of that dimension is described.

field.name: object
field.documentation: Set of objects for a given dimension

field.name: boundary
field.documentation: Set of (n-1)-dimensional objects defining the boundary of this n-dimensional object

field.name: neighbours
field.documentation: List of indices of the n-dimensional objects adjacent to the given n-dimensional object. An object can possibly have multiple neighbours on a boundary

field.name: geometry
field.documentation: Geometry data associated with the object, its detailed content is defined by ../../geometry_content. Its dimension depends on the type of object, geometry and coordinate considered.

field.name: nodes
field.documentation: List of nodes forming this object (indices to objects_per_dimension(1)%object(:) in Fortran notation)

field.name: measure
field.documentation: Measure of the space object, i.e. physical size (length for 1d, area for 2d, volume for 3d objects,...)

field.name: geometry_2d
field.documentation: 2D geometry data associated with the object. Its dimension depends on the type of object, geometry and coordinate considered. Typically, the first dimension represents the object coordinates, while the second dimension would represent the values of the various degrees of freedom of the finite element attached to the object.

field.name: geometry_content
field.documentation: Content of the ../object/geometry node for this dimension

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: dimension
field.documentation: Space dimension of the grid subset elements, using the convention 1=nodes, 2=edges, 3=faces, 4=cells/volumes

field.name: element
field.documentation: Set of elements defining the grid subset. An element is defined by a combination of objects from potentially all spaces

field.name: object
field.documentation: Set of objects defining the element

field.name: space
field.documentation: Index of the space from which that object is taken

field.name: dimension
field.documentation: Dimension of the object - using the convention 1=nodes, 2=edges, 3=faces, 4=cells/volumes

field.name: base
field.documentation: Set of bases for the grid subset. For each base, the structure describes the projection of the base vectors on the canonical frame of the grid.

field.name: tensor_covariant
field.documentation: Covariant metric tensor, given on each element of the subgrid (first dimension)

field.name: identifier
field.documentation: Source term identifier (process causing this source term)

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: species
field.documentation: Species causing this source term (if relevant, e.g. a particular ion or neutral state in case of line radiation)

field.name: type
field.documentation: Species type. index=1 for electron; index=2 for ion species in a single/average state (refer to ion structure); index=3 for ion species in a particular state (refer to ion/state structure); index=4 for neutral species in a single/average state (refer to neutral structure); index=5 for neutral species in a particular state (refer to neutral/state structure); index=6 for neutron; index=7 for photon

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: ion
field.documentation: Description of the ion or neutral species, used if type/index = 2 or 3

field.name: element
field.documentation: List of elements forming the atom or molecule

field.name: atoms_n
field.documentation: Number of atoms of this element in the molecule

field.name: z_ion
field.documentation: Ion charge (of the dominant ionization state; lumped ions are allowed)

field.name: name
field.documentation: String identifying ion (e.g. H+, D+, T+, He+2, C+, ...)

field.name: state
field.documentation: Quantities related to the different states of the species (ionization, energy, excitation, ...)

field.name: z_min
field.documentation: Minimum Z of the charge state bundle (z_min = z_max = 0 for a neutral)

field.name: z_max
field.documentation: Maximum Z of the charge state bundle (equal to z_min if no bundle)

field.name: name
field.documentation: String identifying ion state (e.g. C+, C+2 , C+3, C+4, C+5, C+6, ...)

field.name: electron_configuration
field.documentation: Configuration of atomic orbitals of this state, e.g. 1s2-2s1

field.name: vibrational_mode
field.documentation: Vibrational mode of this state, e.g. "A_g". Need to define, or adopt a standard nomenclature.

field.name: neutral
field.documentation: Description of the neutral species, used if type/index = 4 or 5

field.name: neutral_type
field.documentation: Neutral type, in terms of energy. ID =1: cold; 2: thermal; 3: fast; 4: NBI

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: global_quantities
field.documentation: Total source quantities integrated over the plasma volume or surface

field.name: power
field.documentation: Total power coupled to the plasma

field.name: total_ion_particles
field.documentation: Total ion particle source (summed over ion species)

field.name: total_ion_power
field.documentation: Total power coupled to ion species (summed over ion species)

field.name: profiles_1d
field.documentation: Source profiles for various time slices. Source terms are positive (resp. negative) when there is a gain (resp. a loss) to the considered channel.

field.name: grid
field.documentation: Radial grid. Note that some of the radial coordinates listed above are undefined outside the last closed flux surface, thus they must be filled with EMPTY_FLOAT values in such locations

field.name: psi
field.documentation: Poloidal magnetic flux. Integral of magnetic field passing through a contour defined by the intersection of a flux surface passing through the point of interest and a Z=constant plane. If the integration surface is flat, the surface normal vector is in the increasing vertical coordinate direction, Z, namely upwards.

field.name: rho_tor_norm
field.documentation: Normalised toroidal flux coordinate. The normalizing value for rho_tor_norm, is the toroidal flux coordinate at the equilibrium boundary (LCFS or 99.x % of the LCFS in case of a fixed boundary equilibium calculation, see time_slice/boundary/b_flux_pol_norm in the equilibrium IDS)

field.name: rho_tor
field.documentation: Toroidal flux coordinate. rho_tor = sqrt(b_flux_tor/(pi*b0)) ~ sqrt(pi*r^2*b0/(pi*b0)) ~ r [m]. The toroidal field used in its definition is indicated under vacuum_toroidal_field/b0

field.name: volume
field.documentation: Volume enclosed inside the magnetic surface

field.name: area
field.documentation: Cross-sectional area of the flux surface

field.name: surface
field.documentation: Surface area of the toroidal flux surface

field.name: psi_magnetic_axis
field.documentation: Value of the poloidal magnetic flux at the magnetic axis (useful to normalize the psi array values when the radial grid doesn't go from the magnetic axis to the plasma boundary)

field.name: psi_boundary
field.documentation: Value of the poloidal magnetic flux at the plasma boundary (useful to normalize the psi array values when the radial grid doesn't go from the magnetic axis to the plasma boundary)

field.name: explicit_part
field.documentation: Explicit part of the source term

field.name: momentum_phi
field.documentation: Source term for total toroidal momentum equation

field.name: torque_phi_inside
field.documentation: Toroidal torque inside the flux surface. Cumulative volume integral of the source term for the total toroidal momentum equation

field.name: momentum_phi_j_cross_b_field
field.documentation: Contribution to the toroidal momentum source term (already included in the momentum_tor node) corresponding to the toroidal torques onto the thermal plasma due to Lorentz force associated with radial currents. These currents appear as return-currents (enforcing quasi-neutrality, div(J)=0) balancing radial currents of non-thermal particles, e.g. radial currents of fast and trapped neutral-beam-ions.

field.name: conductivity_parallel

field.documentation: Multiplier applied to the particule flux when adding its contribution in the expression of the heat flux : can be 0, 3/2 or 5/2

field.name: profiles_1d
field.documentation: Transport coefficient profiles for various time slices. The transport of particles, energy and momentum is described by diffusion coefficients, D, and convection velocities, v. In 1D (radial) equations, these are defined by the total fluxes of particles, energy and momentum, across a flux surface given by : V' [-D Y' <|grad(rho_tor_norm)|^2> + v Y <|grad(rho_tor_norm)|>], where Y represents the particles, energy and momentum density, respectively, while V is the volume inside a flux surface, the primes denote derivatives with respect to rho_tor_norm and < X > is the flux surface average of a quantity X. This formulation remains valid when changing simultaneously rho_tor_norm into rho_tor in the gradient terms and in the derivatives denoted by the prime. The average flux stored in the IDS as sibling of D and v is the total flux described above divided by the flux surface area V' <|grad(rho_tor_norm)|>. Note that the energy flux includes the energy transported by the particle flux, in this form: Q = V' [- n D (T)' <|grad(rho_tor_norm)|^2> + v (nT) <|grad(rho_tor_norm)|>] + flux_multiplier * T * particle_flux. Fluxes and convection are positive (resp. negative) when outwards i.e. towards the LCFS (resp. inwards i.e. towards the magnetic axes).

field.name: ggd
field.documentation: Transport coefficients represented using the general grid description, for various time slices. Fluxes are given in the direction perpendicular to the edges or faces of the grid (flow crossing that surface divided by its actual area). Radial fluxes are positive when they are directed away from the magnetic axis. Poloidal fluxes are positive when they are directed in such a way that they travel clockwise around the magnetic axis (poloidal plane viewed such that the centerline of the tokamak is on the left). Parallel fluxes are positive when they are co-directed with the magnetic field. Toroidal fluxes are positive if travelling counter-clockwise when looking at the plasma from above

field.name: grid_index
field.documentation: Index of the grid used to represent this quantity

field.documentation: Index of the grid subset the data is provided on. Corresponds to the index used in the grid subset definition: grid_subset(:)/identifier/index

field.name: values
field.documentation: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.

field.name: reference_type
field.documentation: Reference type: 0:relative (don't use for the moment, to be defined later when segments are introduced in the IDS structure); 1: absolute: the reference time trace is provided in the reference/data node

Lower and upper are taken in the strict mathematical sense, without considering absolute values of the data

field.name: steering_angle_tor
field.documentation: Steering angle of the EC beam away from the poloidal plane that is increasing towards the positive phi axis, angle_tor=arcsin(k_phi/k), where k_phi is the component of the wave vector in the phi direction and k is the length of the wave vector. Here the term wave vector refers to the mean wave vector in the EC beam

field.documentation: Reference name (e.g. in the native pulse schedule system of the device)

field.name: reference
field.documentation: Reference waveform. Caution : error bars of the reference/data node are not used in the usual sense, instead they are used to describe the control envelope, with a meaning depending on the chosen envelope_type option.

field.name: reference_type
field.documentation: Reference type: 0:relative (don't use for the moment, to be defined later when segments are introduced in the IDS structure); 1: absolute: the reference time trace is provided in the reference/data node

field.name: envelope_type
field.documentation: Envelope type: 0:relative: means that the envelope upper and lower bound values are defined respectively as reference.data * reference.data_error_upper and reference.data * reference.data_error_lower. 1: absolute: the envelope upper and lower bound values are given respectively by reference/data_error_upper and reference/data_error_lower. Lower are upper are taken in the strict mathematical sense, without considering absolute values of the data
