field.name: ids_properties
field.documentation: Interface Data Structure properties. This element identifies the node above as an IDS

field.name: comment
field.documentation: Any comment describing the content of this IDS

field.name: name
field.documentation: User-defined name for this IDS occurrence

field.name: homogeneous_time
field.documentation: This node must be filled (with 0, 1, or 2) for the IDS to be valid. If 1, the time of this IDS is homogeneous, i.e. the time values for this IDS are stored in the time node just below the root of this IDS. If 0, the time values are stored in the various time fields at lower levels in the tree. In the case only constant or static nodes are filled within the IDS, homogeneous_time must be set to 2

field.name: occurrence_type
field.documentation: Type of data contained in this occurrence

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: provider
field.documentation: Name of the person in charge of producing this data

field.name: creation_date
field.documentation: Date at which this data has been produced

field.name: version_put
field.documentation: Version of the access layer package used to PUT this IDS

field.name: data_dictionary
field.documentation: Version of Data Dictionary used to PUT this IDS

field.name: access_layer
field.documentation: Version of Access Layer used to PUT this IDS

field.name: access_layer_language
field.documentation: Programming language of the Access Layer high level API used to PUT this IDS

field.name: node
field.documentation: Set of IDS nodes for which the provenance is given. The provenance information applies to the whole structure below the IDS node. For documenting provenance information for the whole IDS, set the size of this array of structure to 1 and leave the child "path" node empty

field.name: path
field.documentation: Path of the node within the IDS, following the syntax given in the link below. If empty, means the provenance information applies to the whole IDS.

field.name: reference
field.documentation: List of references used to populate or calculate this node, identified as explained below. In case the node is the result of of a calculation / data processing, the reference is an input to the process described in the "code" structure at the root of the IDS. The reference can be an IDS (identified by a URI or a persitent identifier, see syntax in the link below) or non-IDS data imported directly from an non-IMAS database (identified by the command used to import the reference, or the persistent identifier of the data reference). Often data are obtained by a chain of processes, however only the last process input are recorded here. The full chain of provenance has then to be reconstructed recursively from the provenance information contained in the data references.

field.name: timestamp
field.documentation: Date and time (UTC) at which the reference was created, expressed in a human readable form (ISO 8601) : the format of the string shall be : YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ. Example : 2020-07-24T14:19:00Z

field.name: plugins

field.name: vacuum_toroidal_field
field.documentation: Characteristics of the vacuum toroidal field (used in rho_tor definition)

field.name: r0
field.documentation: Reference major radius where the vacuum toroidal magnetic field is given (usually a fixed position such as the middle of the vessel at the equatorial midplane)

field.name: b0
field.documentation: Vacuum toroidal field at R0 [T]; Positive sign means anti-clockwise when viewing from above. The product R0B0 must be consistent with the b_tor_vacuum_r field of the tf IDS.

field.name: grid_ggd
field.documentation: Grid (using the Generic Grid Description), for various time slices. The timebase of this array of structure must be a subset of the process/ggd timebases

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: path
field.documentation: Path of the grid, including the IDS name, in case of implicit reference to a grid_ggd node described in another IDS. To be filled only if the grid is not described explicitly in this grid_ggd structure. Example syntax: #wall:2/description_ggd(1)/grid_ggd, means that the grid is located in the wall IDS, occurrence 2, with relative path description_ggd(1)/grid_ggd, using Fortran index convention (here : first index of the array)

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: geometry_type
field.documentation: Type of space geometry (0: standard, 1:Fourier, >1: Fourier with periodicity)

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: coordinates_type
field.documentation: Type of coordinates describing the physical space, for every coordinate of the space. The size of this node therefore defines the dimension of the space.

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: objects_per_dimension
field.documentation: Definition of the space objects for every dimension (from one to the dimension of the highest-dimensional objects). The index correspond to 1=nodes, 2=edges, 3=faces, 4=cells/volumes, .... For every index, a collection of objects of that dimension is described.

field.name: object
field.documentation: Set of objects for a given dimension

field.name: boundary
field.documentation: Set of (n-1)-dimensional objects defining the boundary of this n-dimensional object

field.name: neighbours
field.documentation: List of indices of the n-dimensional objects adjacent to the given n-dimensional object. An object can possibly have multiple neighbours on a boundary

field.name: geometry
field.documentation: Geometry data associated with the object, its detailed content is defined by ../../geometry_content. Its dimension depends on the type of object, geometry and coordinate considered.

field.name: nodes
field.documentation: List of nodes forming this object (indices to objects_per_dimension(1)%object(:) in Fortran notation)

field.name: measure
field.documentation: Measure of the space object, i.e. physical size (length for 1d, area for 2d, volume for 3d objects,...)

field.name: geometry_2d
field.documentation: 2D geometry data associated with the object. Its dimension depends on the type of object, geometry and coordinate considered. Typically, the first dimension represents the object coordinates, while the second dimension would represent the values of the various degrees of freedom of the finite element attached to the object.

field.name: geometry_content
field.documentation: Content of the ../object/geometry node for this dimension

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: dimension
field.documentation: Space dimension of the grid subset elements, using the convention 1=nodes, 2=edges, 3=faces, 4=cells/volumes

field.name: element
field.documentation: Set of elements defining the grid subset. An element is defined by a combination of objects from potentially all spaces

field.name: object
field.documentation: Set of objects defining the element

field.name: space
field.documentation: Index of the space from which that object is taken

field.name: dimension
field.documentation: Dimension of the object - using the convention 1=nodes, 2=edges, 3=faces, 4=cells/volumes

field.name: base
field.documentation: Set of bases for the grid subset. For each base, the structure describes the projection of the base vectors on the canonical frame of the grid.

field.name: tensor_covariant
field.documentation: Covariant metric tensor, given on each element of the subgrid (first dimension)

field.name: tensor_contravariant
field.documentation: Contravariant metric tensor, given on each element of the subgrid (first dimension)

field.name: metric
field.documentation: Metric of the canonical frame onto Cartesian coordinates

field.name: tensor_covariant
field.documentation: Covariant metric tensor, given on each element of the subgrid (first dimension)

field.name: tensor_contravariant
field.documentation: Contravariant metric tensor, given on each element of the subgrid (first dimension)

field.name: process
field.documentation: Set of emission processes. The radiation characteristics are described at the level of the originating entity. For instance describe line radiation from neutrals under profiles_1d/neutral. Line and recombination radiation under profiles_1d/ion. Bremsstrahlung radiation under profiles_1d/neutral and ion ...

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: inside_lcfs
field.documentation: Emissions from the core plasma, inside the last closed flux surface

field.name: power
field.documentation: Total power emitted by all species

field.name: power_ion_total
field.documentation: Total power emitted by all ion species

field.name: power_neutral_total
field.documentation: Total power emitted by all neutral species

field.name: inside_vessel
field.documentation: Total emissions inside the vacuum vessel

field.name: power
field.documentation: Total power emitted by all species

field.name: power_ion_total
field.documentation: Total power emitted by all ion species

field.name: power_neutral_total
field.documentation: Total power emitted by all neutral species

field.name: profiles_1d
field.documentation: Emissivity radial profiles for various time slices

field.name: rho_tor_norm
field.documentation: Normalized toroidal flux coordinate. The normalizing value for rho_tor_norm, is the toroidal flux coordinate at the equilibrium boundary (LCFS or 99.x % of the LCFS in case of a fixed boundary equilibium calculation, see time_slice/boundary/b_flux_pol_norm in the equilibrium IDS)

field.name: rho_tor
field.documentation: Toroidal flux coordinate = sqrt(phi/(pi*b0)), where the toroidal magnetic field, b0, corresponds to that stored in vacuum_toroidal_field/b0 and pi can be found in the IMAS constants

field.name: psi
field.documentation: Poloidal magnetic flux. Integral of magnetic field passing through a contour defined by the intersection of a flux surface passing through the point of interest and a Z=constant plane. If the integration surface is flat, the surface normal vector is in the increasing vertical coordinate direction, Z, namely upwards.

field.name: volume
field.documentation: Volume enclosed inside the magnetic surface

field.name: area
field.documentation: Cross-sectional area of the flux surface

field.name: surface
field.documentation: Surface area of the toroidal flux surface

field.name: psi_magnetic_axis
field.documentation: Value of the poloidal magnetic flux at the magnetic axis (useful to normalize the psi array values when the radial grid doesn't go from the magnetic axis to the plasma boundary)

field.name: psi_boundary
field.documentation: Value of the poloidal magnetic flux at the plasma boundary (useful to normalize the psi array values when the radial grid doesn't go from the magnetic axis to the plasma boundary)

field.name: power_inside
field.documentation: Radiated power from inside the flux surface (volume integral of the emissivity inside the flux surface)

field.name: power_inside_ion_total
field.documentation: Total power from ion species (summed over ion species) inside the flux surface (volume integral of the emissivity inside the flux surface)

field.name: power_inside_neutral_total
field.documentation: Total power from ion species (summed over neutral species) inside the flux surface (volume integral of the emissivity inside the flux surface)

field.name: ion
field.documentation: Process terms related to the different ion species

field.name: element
field.documentation: List of elements forming the atom or molecule

field.name: atoms_n
field.documentation: Number of atoms of this element in the molecule

field.name: z_ion
field.documentation: Ion charge (of the dominant ionization state; lumped ions are allowed)

field.name: name
field.documentation: String identifying ion (e.g. H+, D+, T+, He+2, C+, ...)

field.name: neutral_index
field.documentation: Index of the corresponding neutral species in the ../../neutral array

field.name: power_inside

field.name: index

field.name: power_inside

field.name: grid_index
field.documentation: Index of the grid used to represent this quantity

field.name: grid_subset_index
field.documentation: Index of the grid subset the data is provided on. Corresponds to the index used in the grid subset definition: grid_subset(:)/identifier/index

field.name: values
field.documentation: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.

field.name: coefficients
field.documentation: Interpolation coefficients, to be used for a high precision evaluation of the physical quantity with finite elements, provided per element in the grid subset (first dimension).

field.name: geometry_type
field.documentation: Type of geometry used to describe the surface of the detector or aperture (1:'outline', 2:'circular', 3:'rectangle'). In case of 'outline', the surface is described by an outline of point in a local coordinate system defined by a centre and three unit vectors X1, X2, X3. Note that there is some flexibility here and the data provider should choose the most convenient coordinate system for the object, respecting the definitions of (X1,X2,X3) indicated below. In case of 'circular', the surface is a circle defined by its centre, radius, and normal vector oriented towards the plasma X3. In case of 'rectangle', the surface is a rectangle defined by its centre, widths in the X1 and X2 directions, and normal vector oriented towards the plasma X3.

field.name: centre
field.documentation: If geometry_type=2, coordinates of the centre of the circle. If geometry_type=1 or 3, coordinates of the origin of the local coordinate system (X1,X2,X3) describing the plane detector/aperture. This origin is located within the detector/aperture area.

field.name: phi
field.documentation: Toroidal angle (oriented counter-clockwise when viewing from above)

field.name: radius
field.documentation: Radius of the circle, used only if geometry_type = 2

field.name: x1_unit_vector
field.documentation: Components of the X1 direction unit vector in the (X,Y,Z) coordinate system, where X is the major radius axis for phi = 0, Y is the major radius axis for phi = pi/2, and Z is the height axis. The X1 vector is more horizontal than X2 (has a smaller abs(Z) component) and oriented in the positive phi direction (counter-clockwise when viewing from above).

field.name: x2_unit_vector
field.documentation: Components of the X2 direction unit vector in the (X,Y,Z) coordinate system, where X is the major radius axis for phi = 0, Y is the major radius axis for phi = pi/2, and Z is the height axis. The X2 axis is orthonormal so that uX2 = uX3 x uX1.

field.name: x3_unit_vector
field.documentation: Components of the X3 direction unit vector in the (X,Y,Z) coordinate system, where X is the major radius axis for phi = 0, Y is the major radius axis for phi = pi/2, and Z is the height axis. The X3 axis is normal to the detector/aperture plane and oriented towards the plasma.

field.name: x1_width
field.documentation: Full width of the aperture in the X1 direction, used only if geometry_type = 3

field.name: x2_width
field.documentation: Full width of the aperture in the X2 direction, used only if geometry_type = 3

field.name: outline
field.documentation: Irregular outline of the detector/aperture in the (X1, X2) coordinate system. Repeat the first point since this is a closed contour

field.name: surface
field.documentation: Surface of the detector/aperture, derived from the above geometric data

field.documentation: Components of the X1 direction unit vector in the (X,Y,Z) coordinate system, where X is the major radius axis for phi = 0, Y is the major radius axis for phi = pi/2, and Z is the height axis. The X1 vector is more horizontal than X2 (has a smaller abs(Z) component) and oriented in the positive phi direction (counter-clockwise when viewing from above).

field.name: x2_unit_vector

field.name: geometry_type
field.documentation: Type of geometry used to describe the surface of the detector or aperture (1:'outline', 2:'circular', 3:'rectangle'). In case of 'outline', the surface is described by an outline of point in a local coordinate system defined by a centre and three unit vectors X1, X2, X3. Note that there is some flexibility here and the data provider should choose the most convenient coordinate system for the object, respecting the definitions of (X1,X2,X3) indicated below. In case of 'circular', the surface is a circle defined by its centre, radius, and normal vector oriented towards the plasma X3. In case of 'rectangle', the surface is a rectangle defined by its centre, widths in the X1 and X2 directions, and normal vector oriented towards the plasma X3.

field.documentation: If geometry_type=2, coordinates of the centre of the circle. If geometry_type=1 or 3, coordinates of the origin of the local coordinate system (X1,X2,X3) describing the plane detector/aperture. This origin is located within the detector/aperture area.

field.documentation: Set of coordinate identifiers, coordinates on which the markers are represented

field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.documentation: Weight of the markers, i.e. number of real particles represented by each marker. The dimension of the vector correspond to the number of markers

field.documentation: Position of the markers in the set of coordinates. The first dimension corresponds to the number of markers, the second dimension to the set of coordinates

field.name: orbit_integrals
field.documentation: Integrals along the markers orbit. These dimensionless expressions are of the form: (1/tau) integral (f(n_tor,m_pol,k,eq,...) dt) from time - tau to time, where tau is the transit/trapping time of the marker and f() a dimensionless function (phase factor,drift,etc) of the equilibrium (e.g. q) and perturbation (Fourier harmonics n_tor,m_pol and bounce harmonic k) along the particles orbits. In fact the integrals are taken during the last orbit of each marker at the time value of the time node below

field.name: expressions
field.documentation: List of the expressions f(n_tor,m_pol,k,q,...) used in the orbit integrals

field.name: n_phi
field.documentation: Array of toroidal mode numbers, where quantities vary as exp(i.n_phi.phi) and phi runs anticlockwise when viewed from above

field.name: m_pol
field.documentation: Array of poloidal mode numbers, where quantities vary as exp(-i.m_pol.theta) and theta is the angle defined by the choice of ../../coordinate_identifier, with its centre at the magnetic axis recalled at the root of this IDS

field.name: orbit_integrals_instant
field.documentation: Integrals/quantities along the markers orbit. These dimensionless expressions are of the form: (1/tau) integral ( f(eq) dt) from time - tau to time_orbit for different values of time_orbit in the interval from time - tau to time, where tau is the transit/trapping time of the marker and f(eq) a dimensionless function (phase, drift,q,etc) of the equilibrium along the markers orbits. The integrals are taken during the last orbit of each marker at the time value of the time node below

field.name: expressions
field.documentation: List of the expressions f(eq) used in the orbit integrals

field.name: time_orbit
field.documentation: Time array along the markers last orbit

field.name: n_i_total_over_n_e
field.documentation: Ratio of total ion density (sum over species and charge states) over electron density. (thermal+non-thermal)

field.name: momentum_phi
field.documentation: Total plasma toroidal momentum, summed over ion species and electrons

field.name: p_i_total
field.documentation: Total ion pressure (sum over the ion species)

field.name: p_i_total_fast_perpendicular
field.documentation: Fast (non-thermal) total ion (sum over the ion species) perpendicular pressure

field.name: p_i_total_fast_parallel
field.documentation: Fast (non-thermal) total ion (sum over the ion species) parallel pressure

field.name: j_total
field.documentation: Total parallel current density = average(jtot.B) / B0, where B0 = Core_Profiles/Vacuum_Toroidal_Field/ B0

field.name: j_phi
field.documentation: Total toroidal current density = average(j_phi/R) / average(1/R)

field.name: j_ohmic
field.documentation: Ohmic parallel current density = average(J_Ohmic.B) / B0, where B0 = Core_Profiles/Vacuum_Toroidal_Field/ B0

field.name: j_non_inductive
field.documentation: Non-inductive (includes bootstrap) parallel current density = average(jni.B) / B0, where B0 = Core_Profiles/Vacuum_Toroidal_Field/ B0

field.name: j_bootstrap
field.documentation: Bootstrap current density = average(J_Bootstrap.B) / B0, where B0 = Core_Profiles/Vacuum_Toroidal_Field/ B0

field.name: e_field_parallel
field.documentation: Parallel electric field = average(E.B) / B0, where Core_Profiles/Vacuum_Toroidal_Field/ B0

field.name: magnetic_shear
field.documentation: Magnetic shear, defined as rho_tor/q . dq/drho_tor

field.name: psi_star_pre_crash
field.documentation: Psi* = psi - phi, just before the sawtooth crash

field.name: psi_star_post_crash
field.documentation: Psi* = psi - phi, after the sawtooth crash

field.name: diagnostics
field.documentation: Detailed information about the sawtooth characteristics

field.name: magnetic_shear_q1
field.documentation: Magnetic shear at surface q = 1, defined as rho_tor/q . dq/drho_tor

field.name: rho_tor_norm_q1
field.documentation: Normalized toroidal flux coordinate at surface q = 1

field.name: rho_tor_norm_inversion
field.documentation: Normalized toroidal flux coordinate at inversion radius

field.name: rho_tor_norm_mixing
field.documentation: Normalized toroidal flux coordinate at mixing radius

field.name: previous_crash_trigger
field.documentation: Previous crash trigger. Flag indicating whether a crash condition has been satisfied : 0 = no crash. N(>0) = crash triggered due to condition N

field.name: previous_crash_time
field.documentation: Time at which the previous sawtooth crash occured

field.documentation: Set of channels (detector or pixel of a camera)

field.documentation: Short string identifier (unique for a given device)

field.name: description
field.documentation: Description, e.g. “channel viewing the upper divertor”

field.name: geometry_type
field.documentation: Type of geometry used to describe the surface of the detector or aperture (1:'outline', 2:'circular', 3:'rectangle'). In case of 'outline', the surface is described by an outline of point in a local coordinate system defined by a centre and three unit vectors X1, X2, X3. Note that there is some flexibility here and the data provider should choose the most convenient coordinate system for the object, respecting the definitions of (X1,X2,X3) indicated below. In case of 'circular', the surface is a circle defined by its centre, radius, and normal vector oriented towards the plasma X3. In case of 'rectangle', the surface is a rectangle defined by its centre, widths in the X1 and X2 directions, and normal vector oriented towards the plasma X3.

field.name: centre
field.documentation: If geometry_type=2, coordinates of the centre of the circle. If geometry_type=1 or 3, coordinates of the origin of the local coordinate system (X1,X2,X3) describing the plane detector/aperture. This origin is located within the detector/aperture area.

field.name: phi
field.documentation: Toroidal angle (oriented counter-clockwise when viewing from above)

field.name: radius
field.documentation: Radius of the circle, used only if geometry_type = 2

field.name: x1_unit_vector
field.documentation: Components of the X1 direction unit vector in the (X,Y,Z) coordinate system, where X is the major radius axis for phi = 0, Y is the major radius axis for phi = pi/2, and Z is the height axis. The X1 vector is more horizontal than X2 (has a smaller abs(Z) component) and oriented in the positive phi direction (counter-clockwise when viewing from above).

field.name: x2_unit_vector
field.documentation: Components of the X2 direction unit vector in the (X,Y,Z) coordinate system, where X is the major radius axis for phi = 0, Y is the major radius axis for phi = pi/2, and Z is the height axis. The X2 axis is orthonormal so that uX2 = uX3 x uX1.

field.name: x3_unit_vector
field.documentation: Components of the X3 direction unit vector in the (X,Y,Z) coordinate system, where X is the major radius axis for phi = 0, Y is the major radius axis for phi = pi/2, and Z is the height axis. The X3 axis is normal to the detector/aperture plane and oriented towards the plasma.

field.name: x1_width
field.documentation: Full width of the aperture in the X1 direction, used only if geometry_type = 3

field.name: x2_width
field.documentation: Full width of the aperture in the X2 direction, used only if geometry_type = 3

field.name: outline
field.documentation: Irregular outline of the detector/aperture in the (X1, X2) coordinate system. Repeat the first point since this is a closed contour

field.name: surface
field.documentation: Surface of the detector/aperture, derived from the above geometric data

field.name: etendue_method
field.documentation: Method used to calculate the etendue. Index = 0 : exact calculation with a 4D integral; 1 : approximation with first order formula (detector surface times solid angle subtended by the apertures); 2 : other methods

field.name: x2_curvature

field.name: wavelength_lower
field.documentation: Lower bound of the filter wavelength range

field.name: wavelength_upper

field.name: photon_absorption

field.name: energy_band

field.name: lower_bound
field.documentation: Lower bound of the energy band

field.name: upper_bound
field.documentation: Upper bound of the energy band

field.name: energies
field.documentation: Array of discrete energy values inside the band

field.name: detection_efficiency
field.documentation: Probability of detection of a photon impacting the detector as a function of its energy

field.name: brightness
field.documentation: Power flux received by the detector, per unit solid angle and per unit area (i.e. power divided by the etendue), in multiple energy bands if available from the detector

field.name: power

field.documentation: Indicator of the validity of the channel as a function of time (0 means valid, negative values mean non-valid)

field.name: validity

field.name: latency
field.documentation: Upper bound of the delay between physical information received by the detector and data available on the real-time (RT) network.

If 0, the time values are stored in the various time fields at lower levels in the tree. In the case only constant or static nodes are filled within the IDS, homogeneous_time must be set to 2

field.documentation: Path of the node within the IDS, following the syntax given in the link below. If empty, means the provenance information applies to the whole IDS.

field.name: reference
field.documentation: List of references used to populate or calculate this node, identified as explained below. In case the node is the result of of a calculation / data processing, the reference is an input to the process described in the "code" structure at the root of the IDS. The reference can be an IDS (identified by a URI or a persitent identifier, see syntax in the link below) or non-IDS data imported directly from an non-IMAS database (identified by the command used to import the reference, or the persistent identifier of the data reference). Often data are obtained by a chain of processes, however only the last process input are recorded here. The full chain of provenance has then to be reconstructed recursively from the provenance information contained in the data references.

field.name: timestamp

field.name: etendue
field.documentation: Etendue (geometric extent) of the optical system

field.name: etendue_method
field.documentation: Method used to calculate the etendue. Index = 0 : exact calculation with a 4D integral; 1 : approximation with first order formula (detector surface times solid angle subtended by the apertures); 2 : other methods

field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.documentation: Set of channels (detector or pixel of a camera)

field.documentation: Pixel dimension in each direction (horizontal, vertical)

field.name: pixel_n
field.documentation: Number of pixels in each direction (horizontal, vertical)

field.name: detector_dimensions
field.documentation: Total detector dimension in each direction (horizontal, vertical)

field.name: detector
field.documentation: Description of the front face of the micro channel plate

field.name: geometry_type
field.documentation: Type of geometry used to describe the surface of the detector or aperture (1:'outline', 2:'circular', 3:'rectangle'). In case of 'outline', the surface is described by an outline of point in a local coordinate system defined by a centre and three unit vectors X1, X2, X3. Note that there is some flexibility here and the data provider should choose the most convenient coordinate system for the object, respecting the definitions of (X1,X2,X3) indicated below. In case of 'circular', the surface is a circle defined by its centre, radius, and normal vector oriented towards the plasma X3. In case of 'rectangle', the surface is a rectangle defined by its centre, widths in the X1 and X2 directions, and normal vector oriented towards the plasma X3.

field.name: centre
field.documentation: If geometry_type=2, coordinates of the centre of the circle. If geometry_type=1 or 3, coordinates of the origin of the local coordinate system (X1,X2,X3) describing the plane detector/aperture. This origin is located within the detector/aperture area.

field.name: phi
field.documentation: Toroidal angle (oriented counter-clockwise when viewing from above)

field.name: radius
field.documentation: Radius of the circle, used only if geometry_type = 2

field.name: x1_unit_vector
field.documentation: Components of the X1 direction unit vector in the (X,Y,Z) coordinate system, where X is the major radius axis for phi = 0, Y is the major radius axis for phi = pi/2, and Z is the height axis. The X1 vector is more horizontal than X2 (has a smaller abs(Z) component) and oriented in the positive phi direction (counter-clockwise when viewing from above).

field.name: x2_unit_vector
field.documentation: Components of the X2 direction unit vector in the (X,Y,Z) coordinate system, where X is the major radius axis for phi = 0, Y is the major radius axis for phi = pi/2, and Z is the height axis. The X2 axis is orthonormal so that uX2 = uX3 x uX1.

field.name: x3_unit_vector
field.documentation: Components of the X3 direction unit vector in the (X,Y,Z) coordinate system, where X is the major radius axis for phi = 0, Y is the major radius axis for phi = pi/2, and Z is the height axis. The X3 axis is normal to the detector/aperture plane and oriented towards the plasma.

field.name: x1_width
field.documentation: Full width of the aperture in the X1 direction, used only if geometry_type = 3

field.name: x2_width
field.documentation: Full width of the aperture in the X2 direction, used only if geometry_type = 3

field.name: outline
field.documentation: Irregular outline of the detector/aperture in the (X1, X2) coordinate system. Repeat the first point since this is a closed contour

field.name: surface
field.documentation: Surface of the detector/aperture, derived from the above geometric data

field.name: detector_position_parameter
field.documentation: In case of detector moving during a pulse, position parameter allowing to record and compute the detector position as a function of time

field.name: aperture
field.documentation: Description of a set of collimating apertures

field.name: line_of_sight
field.documentation: Description of the line of sight of the channel, given by 2 points. The 2nd point is allowed to evolve in case of dynamic line of sight.

field.name: phi
field.documentation: Toroidal angle (oriented counter-clockwise when viewing from above)

field.name: second_point
field.documentation: Position of the second point (possibly dynamic)

field.name: moving_mode
field.documentation: Moving mode of the line of sight. Index = 0 : no movement, fixed position. Index = 1 : oscillating

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: position_parameter
field.documentation: In case of line of sight moving during a pulse, position parameter allowing to record and compute the line of sight position as a function of time

field.name: amplitude_parameter
field.documentation: Amplitude of the line of sight position parameter oscillation (in case moving_mode/index = 1)

field.name: period
field.documentation: Period of the line of sight oscillation (in case moving_mode/index = 1)

field.name: supply_high_voltage
field.documentation: Set of high voltage power supplies applied to various parts of the diagnostic

field.name: object
field.documentation: Name of the object connected to the power supply

field.name: voltage_set
field.documentation: Voltage set at the power supply

field.name: type
field.documentation: Grating type. Index = 1 : ruled. Index = 2 : holographic

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: groove_density
field.documentation: Number of grooves per unit length

field.name: geometry_type
field.documentation: Grating geometry. Index = 1 : spherical. Index = 2 : toric

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: centre
field.documentation: Centre of the grating sphere (if grating is spherical) or torus (if grating is toric)

field.name: phi
field.documentation: Toroidal angle (oriented counter-clockwise when viewing from above)

field.name: curvature_radius
field.documentation: Curvature radius of the spherical grating

field.name: summit
field.documentation: Position of the grating summit (defined as the point of contact of its concave side if the grating were put on a table). Used as the origin of the x1, x2, x3 vectors defined below

field.name: phi
field.documentation: Toroidal angle (oriented counter-clockwise when viewing from above)

field.name: x1_unit_vector
field.documentation: Components of the X1 direction unit vector in the (X,Y,Z) coordinate system, where X is the major radius axis for phi = 0, Y is the major radius axis for phi = pi/2, and Z is the height axis. The X1 vector is horizontal and oriented in the positive phi direction (counter-clockwise when viewing from above).

field.name: x2_unit_vector
field.documentation: Components of the X2 direction unit vector in the (X,Y,Z) coordinate system, where X is the major radius axis for phi = 0, Y is the major radius axis for phi = pi/2, and Z is the height axis. The X2 axis is orthonormal so that uX2 = uX3 x uX1.

field.name: x3_unit_vector
field.documentation: Components of the X3 direction unit vector in the (X,Y,Z) coordinate system, where X is the major radius axis for phi = 0, Y is the major radius axis for phi = pi/2, and Z is the height axis. The X3 axis is normal to the grating at its summit and oriented towards the plasma.

field.name: outline
field.documentation: List of the 4 extreme points of the spherical grating in the (X1, X2) coordinate system, using the summit as the origin. Repeat the first point since this is a closed contour

field.name: image_field
field.documentation: Surface on which the grating image is focused

field.name: geometry_type
field.documentation: Surface geometry. Index = 1 : spherical. Index = 2 : plane

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: centre
field.documentation: Centre of the image surface in case it is spherical, or position of a point on the surface in case it is a plane

field.name: phi
field.documentation: Toroidal angle (oriented counter-clockwise when viewing from above)

field.name: curvature_radius
field.documentation: Curvature radius of the image surface

field.name: x3_unit_vector
field.documentation: Components of the X3 direction unit vector in the (X,Y,Z) coordinate system, where X is the major radius axis for phi = 0, Y is the major radius axis for phi = pi/2, and Z is the height axis. The X3 axis is normal to the surface ( in case it is plane) and oriented towards the plasma.

field.name: radiance_spectral
field.documentation: Calibrated spectral radiance (radiance per unit wavelength)

field.name: intensity_spectrum
field.documentation: Intensity spectrum (not calibrated), i.e. number of photoelectrons detected by unit time by a wavelength pixel of the channel, taking into account electronic gain compensation and channels relative calibration

field.name: name
field.documentation: String identifying the processed line. To avoid ambiguities, the following syntax is used : element with ionization state_wavelength in Angstrom (e.g. WI_4000)

field.name: wavelength_central
field.documentation: Central wavelength of the processed line

field.name: radiance
field.documentation: Calibrated, background subtracted radiance (integrated over the spectrum for this line)

field.name: intensity
field.documentation: Non-calibrated intensity (integrated over the spectrum for this line)

field.name: wavelength_calibration
field.documentation: Wavelength calibration data. The wavelength is obtained from the pixel index k by: wavelength = k * gain + offset. k is starting from 1.

field.name: validity_timed
field.documentation: Indicator of the validity of the data for each wavelength and each time slice. 0: valid from automated processing, 1: valid and certified by the diagnostic RO; - 1 means problem identified in the data processing (request verification by the diagnostic RO), -2: invalid data, should not be used (values lower than -2 have a code-specific meaning detailing the origin of their invalidity)

field.name: validity
field.documentation: Indicator of the validity of the data for the whole acquisition period. 0: valid from automated processing, 1: valid and certified by the diagnostic RO; - 1 means problem identified in the data processing (request verification by the diagnostic RO), -2: invalid data, should not be used (values lower than -2 have a code-specific meaning detailing the origin of their invalidity)

field.name: latency
field.documentation: Upper bound of the delay between physical information received by the detector and data available on the real-time (RT) network.

field.documentation: Calibrated spectral radiance (radiance per unit wavelength)

field.documentation: Intensity spectrum (not calibrated), i.e. number of photoelectrons detected by unit time by a wavelength pixel of the channel, taking into account electronic gain compensation and channels relative calibration

field.name: name
field.documentation: String identifying the processed line. To avoid ambiguities, the following syntax is used : element with ionization state_wavelength in Angstrom (e.g. WI_4000)

field.name: wavelength_central
field.documentation: Central wavelength of the processed line

field.name: radiance
field.documentation: Calibrated, background subtracted radiance (integrated over the spectrum for this line)

field.name: intensity
field.documentation: Non-calibrated intensity (integrated over the spectrum for this line)

field.name: wavelength_calibration
field.documentation: Wavelength calibration data. The wavelength is obtained from the pixel index k by: wavelength = k * gain + offset. k is starting from 1.

field.name: instrument_function
field.documentation: Array of Gaussian widths and amplitudes which as a sum make up the instrument function. The instrument function is the shape that would be measured by a grating spectrometer if perfectly monochromatic line emission would be used as input. F(lambda) = 1 / sqrt (2*pi) * sum( instrument_function(1,i) / instrument_function(2,i) ) * exp( -lambda^2 / (2 * instrument_function(2,i)^2) ) ), whereby sum( instrument_function(1,i) ) = 1

field.name: filter_spectrometer
field.documentation: Quantities measured by the channel if connected to a filter spectrometer

field.name: processed_line
field.documentation: Set of processed spectral lines (normally a single line is filtered out, but it may happen in some cases that several lines go through the filter).

field.name: data
field.documentation: The Ray Transfer Matrix (RTM, or geometry matrix) here provides transformation of the signal from each individual unit light source (voxel) to the receiver (detector or head of an optic fibre). The emission profile has [photons.m^-3.s^-1.sr^-1] units and radiance signal has [photons.m^-2.s^-1.sr^-1] units. So the RTM has [m] units. This data is stored in a sparse form, i.e. the array contains only the non-zero element of the Ray transfer matrix. The voxel index corresponding to an element of this array can be found in voxel_indices

field.name: voxel_indices
field.documentation: List of voxel indices (defined in the voxel map) used in the sparse data array

The interpolated matrix is given on an array of interpolation knots of coordinates r, z and phi

field.documentation: Measurement channel, composed of a camera, a crystal, and (optional) a set of reflectors. The light coming from the plasma passes through the (optional) set of reflectors, then the crystal and arrives at the camera

field.name: energy_bound_lower
field.documentation: Lower energy bound for the photon detection, for each pixel (horizontal, vertical)

field.name: energy_bound_upper
field.documentation: Upper energy bound for the photon detection, for each pixel (horizontal, vertical)

field.name: geometry_type
field.documentation: Type of geometry used to describe the surface of the detector or aperture (1:'outline', 2:'circular', 3:'rectangle'). In case of 'outline', the surface is described by an outline of point in a local coordinate system defined by a centre and three unit vectors X1, X2, X3. Note that there is some flexibility here and the data provider should choose the most convenient coordinate system for the object, respecting the definitions of (X1,X2,X3) indicated below. In case of 'circular', the surface is a circle defined by its centre, radius, and normal vector oriented towards the plasma X3. In case of 'rectangle', the surface is a rectangle defined by its centre, widths in the X1 and X2 directions, and normal vector oriented towards the plasma X3.

field.name: centre
field.documentation: If geometry_type=2, coordinates of the centre of the circle. If geometry_type=1 or 3, coordinates of the origin of the local coordinate system (X1,X2,X3) describing the plane detector/aperture. This origin is located within the detector/aperture area.

field.name: phi
field.documentation: Toroidal angle (oriented counter-clockwise when viewing from above)

field.name: radius
field.documentation: Radius of the circle, used only if geometry_type = 2

field.name: x1_unit_vector
field.documentation: Components of the X1 direction unit vector in the (X,Y,Z) coordinate system, where X is the major radius axis for phi = 0, Y is the major radius axis for phi = pi/2, and Z is the height axis. The X1 vector is more horizontal than X2 (has a smaller abs(Z) component) and oriented in the positive phi direction (counter-clockwise when viewing from above).

field.name: x2_unit_vector
field.documentation: Components of the X2 direction unit vector in the (X,Y,Z) coordinate system, where X is the major radius axis for phi = 0, Y is the major radius axis for phi = pi/2, and Z is the height axis. The X2 axis is orthonormal so that uX2 = uX3 x uX1.

field.name: x3_unit_vector
field.documentation: Components of the X3 direction unit vector in the (X,Y,Z) coordinate system, where X is the major radius axis for phi = 0, Y is the major radius axis for phi = pi/2, and Z is the height axis. The X3 axis is normal to the detector/aperture plane and oriented towards the plasma.

field.name: x1_width
field.documentation: Full width of the aperture in the X1 direction, used only if geometry_type = 3

field.name: x2_width
field.documentation: Full width of the aperture in the X2 direction, used only if geometry_type = 3

field.name: outline
field.documentation: Irregular outline of the detector/aperture in the (X1, X2) coordinate system. Repeat the first point since this is a closed contour

field.name: surface
field.documentation: Surface of the detector/aperture, derived from the above geometric data

field.name: reflector
field.documentation: Set of reflectors (optional) reflecting the light coming from the plasma towards the crystal. If empty, means that the plasma light directly arrives on the crystal.

field.documentation: Short string identifier (unique for a given device)

field.name: description

field.name: z_frames
field.documentation: Height of the observed zone at the focal plane in the plasma, corresponding to the vertical dimension of the frame

field.name: wavelength_frames
field.documentation: Wavelength of incoming photons on each pixel of the frames, mainly varying accross the horizontal dimension of the frame. However a 2D map of the wavelength is given since it is not constant vertically due to the elliptical curvature of the photon iso-surfaces

field.name: bin
field.documentation: Set of bins (binning in the vertical dimension) defined to increase the signal to noise ratio of the spectra

field.name: z_pixel_range
field.documentation: Vertical pixel index range indicating the corresponding binned detector area

field.name: wavelength
field.documentation: Wavelength of incoming photons on each horizontal pixel of this bin.

field.name: line_of_sight
field.documentation: Description of the line of sight from the crystal to the plasma for this bin, defined by two points

field.documentation: Toroidal angle (oriented counter-clockwise when viewing from above)

field.documentation: Toroidal angle (oriented counter-clockwise when viewing from above)

field.name: instrument_function
field.documentation: Instrument function for this bin (replaces the ../../instrument function in case vertical binning is used), i.e. response of the detector to a monochromatic emission passing through the spectrometer. The resulting image on the detector will be a 2-D distribution of pixel values, for each wavelength. It can be given as explicit values for each detector pixel (values node) or as a parametric function of wavelength (described by the other nodes)

field.name: wavelengths
field.documentation: Array of wavelengths on which the instrument function is defined

field.name: values
field.documentation: Explicit instrument function values for the detector. When multiplied by the line-integrated emission spectrum in photons/second/sr/m/m^2 received on a binned pixel of the detector, gives the detector pixel output in counts/seconds.

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: intensity
field.documentation: Scaling factor for the instrument function such that convolving the instrument function with an emission spectrum gives the counts per second on the detector

field.name: centre
field.documentation: Centre (in terms of absolute wavelength) of instrument function

field.name: sigma
field.documentation: Standard deviation of Gaussian instrument function

field.name: scale
field.documentation: Scale of Lorentzian instrument function (full width at half height)

field.name: counts_n
field.documentation: Number of counts detected on each pixel of the frame during one exposure time

field.name: counts_bin_n
field.documentation: Number of counts detected on each pixel/bin of the binned frame during one exposure time

field.name: energies
field.documentation: Array of energy values for tabulation of the detection efficiency

field.name: detection_efficiency
field.documentation: Probability of detection of a photon impacting the detector as a function of its energy

field.name: profiles_line_integrated
field.documentation: Profiles proxies are given in the vertical direction of the detector. They are estimated directly from the camera, without tomographic inversion. Binning is allowed so the number of profile points may be lower than the length of z_frames. Physical quantities deduced from the measured spectra are given for each profile point. They correspond to the spectra integrated along lines of sight, defined by a first point given by the centre of the crystal and a second point (depending on the profile point) described below.

field.name: lines_of_sight_second_point
field.documentation: For each profile point, a line of sight is defined by a first point given by the centre of the crystal and a second point described here.

field.name: phi

field.name: lines_of_sight_rho_tor_norm
field.documentation: Shortest distance in rho_tor_norm between lines of sight and magnetic axis, signed with following convention : positive (resp. negative) means the point of shortest distance is above (resp. below) the magnetic axis

field.documentation: This node must be filled (with 0, 1, or 2) for the IDS to be valid. If 1, the time of this IDS is homogeneous, i.e. the time values for this IDS are stored in the time node just below the root of this IDS. If 0, the time values are stored in the various time fields at lower levels in the tree. In the case only constant or static nodes are filled within the IDS, homogeneous_time must be set to 2

field.name: path
field.documentation: Path of the node within the IDS, following the syntax given in the link below. If empty, means the provenance information applies to the whole IDS.

field.name: reference
field.documentation: List of references used to populate or calculate this node, identified as explained below. In case the node is the result of of a calculation / data processing, the reference is an input to the process described in the "code" structure at the root of the IDS. The reference can be an IDS (identified by a URI or a persitent identifier, see syntax in the link below) or non-IDS data imported directly from an non-IMAS database (identified by the command used to import the reference, or the persistent identifier of the data reference). Often data are obtained by a chain of processes, however only the last process input are recorded here. The full chain of provenance has then to be reconstructed recursively from the provenance information contained in the data references.

field.name: timestamp
field.documentation: Date and time (UTC) at which the reference was created, expressed in a human readable form (ISO 8601) : the format of the string shall be : YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ. Example : 2020-07-24T14:19:00Z

In case the node is the result of of a calculation / data processing, the reference is an input to the process described in the "code" structure at the root of the IDS. The reference can be an IDS (identified by a URI or a persitent identifier, see syntax in the link below) or non-IDS data imported directly from an non-IMAS database (identified by the command used to import the reference, or the persistent identifier of the data reference). Often data are obtained by a chain of processes, however only the last process input are recorded here. The full chain of provenance has then to be reconstructed recursively from the provenance information contained in the data references.

field.name: midplane
field.documentation: Choice of midplane definition for the mapping of measurements on an equilibrium. Indicate the IMAS URI of the used equilibrium IDS in the ids_properties/provenance section.

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: name
field.documentation: Short string identifier (unique for a given device)

field.name: description
field.documentation: Description, e.g. “channel viewing the upper divertor”

field.name: line_of_sight
field.documentation: Description of the line of sight of the channel, given by 2 points

field.name: phi
field.documentation: Toroidal angle (oriented counter-clockwise when viewing from above)

field.name: phi
field.documentation: Toroidal angle (oriented counter-clockwise when viewing from above)

field.name: polychromator_index
field.documentation: Index of the polychromator used by this channel (refers to the ../../polychromator array)

field.name: scattering_angle
field.documentation: Angle formed by the laser beam wave vector and the line of sight, counted clockwise when projected in the poloidal plane

field.name: width_z
field.documentation: Full width of the light collection area along the Z coordinate

field.name: solid_angle
field.documentation: Solid angle of the line of sight

field.name: position
field.documentation: Average position of the measurements (intersection between laser beam and line of sight)

field.name: phi
field.documentation: Toroidal angle (oriented counter-clockwise when viewing from above)

field.name: delta_position
field.documentation: Incremental variation of the position of the measurements, due to e.g. different lasers not intersecting the line of sight at the same position. The actual position is then the static position + delta_position

field.name: position_per_laser
field.documentation: Position of the intersection between each laser beam and this line of sight

field.name: phi
field.documentation: Toroidal angle (oriented counter-clockwise when viewing from above)

field.name: distance_separatrix_midplane
field.documentation: Distance between the measurement position and the separatrix, mapped along flux surfaces to the outboard midplane, in the major radius direction. Positive value means the measurement is outside of the separatrix.

field.name: validity_timed
field.documentation: Indicator of the validity of the data for each time slice. 0: valid from automated processing, 1: valid and certified by the diagnostic RO; - 1 means problem identified in the data processing (request verification by the diagnostic RO), -2: invalid data, should not be used (values lower than -2 have a code-specific meaning detailing the origin of their invalidity)

field.name: validity
field.documentation: Indicator of the validity of the data for the whole acquisition period. 0: valid from automated processing, 1: valid and certified by the diagnostic RO; - 1 means problem identified in the data processing (request verification by the diagnostic RO), -2: invalid data, should not be used (values lower than -2 have a code-specific meaning detailing the origin of their invalidity)

field.name: validity_timed
field.documentation: Indicator of the validity of the data for each time slice. 0: valid from automated processing, 1: valid and certified by the diagnostic RO; - 1 means problem identified in the data processing (request verification by the diagnostic RO), -2: invalid data, should not be used (values lower than -2 have a code-specific meaning detailing the origin of their invalidity)

field.name: validity
field.documentation: Indicator of the validity of the data for the whole acquisition period. 0: valid from automated processing, 1: valid and certified by the diagnostic RO; - 1 means problem identified in the data processing (request verification by the diagnostic RO), -2: invalid data, should not be used (values lower than -2 have a code-specific meaning detailing the origin of their invalidity)

field.name: gaussian_fit
field.documentation: Amplitude of the gaussian fit of the measured signal in each energy band, used to estimate the electron temperature

field.name: energy_in
field.documentation: Energy of the laser pulse measured just before entering the vacuum vessel

field.name: energy_out
field.documentation: Energy of the laser pulse measured after crossing the plasma

field.name: wavelength_band
field.documentation: Set of wavelength bands in which photons are counted by the polychromator

field.name: wavelength_lower
field.documentation: Lower bound of the detector wavelength range

field.name: wavelength_upper
field.documentation: Upper bound of the detector wavelength range

field.name: detection_efficiency
field.documentation: Probability of detection of a photon impacting the detector as a function of its wavelength

field.name: calibration_absolute
field.documentation: Factor to be multiplied by the spectral calibration to obtain the instrument function (fraction of signal received on each energy channel when a photon of relevant energy enters the optical system)

field.name: calibration_absolute_date
field.documentation: Date at which the absolute calibration was carried out

field.name: calibration_spectral
field.documentation: Polychromator response function: fraction of signal received on each energy channel when a photon of relevant energy enters the polychromator.

field.name: calibration_spectral_date
field.documentation: Date at which the spectral calibration was carried out

field.name: latency
field.documentation: Upper bound of the delay between physical information received by the detector and data available on the real-time (RT) network.

field.name: r0
field.documentation: Reference major radius of the device (from the official description of the device). This node is the placeholder for this official machine description quantity (typically the middle of the vessel at the equatorial midplane, although the exact definition may depend on the device)

field.name: is_periodic
field.documentation: Flag indicating whether coils are described one by one in the coil() structure (flag=0) or whether the coil structure represents only coils having different characteristics (flag = 1, n_coils must be filled in that case). In the latter case, the coil() sequence is repeated periodically around the torus.

field.name: coils_n
field.documentation: Number of coils around the torus, in case is_periodic = 1

field.name: coil
field.documentation: Set of coils around the tokamak

field.name: conductor
field.documentation: Set of conductors inside the coil. The structure can be used with size 1 for a simplified description as a single conductor. A conductor is composed of several elements, serially connected, i.e. transporting the same current.

field.name: elements
field.documentation: Set of geometrical elements (line segments and/or arcs of a circle) describing the contour of the conductor centre. We define a coordinate system associated to each element as follows: for the arc and circle elements: binormal = (start point - center) x (intermediate point - center). This vector points in the direction of the circle / arc axis. normal = (center - point on curve). The normal vector will rotate as the point moves around the curve. Tangent = normal x binormal. For the line element we require an extra point, using the currently redundant intermediate point to define the line element's normal axis. The local coordinates for the line element then become: tangent = end point - start point; normal = intermediate point - start point; binormal = tangent x normal. It is assumed that all the axes above are normalized such that they have a unit length.

field.name: types
field.documentation: Type of every element: 1: line segment, its ends are given by the start and end points; index = 2: arc of a circle; index = 3: full circle

field.name: start_points
field.documentation: Position of the start point of every element

field.name: phi
field.documentation: Toroidal angle (oriented counter-clockwise when viewing from above)

field.name: intermediate_points
field.documentation: Position of an intermediate point along the circle or arc of circle, for every element, providing the orientation of the element (must define with the corresponding start point an aperture angle strictly inferior to PI). In the case of a line segment (../types/index=1), fill this node with a point such that the vector intermediate_point - start_point defines the direction of the element's normal axis (see documentation of ../elements)

field.name: phi
field.documentation: Toroidal angle (oriented counter-clockwise when viewing from above)

field.name: end_points
field.documentation: Position of the end point of every element. Meaningful only if type/index = 1 or 2, fill with default/empty value otherwise

field.name: phi
field.documentation: Toroidal angle (oriented counter-clockwise when viewing from above)

field.name: centres
field.documentation: Position of the centre of the arc of a circle of every element (meaningful only if type/index = 2 or 3, fill with default/empty value otherwise)

field.name: phi
field.documentation: Toroidal angle (oriented counter-clockwise when viewing from above)

field.name: cross_section
field.documentation: The cross-section perpendicular to the conductor contour is described by a series of contour points, given by their relative position with respect to the start point of each element. If the size of this array of structure is equal to 1, then the cross-section is given only for the first element and translated along the conductor elements. Otherwise, it's given explictly for each element, allowing to describe changes of the cross section shape

field.name: geometry_type
field.documentation: Geometry type used to describe the cross section of this element. The conductor centre is given by the ../../elements description.

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: width
field.documentation: Full width of the rectangle or square in the normal direction, when geometry_type/index = 3 or 4. Diameter of the circle when geometry_type/index = 2. Outer diameter of the annulus in case geometry_type/index = 5

field.name: height
field.documentation: Full height of the rectangle in the binormal direction, used only if geometry_type/index = 3

field.name: radius_inner
field.documentation: Inner radius of the annulus, used only if geometry_type/index = 5

field.name: outline
field.documentation: Polygonal outline of the cross section in the (normal, binormal) coordinate system. Do NOT repeat the first point.

field.name: area
field.documentation: Area of the conductor cross-section, derived from the above geometric data

field.name: voltage
field.documentation: Voltage on the conductor terminals. Sign convention : positive when the current flows in the direction in which conductor elements are ordered (from start to end for a positive polarity coil)

field.name: turns
field.documentation: Number of total turns in the coil. May be a fraction when describing the coil connections.

field.name: current
field.documentation: Current in one turn of the coil (to be multiplied by the number of turns to calculate the magnetic field generated). Sign convention : a positive current flows in the direction in which conductor elements are ordered (from start to end for a positive polarity coil)

field.name: voltage
field.documentation: Voltage on the coil terminals. Sign convention : positive when the current flows in the direction in which conductor elements are ordered (from start to end for a positive polarity coil)

field.name: field_map
field.documentation: Map of the vacuum field at various time slices, represented using the generic grid description

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: path
field.documentation: Path of the grid, including the IDS name, in case of implicit reference to a grid_ggd node described in another IDS. To be filled only if the grid is not described explicitly in this grid_ggd structure. Example syntax: #wall:2/description_ggd(1)/grid_ggd, means that the grid is located in the wall IDS, occurrence 2, with relative path description_ggd(1)/grid_ggd, using Fortran index convention (here : first index of the array)

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: geometry_type
field.documentation: Type of space geometry (0: standard, 1:Fourier, >1: Fourier with periodicity)

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: coordinates_type
field.documentation: Type of coordinates describing the physical space, for every coordinate of the space. The size of this node therefore defines the dimension of the space.

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: objects_per_dimension
field.documentation: Definition of the space objects for every dimension (from one to the dimension of the highest-dimensional objects). The index correspond to 1=nodes, 2=edges, 3=faces, 4=cells/volumes, .... For every index, a collection of objects of that dimension is described.

field.name: object
field.documentation: Set of objects for a given dimension

field.name: boundary
field.documentation: Set of (n-1)-dimensional objects defining the boundary of this n-dimensional object

field.name: neighbours
field.documentation: List of indices of the n-dimensional objects adjacent to the given n-dimensional object. An object can possibly have multiple neighbours on a boundary

field.name: geometry
field.documentation: Geometry data associated with the object, its detailed content is defined by ../../geometry_content. Its dimension depends on the type of object, geometry and coordinate considered.

field.name: nodes
field.documentation: List of nodes forming this object (indices to objects_per_dimension(1)%object(:) in Fortran notation)

field.name: measure
field.documentation: Measure of the space object, i.e. physical size (length for 1d, area for 2d, volume for 3d objects,...)

field.name: geometry_2d
field.documentation: 2D geometry data associated with the object. Its dimension depends on the type of object, geometry and coordinate considered. Typically, the first dimension represents the object coordinates, while the second dimension would represent the values of the various degrees of freedom of the finite element attached to the object.

field.name: geometry_content
field.documentation: Content of the ../object/geometry node for this dimension

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: dimension
field.documentation: Space dimension of the grid subset elements, using the convention 1=nodes, 2=edges, 3=faces, 4=cells/volumes

field.name: element
field.documentation: Set of elements defining the grid subset. An element is defined by a combination of objects from potentially all spaces

field.name: object
field.documentation: Set of objects defining the element

field.name: space
field.documentation: Index of the space from which that object is taken

field.name: dimension
field.documentation: Dimension of the object - using the convention 1=nodes, 2=edges, 3=faces, 4=cells/volumes

field.name: base
field.documentation: Set of bases for the grid subset. For each base, the structure describes the projection of the base vectors on the canonical frame of the grid.

field.name: tensor_covariant
field.documentation: Covariant metric tensor, given on each element of the subgrid (first dimension)

field.name: tensor_contravariant
field.documentation: Contravariant metric tensor, given on each element of the subgrid (first dimension)

field.name: metric
field.documentation: Metric of the canonical frame onto Cartesian coordinates

field.name: tensor_covariant
field.documentation: Covariant metric tensor, given on each element of the subgrid (first dimension)

field.name: tensor_contravariant
field.documentation: Contravariant metric tensor, given on each element of the subgrid (first dimension)

field.name: b_field_r
field.documentation: R component of the vacuum magnetic field, given on various grid subsets

field.name: grid_index
field.documentation: Index of the grid used to represent this quantity

field.name: grid_subset_index
field.documentation: Index of the grid subset the data is provided on. Corresponds to the index used in the grid subset definition: grid_subset(:)/identifier/index

field.name: values
field.documentation: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.

field.name: coefficients
field.documentation: Interpolation coefficients, to be used for a high precision evaluation of the physical quantity with finite elements, provided per element in the grid subset (first dimension).

field.name: b_field_z
field.documentation: Z component of the vacuum magnetic field, given on various grid subsets

field.documentation: Index of the grid used to represent this quantity

field.name: delta_b_field_phi_vacuum_r

field.name: latency
field.documentation: Upper bound of the delay between input command received from the RT network and actuator starting to react. Applies globally to the system described by this IDS unless specific latencies (e.g. channel-specific or antenna-specific) are provided at a deeper level in the IDS structure.

field.name: homogeneous_time
field.documentation: This node must be filled (with 0, 1, or 2) for the IDS to be valid. If 1, the time of this IDS is homogeneous, i.e. the time values for this IDS are stored in the time node just below the root of this IDS. If 0, the time values are stored in the various time fields at lower levels in the tree. In the case only constant or static nodes are filled within the IDS, homogeneous_time must be set to 2

field.name: node
field.documentation: Set of IDS nodes for which the provenance is given. The provenance information applies to the whole structure below the IDS node. For documenting provenance information for the whole IDS, set the size of this array of structure to 1 and leave the child "path" node empty

field.name: path
field.documentation: Path of the node within the IDS, following the syntax given in the link below. If empty, means the provenance information applies to the whole IDS.

field.name: reference
field.documentation: List of references used to populate or calculate this node, identified as explained below. In case the node is the result of of a calculation / data processing, the reference is an input to the process described in the "code" structure at the root of the IDS. The reference can be an IDS (identified by a URI or a persitent identifier, see syntax in the link below) or non-IDS data imported directly from an non-IMAS database (identified by the command used to import the reference, or the persistent identifier of the data reference). Often data are obtained by a chain of processes, however only the last process input are recorded here. The full chain of provenance has then to be reconstructed recursively from the provenance information contained in the data references.

field.name: timestamp
field.documentation: Date and time (UTC) at which the reference was created, expressed in a human readable form (ISO 8601) : the format of the string shall be : YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ. Example : 2020-07-24T14:19:00Z

field.name: time_step
field.documentation: Internal time step used by the transport solver (assuming all transport equations are solved with the same time step)

field.name: time_step_average
field.documentation: Average internal time step used by the transport solver between the previous and the current time stored for this quantity (assuming all transport equations are solved with the same time step)

field.name: time_step_min
field.documentation: Minimum internal time step used by the transport solver between the previous and the current time stored for this quantity (assuming all transport equations are solved with the same time step)

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: primary_coordinate
field.documentation: Primary coordinate system with which the transport equations are solved. For a 1D transport solver: index = 1 means rho_tor_norm; 2 = rho_tor.

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: solver_1d
field.documentation: Numerics related to 1D radial solver, for various time slices.

field.name: rho_tor_norm
field.documentation: Normalized toroidal flux coordinate. The normalizing value for rho_tor_norm, is the toroidal flux coordinate at the equilibrium boundary (LCFS or 99.x % of the LCFS in case of a fixed boundary equilibium calculation, see time_slice/boundary/b_flux_pol_norm in the equilibrium IDS)

field.name: rho_tor
field.documentation: Toroidal flux coordinate = sqrt(phi/(pi*b0)), where the toroidal magnetic field, b0, corresponds to that stored in vacuum_toroidal_field/b0 and pi can be found in the IMAS constants

field.name: psi
field.documentation: Poloidal magnetic flux. Integral of magnetic field passing through a contour defined by the intersection of a flux surface passing through the point of interest and a Z=constant plane. If the integration surface is flat, the surface normal vector is in the increasing vertical coordinate direction, Z, namely upwards.

field.name: volume
field.documentation: Volume enclosed inside the magnetic surface

field.name: area
field.documentation: Cross-sectional area of the flux surface

field.name: surface
field.documentation: Surface area of the toroidal flux surface

field.name: psi_magnetic_axis
field.documentation: Value of the poloidal magnetic flux at the magnetic axis (useful to normalize the psi array values when the radial grid doesn't go from the magnetic axis to the plasma boundary)

field.name: psi_boundary
field.documentation: Value of the poloidal magnetic flux at the plasma boundary (useful to normalize the psi array values when the radial grid doesn't go from the magnetic axis to the plasma boundary)

field.name: primary_quantity
field.documentation: Profile and derivatives of the primary quantity of the transport equation

field.name: identifier
field.documentation: Identifier of the primary quantity of the transport equation. The description node contains the path to the quantity in the physics IDS (example: core_profiles/profiles_1d/ion(1)/density)

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: ion_index
field.documentation: If the primary quantity is related to a ion species, index of the corresponding species in the core_profiles/profiles_1d/ion array

field.name: neutral_index
field.documentation: If the primary quantity is related to a neutral species, index of the corresponding species in the core_profiles/profiles_1d/neutral array

field.name: state_index
field.documentation: If the primary quantity is related to a particular state (of an ion or a neutral species), index of the corresponding state in the core_profiles/profiles_1d/ion (or neutral)/state array

field.name: d_dr
field.documentation: Radial derivative with respect to the primary coordinate

field.name: d2_dr2
field.documentation: Second order radial derivative with respect to the primary coordinate

field.name: d_dt_cphi
field.documentation: Derivative with respect to time, at constant toroidal flux (for current diffusion equation)

field.name: d_dt_cr
field.documentation: Derivative with respect to time, at constant primary coordinate coordinate (for current diffusion equation)

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: boundary_condition
field.documentation: Set of boundary conditions of the transport equation

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: value
field.documentation: Value of the boundary condition. For type/index = 1 to 3, only the first position in the vector is used. For type/index = 5, all three positions are used, meaning respectively a1, a2, a3.

field.name: position
field.documentation: Position, in terms of the primary coordinate, at which the boundary condition is imposed. Outside this position, the value of the data are considered to be prescribed (in case of a single boundary condition).

field.name: coefficient
field.documentation: Set of numerical coefficients involved in the transport equation

field.name: profile
field.documentation: Radial profile of the numerical coefficient

field.name: iterations_n
field.documentation: Number of iterations carried out in the convergence loop

field.name: delta_relative

field.name: expression

field.documentation: Effective coefficient of physical sputtering for various neutral types (first dimension: 1: cold; 2: thermal; 3: fast), due to this incident species and for various energies (second dimension)

field.documentation: Effective coefficient of chemical sputtering for various neutral types (first dimension: 1: cold; 2: thermal; 3: fast), due to this incident species
