field.name: power_convected
field.documentation: Power convected by the plasma onto the wall

field.name: power_radiated
field.documentation: Net radiated power from plasma onto the wall (incident-reflected)

field.name: power_black_body
field.documentation: Black body radiated power emitted from the wall (emissivity is included)

field.name: power_neutrals
field.documentation: Net power from neutrals on the wall (positive means power is deposited on the wall)

field.name: power_recombination_plasma
field.documentation: Power deposited on the wall due to recombination of plasma ions

field.name: power_recombination_neutrals
field.documentation: Power deposited on the wall due to recombination of neutrals into a ground state (e.g. molecules)

field.name: power_currents
field.documentation: Power deposited on the wall due to electric currents (positive means power is deposited on the target)

field.name: power_inner_target_ion_total

field.name: power_density_inner_target_max

field.name: power_density_outer_target_max
field.documentation: Maximum power density on the outer target

field.name: current_phi

field.documentation: Set of 2D wall descriptions, for each type of possible physics or engineering configurations necessary (gas tight vs wall with ports and holes, coarse vs fine representation, single contour limiter, disjoint gapped plasma facing components, ...). A simplified description of the toroidal extension of the 2D contours is also provided by using the phi_extensions nodes.

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: limiter
field.documentation: Description of the immobile limiting surface(s) or plasma facing components for defining the Last Closed Flux Surface.

field.name: type
field.documentation: Type of the limiter description. index = 0 for the official single contour limiter and 1 for the official disjoint PFC structure like first wall. Additional representations needed on a code-by-code basis follow same incremental pair tagging starting on index =2

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: unit
field.documentation: Set of limiter units. Whenever relevant, multiple units should be ordered so that they define contiguous sections, clockwise in the poloidal direction.

field.name: name
field.documentation: Short string identifier (unique for a given device). Although the details may be machine-specific, a tree-like syntax must be followed, listing first top level components, then going down to finer element description. The tree levels are separated by a /, using a number of levels relevant to the granularity of the description. Example : ic_antenna/a1/bumpers refers to the bumpers of the a1 IC antenna

field.name: description
field.documentation: Description, e.g. “channel viewing the upper divertor”

field.name: component_type
field.documentation: Type of component of this unit

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: outline
field.documentation: Irregular outline of the limiting surface. Repeat the first point in case of a closed contour

field.name: phi_extensions
field.documentation: Simplified description of toroidal angle extensions of the unit, by a list of zones defined by their centre and full width (in toroidal angle). In each of these zones, the unit outline remains the same. Leave this node empty for an axisymmetric unit. The first dimension gives the centre and full width toroidal angle values for the unit. The second dimension represents the toroidal occurrences of the unit countour (i.e. the number of toroidal zones).

field.name: mobile
field.documentation: In case of mobile plasma facing components, use the time-dependent description below this node to provide the full outline of the closest PFC surfaces to the plasma. Even in such a case, the 'limiter' structure is still used to provide the outermost limiting surface (can be used e.g. to define the boundary of the mesh of equilibrium reconstruction codes)

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: outline
field.documentation: Irregular outline of the mobile unit, for a set of time slices. Repeat the first point in case of a closed contour

field.name: phi_extensions
field.documentation: Simplified description of toroidal angle extensions of the unit, by a list of zones defined by their centre and full width (in toroidal angle). In each of these zones, the unit outline remains the same. Leave this node empty for an axisymmetric unit. The first dimension gives the centre and full width toroidal angle values for the unit. The second dimension represents the toroidal occurrences of the unit countour (i.e. the number of toroidal zones).

field.name: vessel
field.documentation: Mechanical structure of the vacuum vessel. The vessel is described as a set of nested layers with given physics properties; Two representations are admitted for each vessel unit : annular (two contours) or block elements.

field.name: type
field.documentation: Type of the description. index = 0 for the official single/multiple annular representation and 1 for the official block element representation for each unit. Additional representations needed on a code-by-code basis follow same incremental pair tagging starting on index=2

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: name
field.documentation: Short string identifier (unique for a given device)

field.name: description
field.documentation: Description, e.g. “channel viewing the upper divertor”

field.name: annular
field.documentation: Annular representation of a layer by two contours, inner and outer. Alternatively, the layer can be described by a centreline and thickness.

field.name: outline_inner
field.documentation: Inner vessel outline. Repeat the first point in case of a closed contour

field.name: outline_outer
field.documentation: Outer vessel outline. Repeat the first point in case of a closed contour

field.name: centreline
field.documentation: Centreline, i.e. middle of the vessel layer as a series of point. Repeat the first point in case of a closed contour

field.name: thickness
field.documentation: Thickness of the vessel layer in the perpendicular direction to the centreline. Thickness(i) is the thickness of the layer between centreline/r(i),z(i) and centreline/r(i+1),z(i+1), so its size is equal to the length of centreline/r-1 if the thickness is varying. If the thickness is constant for all points, allocate this node to size 1 to store a single value.

field.name: outline
field.documentation: Outline of the block element. Repeat the first point in case of a closed contour

field.name: j_phi
field.documentation: Toroidal current induced in this block element

field.name: description_ggd
field.documentation: Set of 3D wall descriptions, described using the GGD, for each type of possible physics or engineering configurations necessary (gas tight vs wall with ports and holes, coarse vs fine representation, ...).

field.name: type
field.documentation: Type of wall: index = 0 for gas tight, 1 for a wall with holes/open ports, 2 for a thin wall description

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: grid_ggd
field.documentation: Wall geometry described using the Generic Grid Description, for various time slices (in case of mobile wall elements). The timebase of this array of structure must be a subset of the timebase on which physical quantities are described (../ggd structure). Grid_subsets are used to describe various wall components in a modular way.

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: path
field.documentation: Path of the grid, including the IDS name, in case of implicit reference to a grid_ggd node described in another IDS. To be filled only if the grid is not described explicitly in this grid_ggd structure. Example syntax: #wall:2/description_ggd(1)/grid_ggd, means that the grid is located in the wall IDS, occurrence 2, with relative path description_ggd(1)/grid_ggd, using Fortran index convention (here : first index of the array)

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: geometry_type
field.documentation: Type of space geometry (0: standard, 1:Fourier, >1: Fourier with periodicity)

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: coordinates_type
field.documentation: Type of coordinates describing the physical space, for every coordinate of the space. The size of this node therefore defines the dimension of the space.

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: objects_per_dimension
field.documentation: Definition of the space objects for every dimension (from one to the dimension of the highest-dimensional objects). The index correspond to 1=nodes, 2=edges, 3=faces, 4=cells/volumes, .... For every index, a collection of objects of that dimension is described.

field.name: object
field.documentation: Set of objects for a given dimension

field.name: boundary
field.documentation: Set of (n-1)-dimensional objects defining the boundary of this n-dimensional object

field.name: neighbours
field.documentation: List of indices of the n-dimensional objects adjacent to the given n-dimensional object. An object can possibly have multiple neighbours on a boundary

field.name: geometry
field.documentation: Geometry data associated with the object, its detailed content is defined by ../../geometry_content. Its dimension depends on the type of object, geometry and coordinate considered.

field.name: nodes
field.documentation: List of nodes forming this object (indices to objects_per_dimension(1)%object(:) in Fortran notation)

field.name: measure
field.documentation: Measure of the space object, i.e. physical size (length for 1d, area for 2d, volume for 3d objects,...)

field.name: geometry_2d
field.documentation: 2D geometry data associated with the object. Its dimension depends on the type of object, geometry and coordinate considered. Typically, the first dimension represents the object coordinates, while the second dimension would represent the values of the various degrees of freedom of the finite element attached to the object.

field.name: geometry_content
field.documentation: Content of the ../object/geometry node for this dimension

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: dimension
field.documentation: Space dimension of the grid subset elements, using the convention 1=nodes, 2=edges, 3=faces, 4=cells/volumes

field.name: element
field.documentation: Set of elements defining the grid subset. An element is defined by a combination of objects from potentially all spaces

field.name: object
field.documentation: Set of objects defining the element

field.name: space
field.documentation: Index of the space from which that object is taken

field.name: dimension
field.documentation: Dimension of the object - using the convention 1=nodes, 2=edges, 3=faces, 4=cells/volumes

field.name: base
field.documentation: Set of bases for the grid subset. For each base, the structure describes the projection of the base vectors on the canonical frame of the grid.

field.name: tensor_covariant
field.documentation: Covariant metric tensor, given on each element of the subgrid (first dimension)

field.name: tensor_contravariant
field.documentation: Contravariant metric tensor, given on each element of the subgrid (first dimension)

field.name: metric
field.documentation: Metric of the canonical frame onto Cartesian coordinates

field.name: tensor_covariant
field.documentation: Covariant metric tensor, given on each element of the subgrid (first dimension)

field.name: tensor_contravariant
field.documentation: Contravariant metric tensor, given on each element of the subgrid (first dimension)

field.name: material
field.documentation: Material of each grid_ggd object, given for each slice of the grid_ggd time base (the material is not supposed to change, but grid_ggd may evolve with time)

field.name: grid_subset
field.documentation: Material is described for various wall components (grid subsets), using the identifier convention below

field.name: grid_index
field.documentation: Index of the grid used to represent this quantity

field.name: grid_subset_index
field.documentation: Index of the grid subset the data is provided on. Corresponds to the index used in the grid subset definition: grid_subset(:)/identifier/index

field.name: identifiers
field.documentation: Identifier values, one value is provided per element in the grid subset. If the size of the child arrays is 1, their value applies to all elements of the subset.

field.name: indices
field.documentation: Integer identifiers (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: component
field.documentation: Description of the components represented by various subsets, given for each slice of the grid_ggd time base (the component description is not supposed to change, but grid_ggd may evolve with time)

field.name: identifiers
field.documentation: Identifiers of the components (described in the various grid_subsets). Although the details may be machine-specific, a tree-like syntax must be followed, listing first top level components, then going down to finer element description. The tree levels are separated by a /, using a number of levels relevant to the granularity of the description. Example : ic_antenna/a1/bumpers refers to the bumpers of the a1 IC antenna

field.name: type
field.documentation: The component type is given for various grid_subsets, using the identifier convention below

field.name: grid_index
field.documentation: Index of the grid used to represent this quantity

field.name: grid_subset_index
field.documentation: Index of the grid subset the data is provided on. Corresponds to the index used in the grid subset definition: grid_subset(:)/identifier/index

field.name: identifier
field.documentation: Identifier value for the grid subset

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: thickness
field.documentation: In the case of a thin wall description, effective thickness of each surface element of grid_ggd, given for each slice of the grid_ggd time base (the thickness is not supposed to change, but grid_ggd may evolve with time)

field.name: grid_subset
field.documentation: The thickness is given for various wall components (grid subsets)

field.name: grid_index
field.documentation: Index of the grid used to represent this quantity

field.name: grid_subset_index
field.documentation: Index of the grid subset the data is provided on. Corresponds to the index used in the grid subset definition: grid_subset(:)/identifier/index

field.name: values
field.documentation: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.

field.name: coefficients
field.documentation: Interpolation coefficients, to be used for a high precision evaluation of the physical quantity with finite elements, provided per element in the grid subset (first dimension).

field.name: brdf
field.documentation: Bidirectional Reflectance Distribution Function, given for each slice of the grid_ggd time base (the component description is not supposed to change, but grid_ggd may evolve with time)

field.name: node

field.name: path
field.documentation: Path of the node within the IDS, following the syntax given in the link below. If empty, means the provenance information applies to the whole IDS.

field.name: reference
field.documentation: List of references used to populate or calculate this node, identified as explained below. In case the node is the result of of a calculation / data processing, the reference is an input to the process described in the "code" structure at the root of the IDS. The reference can be an IDS (identified by a URI or a persitent identifier, see syntax in the link below) or non-IDS data imported directly from an non-IMAS database (identified by the command used to import the reference, or the persistent identifier of the data reference). Often data are obtained by a chain of processes, however only the last process input are recorded here. The full chain of provenance has then to be reconstructed recursively from the provenance information contained in the data references.

field.name: timestamp
field.documentation: Date and time (UTC) at which the reference was created, expressed in a human readable form (ISO 8601) : the format of the string shall be : YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ. Example : 2020-07-24T14:19:00Z

field.name: identifier
field.documentation: Identifier of the coherent wave, in terms of the type and name of the antenna driving the wave and an index separating waves driven by the same antenna.

field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: antenna_name
field.documentation: Name of the antenna that launches this wave. Corresponds to the name specified in antennas/ec(i)/name, or antennas/ic(i)/name or antennas/lh(i)/name (depends of antenna/wave type) in the ANTENNAS IDS.

field.name: index_in_antenna
field.documentation: Index of the wave (starts at 1), separating different waves generated from a single antenna.

field.name: wave_solver_type
field.documentation: Type of wave deposition solver used for this wave. Index = 1 for beam/ray tracing; index = 2 for full wave

field.name: power_n_phi

field.documentation: Normalized toroidal flux coordinate. The normalizing value for rho_tor_norm, is the toroidal flux coordinate at the equilibrium boundary (LCFS or 99.x % of the LCFS in case of a fixed boundary equilibium calculation, see time_slice/boundary/b_flux_pol_norm in the equilibrium IDS)

field.name: rho_tor
field.documentation: Toroidal flux coordinate = sqrt(phi/(pi*b0)), where the toroidal magnetic field, b0, corresponds to that stored in vacuum_toroidal_field/b0 and pi can be found in the IMAS constants

field.name: psi
field.documentation: Poloidal magnetic flux. Integral of magnetic field passing through a contour defined by the intersection of a flux surface passing through the point of interest and a Z=constant plane. If the integration surface is flat, the surface normal vector is in the increasing vertical coordinate direction, Z, namely upwards.

field.name: psi_boundary

To be filled only if the grid is not described explicitly in this grid_ggd structure. Example syntax: #wall:2/description_ggd(1)/grid_ggd, means that the grid is located in the wall IDS, occurrence 2, with relative path description_ggd(1)/grid_ggd, using Fortran index convention (here : first index of the array)

field.name: index

field.documentation: Definition of the space objects for every dimension (from one to the dimension of the highest-dimensional objects). The index correspond to 1=nodes, 2=edges, 3=faces, 4=cells/volumes, .... For every index, a collection of objects of that dimension is described.

field.name: boundary

field.name: neighbours

field.name: geometry
field.documentation: Geometry data associated with the object, its detailed content is defined by ../../geometry_content. Its dimension depends on the type of object, geometry and coordinate considered.

field.name: nodes

field.name: measure

field.name: geometry_2d
field.documentation: 2D geometry data associated with the object. Its dimension depends on the type of object, geometry and coordinate considered. Typically, the first dimension represents the object coordinates, while the second dimension would represent the values of the various degrees of freedom of the finite element attached to the object.

field.name: homogeneous_time
field.documentation: This node must be filled (with 0, 1, or 2) for the IDS to be valid. If 1, the time of this IDS is homogeneous, i.e. the time values for this IDS are stored in the time node just below the root of this IDS. If 0, the time values are stored in the various time fields at lower levels in the tree. In the case only constant or static nodes are filled within the IDS, homogeneous_time must be set to 2

field.name: node
field.documentation: Set of IDS nodes for which the provenance is given. The provenance information applies to the whole structure below the IDS node. For documenting provenance information for the whole IDS, set the size of this array of structure to 1 and leave the child "path" node empty

field.name: path
field.documentation: Path of the node within the IDS, following the syntax given in the link below. If empty, means the provenance information applies to the whole IDS.

field.name: reference
field.documentation: List of references used to populate or calculate this node, identified as explained below. In case the node is the result of of a calculation / data processing, the reference is an input to the process described in the "code" structure at the root of the IDS. The reference can be an IDS (identified by a URI or a persitent identifier, see syntax in the link below) or non-IDS data imported directly from an non-IMAS database (identified by the command used to import the reference, or the persistent identifier of the data reference). Often data are obtained by a chain of processes, however only the last process input are recorded here. The full chain of provenance has then to be reconstructed recursively from the provenance information contained in the data references.

field.name: timestamp
field.documentation: Date and time (UTC) at which the reference was created, expressed in a human readable form (ISO 8601) : the format of the string shall be : YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ. Example : 2020-07-24T14:19:00Z

field.name: workflow_cycle
field.documentation: Set of time slices corresponding to the beginning of workflow cycles (main time loop of the workflow). During each workflow cycle, active components compute their result during their given time_interval. Components having completed their computation are frozen until the end of the workflow cycle. The next workflow cycle begins when the maximum time_interval (over the components) has been reached.

field.name: execution_mode
field.documentation: Component execution mode for current workflow cycle. 0 means the component is not executed and the workflow uses results from previous workflow cycle. 1 means the component is executed for this workflow cycle.

field.name: time_interval_request

field.name: time_interval_elapsed
